The value of an audience doesn't grow anything like linearly with its size. Which is bad news if you're famous, but good news if you're just starting out, because it means a small but dedicated audience can be enough to sustain you. If a handful of people genuinely love what you're doing, that's enough.

To the extent you can, avoid letting intermediaries come between you and your audience. In some types of work this is inevitable, but it's so liberating to escape it that you might be better off switching to an adjacent type if that will let you go direct.

[28]

The people you spend time with will also have a big effect on your morale. You'll find there are some who increase your energy and others who decrease it, and the effect someone has is not always what you'd expect. Seek out the people who increase your energy and avoid those who decrease it. Though of course if there's someone you need to take care of, that takes precedence.

Don't marry someone who doesn't understand that you need to work, or sees your work as competition for your attention. If you're ambitious, you need to work; it's almost like a medical condition; so someone who won't let you work either doesn't understand you, or does and doesn't care.

Ultimately morale is physical. You think with your body, so it's important to take care of it. That means exercising regularly, eating and sleeping well, and avoiding the more dangerous kinds of drugs. Running and walking are particularly good forms of exercise because they're good for thinking.

[29]

People who do great work are not necessarily happier than everyone else, but they're happier than they'd be if they didn't. In fact, if you're smart and ambitious, it's dangerous not to be productive. People who are smart and ambitious but don't achieve much tend to become bitter.

It's ok to want to impress other people, but choose the right people. The opinion of people you respect is signal. Fame, which is the opinion of a much larger group you might or might not respect, just adds noise.

The prestige of a type of work is at best a trailing indicator and sometimes completely mistaken. If you do anything well enough, you'll make it prestigious. So the question to ask about a type of work is not how much prestige it has, but how well it could be done.

Competition can be an effective motivator, but don't let it choose the problem for you; don't let yourself get drawn into chasing something just because others are. In fact, don't let competitors make you do anything much more specific than work harder.

Curiosity is the best guide. Your curiosity never lies, and it knows more than you do about what's worth paying attention to.

Notice how often that word has come up. If you asked an oracle the secret to doing great work and the oracle replied with a single word, my bet would be on "curiosity."

That doesn't translate directly to advice. It's not enough just to be curious, and you can't command curiosity anyway. But you can nurture it and let it drive you.

Curiosity is the key to all four steps in doing great work: it will choose the field for you, get you to the frontier, cause you to notice the gaps in it, and drive you to explore them. The whole process is a kind of dance with curiosity.

Believe it or not, I tried to make this essay as short as I could. But its length at least means it acts as a filter. If you made it this far, you must be interested in doing great work. And if so you're already further along than you might realize, because the set of people willing to want to is small.

The factors in doing great work are factors in the literal, mathematical sense, and they are: ability, interest, effort, and luck. Luck by definition you can't do anything about, so we can ignore that. And we can assume effort, if you do in fact want to do great work. So the problem boils down to ability and interest. Can you find a kind of work where your ability and interest will combine to yield an explosion of new ideas?

Here there are grounds for optimism. There are so many different ways to do great work, and even more that are still undiscovered. Out of all those different types of work, the one you're most suited for is probably a pretty close match. Probably a comically close match. It's just a question of finding it, and how far into it your ability and interest can take you. And you can only answer that by trying.

Many more people could try to do great work than do. What holds them back is a combination of modesty and fear. It seems presumptuous to try to be Newton or Shakespeare. It also seems hard; surely if you tried something like that, you'd fail. Presumably the calculation is rarely explicit. Few people consciously decide not to try to do great work. But that's what's going on subconsciously; they shy away from the question.

So I'm going to pull a sneaky trick on you. Do you want to do great work, or not? Now you have to decide consciously. Sorry about that. I wouldn't have done it to a general audience. But we already know you're interested.

Don't worry about being presumptuous. You don't have to tell anyone. And if it's too hard and you fail, so what? Lots of people have worse problems than that. In fact you'll be lucky if it's the worst problem you have.

Yes, you'll have to work hard. But again, lots of people have to work hard. And if you're working on something you find very interesting, which you necessarily will if you're on the right path, the work will probably feel less burdensome than a lot of your peers'.

The discoveries are out there, waiting to be made. Why not by you?

Notes

[

1] I don't think you could give a precise definition of what counts as great work. Doing great work means doing something important so well that you expand people's ideas of what's possible. But there's no threshold for importance. It's a matter of degree, and often hard to judge at the time anyway. So I'd rather people focused on developing their interests rather than worrying about whether they're important or not. Just try to do something amazing, and leave it to future generations to say if you succeeded.

[

2] A lot of standup comedy is based on noticing anomalies in everyday life. "Did you ever notice...?" New ideas come from doing this about nontrivial things. Which may help explain why people's reaction to a new idea is often the first half of laughing: Ha!

[

3] That second qualifier is critical. If you're excited about something most authorities discount, but you can't give a more precise explanation than "they don't get it," then you're starting to drift into the territory of cranks.

[

4] Finding something to work on is not simply a matter of finding a match between the current version of you and a list of known problems. You'll often have to coevolve with the problem. That's why it can sometimes be so hard to figure out what to work on. The search space is huge. It's the cartesian product of all possible types of work, both known and yet to be discovered, and all possible future versions of you.

There's no way you could search this whole space, so you have to rely on heuristics to generate promising paths through it and hope the best matches will be clustered. Which they will not always be; different types of work have been collected together as much by accidents of history as by the intrinsic similarities between them.

[

5] There are many reasons curious people are more likely to do great work, but one of the more subtle is that, by casting a wide net, they're more likely to find the right thing to work on in the first place.

[

6] It can also be dangerous to make things for an audience you feel is less sophisticated than you, if that causes you to talk down to them. You can make a lot of money doing that, if you do it in a sufficiently cynical way, but it's not the route to great work. Not that anyone using this m.o. would care.

[

7] This idea I learned from Hardy's A Mathematician's Apology, which I recommend to anyone ambitious to do great work, in any field.

[

8] Just as we overestimate what we can do in a day and underestimate what we can do over several years, we overestimate the damage done by procrastinating for a day and underestimate the damage done by procrastinating for several years.

[

9] You can't usually get paid for doing exactly what you want, especially early on. There are two options: get paid for doing work close to what you want and hope to push it closer, or get paid for doing something else entirely and do your own projects on the side. Both can work, but both have drawbacks: in the first approach your work is compromised by default, and in the second you have to fight to get time to do it.

[

10] If you set your life up right, it will deliver the focus-relax cycle automatically. The perfect setup is an office you work in and that you walk to and from.

[

11] There may be some very unworldly people who do great work without consciously trying to. If you want to expand this rule to cover that case, it becomes: Don't try to be anything except the best.

[

12] This gets more complicated in work like acting, where the goal is to adopt a fake persona. But even here it's possible to be affected. Perhaps the rule in such fields should be to avoid unintentional affectation.

[

13] It's safe to have beliefs that you treat as unquestionable if and only if they're also unfalsifiable. For example, it's safe to have the principle that everyone should be treated equally under the law, because a sentence with a "should" in it isn't really a statement about the world and is therefore hard to disprove. And if there's no evidence that could disprove one of your principles, there can't be any facts you'd need to ignore in order to preserve it.

[

14] Affectation is easier to cure than intellectual dishonesty. Affectation is often a shortcoming of the young that burns off in time, while intellectual dishonesty is more of a character flaw.

[

15] Obviously you don't have to be working at the exact moment you have the idea, but you'll probably have been working fairly recently.

[

16] Some say psychoactive drugs have a similar effect. I'm skeptical, but also almost totally ignorant of their effects.

[

17] For example you might give the nth most important topic (m-1)/m^n of your attention, for some m > 1. You couldn't allocate your attention so precisely, of course, but this at least gives an idea of a reasonable distribution.

[

18] The principles defining a religion have to be mistaken. Otherwise anyone might adopt them, and there would be nothing to distinguish the adherents of the religion from everyone else.

[

19] It might be a good exercise to try writing down a list of questions you wondered about in your youth. You might find you're now in a position to do something about some of them.

[

20] The connection between originality and uncertainty causes a strange phenomenon: because the conventional-minded are more certain than the independent-minded, this tends to give them the upper hand in disputes, even though they're generally stupider.
The best lack all conviction, while the worst
Are full of passionate intensity.
[21] Derived from Linus Pauling's "If you want to have good ideas, you must have many ideas."

[

22] Attacking a project as a "toy" is similar to attacking a statement as "inappropriate." It means that no more substantial criticism can be made to stick.

[

23] One way to tell whether you're wasting time is to ask if you're producing or consuming. Writing computer games is less likely to be a waste of time than playing them, and playing games where you create something is less likely to be a waste of time than playing games where you don't.

[

24] Another related advantage is that if you haven't said anything publicly yet, you won't be biased toward evidence that supports your earlier conclusions. With sufficient integrity you could achieve eternal youth in this respect, but few manage to. For most people, having previously published opinions has an effect similar to ideology, just in quantity 1.

[

25] In the early 1630s Daniel Mytens made a painting of Henrietta Maria handing a laurel wreath to Charles I. Van Dyck then painted his own version to show how much better he was.

[

26] I'm being deliberately vague about what a place is. As of this writing, being in the same physical place has advantages that are hard to duplicate, but that could change.

[

27] This is false when the work the other people have to do is very constrained, as with SETI@home or Bitcoin. It may be possible to expand the area in which it's false by defining similarly restricted protocols with more freedom of action in the nodes.

[

28] Corollary: Building something that enables people to go around intermediaries and engage directly with their audience is probably a good idea.

[

29] It may be helpful always to walk or run the same route, because that frees attention for thinking. It feels that way to me, and there is some historical evidence for it.Thanks to Trevor Blackwell, Daniel Gackle, Pam Graham, Tom Howard, Patrick Hsu, Steve Huffman, Jessica Livingston, Henry Lloyd-Baker, Bob Metcalfe, Ben Miller, Robert Morris, Michael Nielsen, Courtenay Pipkin, Joris Poort, Mieke Roos, Rajat Suri, Harj Taggar, Garry Tan, and my younger son for suggestions and for reading drafts.

sentences.en: July 2023If you collected lists of techniques for doing great work in a lot of different fields, what would the intersection look like?
sentences.zh: 七月 2023如果您收集了在许多不同领域做出出色工作的技术列表，那么交集会是什么样子？

sentences.en: I decided to find out by making it.Partly my goal was to create a guide that could be used by someone working in any field.
sentences.zh: 我决定通过制作来找出答案。我的部分目标是创建一个可供任何领域工作的人使用的指南。

sentences.en: But I was also curious about the shape of the intersection.
sentences.zh: 但我也对十字路口的形状感到好奇。

sentences.en: And one thing this exercise shows is that it does have a definite shape; it's not just a point labelled "work hard."The following recipe assumes you're very ambitious.
sentences.zh: 这个练习表明的一件事是它确实有一个明确的形状；这不仅仅是一个标有“努力工作”的点。以下秘诀假设您非常雄心勃勃。

sentences.en: The first step is to decide what to work on.
sentences.zh: 第一步是决定要做什么。

sentences.en: The work you choose needs to have three qualities: it has to be something you have a natural aptitude for, that you have a deep interest in, and that offers scope to do great work.In practice you don't have to worry much about the third criterion.
sentences.zh: 你选择的工作需要具备三个品质：它必须是你有天赋的东西，你对此有浓厚的兴趣，并且它提供了完成伟大工作的空间。在实践中，你不必太担心第三个标准。

sentences.en: Ambitious people are if anything already too conservative about it.
sentences.zh: 雄心勃勃的人对此已经过于保守了。

sentences.en: So all you need to do is find something you have an aptitude for and great interest in. [1]That sounds straightforward, but it's often quite difficult.
sentences.zh: 因此，您需要做的就是找到您有天赋并且非常感兴趣的东西。[1]这听起来很简单，但通常非常困难。

sentences.en: When you're young you don't know what you're good at or what different kinds of work are like.
sentences.zh: 当你年轻的时候，你不知道自己擅长什么，也不知道不同种类的工作是什么样的。

sentences.en: Some kinds of work you end up doing may not even exist yet.
sentences.zh: 你最终要做的某些工作可能还不存在。

sentences.en: So while some people know what they want to do at 14, most have to figure it out.The way to figure out what to work on is by working.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然有些人知道自己 14 岁时想做什么，但大多数人都必须弄清楚。弄清楚要做什么的方法就是通过工作。

sentences.en: If you're not sure what to work on, guess.
sentences.zh: 如果您不确定要做什么，请猜测。

sentences.en: But pick something and get going.
sentences.zh: 但选择一些东西然后开始吧。

sentences.en: You'll probably guess wrong some of the time, but that's fine.
sentences.zh: 有时你可能会猜错，但这没关系。

sentences.en: It's good to know about multiple things; some of the biggest discoveries come from noticing connections between different fields.Develop a habit of working on your own projects.
sentences.zh: 了解多种事物是件好事；一些最大的发现来自于注意到不同领域之间的联系。养成从事自己的项目的习惯。

sentences.en: Don't let "work" mean something other people tell you to do.
sentences.zh: 不要让“工作”意味着别人告诉你做的事情。

sentences.en: If you do manage to do great work one day, it will probably be on a project of your own.
sentences.zh: 如果有一天你确实能做出出色的工作，那很可能是在你自己的一个项目上。

sentences.en: It may be within some bigger project, but you'll be driving your part of it.What should your projects be?
sentences.zh: 它可能在一些更大的项目中，但你将推动你的部分。你的项目应该是什么？

sentences.en: Whatever seems to you excitingly ambitious.
sentences.zh: 任何在你看来令人兴奋的雄心勃勃的事情。

sentences.en: As you grow older and your taste in projects evolves, exciting and important will converge.
sentences.zh: 随着年龄的增长和对项目的品味的变化，令人兴奋和重要的事情将会融合在一起。

sentences.en: At 7 it may seem excitingly ambitious to build huge things out of Lego, then at 14 to teach yourself calculus, till at 21 you're starting to explore unanswered questions in physics.
sentences.zh: 7 岁的时候，用乐高搭建巨大的东西似乎是令人兴奋的雄心勃勃，然后 14 岁的时候自学微积分，直到 21 岁开始探索物理学中尚未解答的问题。

sentences.en: But always preserve excitingness.There's a kind of excited curiosity that's both the engine and the rudder of great work.
sentences.zh: 但始终保持兴奋感。有一种兴奋的好奇心，它既是伟大工作的引擎，也是伟大工作的舵。

sentences.en: It will not only drive you, but if you let it have its way, will also show you what to work on.What are you excessively curious about — curious to a degree that would bore most other people?
sentences.zh: 它不仅会驱动你，而且如果你顺其自然，它也会告诉你该做什么。你对什么过度好奇——好奇到让大多数人感到厌烦的程度？

sentences.en: That's what you're looking for.Once you've found something you're excessively interested in, the next step is to learn enough about it to get you to one of the frontiers of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 这就是你正在寻找的东西。一旦你发现了你非常感兴趣的东西，下一步就是充分了解它，让你到达知识的前沿之一。

sentences.en: Knowledge expands fractally, and from a distance its edges look smooth, but once you learn enough to get close to one, they turn out to be full of gaps.The next step is to notice them.
sentences.zh: 知识以分形方式扩展，从远处看，它的边缘看起来很光滑，但一旦你学到了足够多的东西来接近它，它们就会变得充满了间隙。下一步就是注意它们。

sentences.en: This takes some skill, because your brain wants to ignore such gaps in order to make a simpler model of the world.
sentences.zh: 这需要一些技巧，因为你的大脑想要忽略这些差距，以便建立一个更简单的世界模型。

sentences.en: Many discoveries have come from asking questions about things that everyone else took for granted. [2]If the answers seem strange, so much the better.
sentences.zh: 许多发现都来自于对其他人认为理所当然的事情提出问题。 [2]如果答案看起来很奇怪，那就更好了。

sentences.en: Great work often has a tincture of strangeness.
sentences.zh: 伟大的作品常常带有一丝陌生的味道。

sentences.en: You see this from painting to math.
sentences.zh: 从绘画到数学你都能看到这一点。

sentences.en: It would be affected to try to manufacture it, but if it appears, embrace it.Boldly chase outlier ideas, even if other people aren't interested in them — in fact, especially if they aren't.
sentences.zh: 尝试制造它会受到影响，但如果它出现，就拥抱它。大胆地追逐离群想法，即使其他人对它们不感兴趣——事实上，尤其是如果他们不感兴趣的话。

sentences.en: If you're excited about some possibility that everyone else ignores, and you have enough expertise to say precisely what they're all overlooking, that's as good a bet as you'll find. [3]Four steps: choose a field, learn enough to get to the frontier, notice gaps, explore promising ones.
sentences.zh: 如果你对其他人都忽略的某种可能性感到兴奋，并且你有足够的专业知识来准确地说出他们都忽略的事情，那么这就是你会发现的最好的选择。 [3]四步：选择一个领域，充分学习以达到前沿，注意到差距，探索有前途的领域。

sentences.en: This is how practically everyone who's done great work has done it, from painters to physicists.Steps two and four will require hard work.
sentences.zh: 实际上，从画家到物理学家，每个做出伟大工作的人都是这样做的。第二步和第四步需要艰苦的工作。

sentences.en: It may not be possible to prove that you have to work hard to do great things, but the empirical evidence is on the scale of the evidence for mortality.
sentences.zh: 也许无法证明你必须努力工作才能做伟大的事情，但经验证据的规模与死亡率的证据相当。

sentences.en: That's why it's essential to work on something you're deeply interested in.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么从事您感兴趣的事情至关重要。

sentences.en: Interest will drive you to work harder than mere diligence ever could.The three most powerful motives are curiosity, delight, and the desire to do something impressive.
sentences.zh: 兴趣会驱使你比单纯的勤奋更加努力地工作。三个最强大的动机是好奇心、快乐和做一些令人印象深刻的事情的愿望。

sentences.en: Sometimes they converge, and that combination is the most powerful of all.The big prize is to discover a new fractal bud.
sentences.zh: 有时它们会聚合，而这种组合是最强大的。最大的奖品是发现一个新的分形芽。

sentences.en: You notice a crack in the surface of knowledge, pry it open, and there's a whole world inside.Let's talk a little more about the complicated business of figuring out what to work on.
sentences.zh: 你注意到知识表面有一条裂缝，把它撬开，里面有一个完整的世界。让我们多谈谈弄清楚要做什么的复杂事情。

sentences.en: The main reason it's hard is that you can't tell what most kinds of work are like except by doing them.
sentences.zh: 其困难的主要原因是，除非亲自去做，否则你无法辨别大多数类型的工作是什么样的。

sentences.en: Which means the four steps overlap: you may have to work at something for years before you know how much you like it or how good you are at it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这四个步骤是重叠的：你可能需要在某件事上工作多年才能知道你有多喜欢它或者你有多擅长它。

sentences.en: And in the meantime you're not doing, and thus not learning about, most other kinds of work.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，你并没有做，因此也没有学习大多数其他类型的工作。

sentences.en: So in the worst case you choose late based on very incomplete information. [4]The nature of ambition exacerbates this problem.
sentences.zh: 因此，在最坏的情况下，您会根据非常不完整的信息选择延迟。 [4]野心的本质加剧了这个问题。

sentences.en: Ambition comes in two forms, one that precedes interest in the subject and one that grows out of it.
sentences.zh: 野心有两种形式，一种是先于对某个学科的兴趣，另一种则源于对该学科的兴趣。

sentences.en: Most people who do great work have a mix, and the more you have of the former, the harder it will be to decide what to do.The educational systems in most countries pretend it's easy.
sentences.zh: 大多数做出出色工作的人都是混合的，而且前者越多，就越难决定做什么。大多数国家的教育体系假装这很容易。

sentences.en: They expect you to commit to a field long before you could know what it's really like.
sentences.zh: 他们希望你早在知道某个领域到底是什么样子之前就投入其中。

sentences.en: And as a result an ambitious person on an optimal trajectory will often read to the system as an instance of breakage.It would be better if they at least admitted it — if they admitted that the system not only can't do much to help you figure out what to work on, but is designed on the assumption that you'll somehow magically guess as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 因此，一个雄心勃勃、处于最佳轨道上的人经常会将系统视为破坏的一个例子。如果他们至少承认这一点，那就更好了——如果他们承认系统不仅不能帮助你弄清楚要做什么，而且是基于你在青少年时期会以某种方式神奇地猜测的假设而设计的。

sentences.en: They don't tell you, but I will: when it comes to figuring out what to work on, you're on your own.
sentences.zh: 他们不会告诉你，但我会告诉你：当谈到弄清楚要做什么时，你得靠自己。

sentences.en: Some people get lucky and do guess correctly, but the rest will find themselves scrambling diagonally across tracks laid down on the assumption that everyone does.What should you do if you're young and ambitious but don't know what to work on?
sentences.zh: 有些人很幸运，猜对了，但其他人会发现自己在假设每个人都猜对的轨道上爬行。如果你年轻、雄心勃勃，但不知道该做什么，你该怎么办？

sentences.en: What you should not do is drift along passively, assuming the problem will solve itself.
sentences.zh: 你不应该做的是被动地随波逐流，假设问题会自行解决。

sentences.en: You need to take action.
sentences.zh: 你需要采取行动。

sentences.en: But there is no systematic procedure you can follow.
sentences.zh: 但没有可以遵循的系统程序。

sentences.en: When you read biographies of people who've done great work, it's remarkable how much luck is involved.
sentences.zh: 当你阅读那些做出了伟大工作的人的传记时，你会发现其中涉及到多少运气。

sentences.en: They discover what to work on as a result of a chance meeting, or by reading a book they happen to pick up.
sentences.zh: 他们通过一次偶然的机会，或者通过读一本他们偶然拿起的书来发现要做什么。

sentences.en: So you need to make yourself a big target for luck, and the way to do that is to be curious.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要让自己成为一个幸运的大目标，而做到这一点的方法就是保持好奇心。

sentences.en: Try lots of things, meet lots of people, read lots of books, ask lots of questions. [5]When in doubt, optimize for interestingness.
sentences.zh: 尝试很多事情，认识很多人，读很多书，问很多问题。 [5]当有疑问时，优化趣味性。

sentences.en: Fields change as you learn more about them.
sentences.zh: 当您了解更多领域时，领域就会发生变化。

sentences.en: What mathematicians do, for example, is very different from what you do in high school math classes.
sentences.zh: 例如，数学家所做的事情与你在高中数学课上所做的事情非常不同。

sentences.en: So you need to give different types of work a chance to show you what they're like.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要给不同类型的工作一个机会来展示它们是什么样的。

sentences.en: But a field should become increasingly interesting as you learn more about it.
sentences.zh: 但当你对某个领域了解得越多时，它就会变得越来越有趣。

sentences.en: If it doesn't, it's probably not for you.Don't worry if you find you're interested in different things than other people.
sentences.zh: 如果没有，它可能不适合您。如果您发现自己对与其他人不同的事物感兴趣，请不要担心。

sentences.en: The stranger your tastes in interestingness, the better.
sentences.zh: 你的兴趣爱好越陌生越好。

sentences.en: Strange tastes are often strong ones, and a strong taste for work means you'll be productive.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的品味往往很强烈，而强烈的工作品味意味着你会富有成效。

sentences.en: And you're more likely to find new things if you're looking where few have looked before.One sign that you're suited for some kind of work is when you like even the parts that other people find tedious or frightening.But fields aren't people; you don't owe them any loyalty.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在寻找以前很少有人看过的地方，你就更有可能发现新的东西。你适合某种工作的一个迹象是，你甚至喜欢其他人觉得乏味或令人恐惧的部分。但领域不是人；它是人。你不欠他们任何忠诚。

sentences.en: If in the course of working on one thing you discover another that's more exciting, don't be afraid to switch.If you're making something for people, make sure it's something they actually want.
sentences.zh: 如果在做一件事的过程中你发现另一件事更令人兴奋，不要害怕改变。如果你正在为人们做一些事情，请确保这是他们真正想要的东西。

sentences.en: The best way to do this is to make something you yourself want.
sentences.zh: 做到这一点的最好方法就是做一些你自己想要的东西。

sentences.en: Write the story you want to read; build the tool you want to use.
sentences.zh: 写下你想读的故事；构建您想要使用的工具。

sentences.en: Since your friends probably have similar interests, this will also get you your initial audience.This should follow from the excitingness rule.
sentences.zh: 由于您的朋友可能有相似的兴趣，这也将为您提供最初的受众。这应该遵循令人兴奋的规则。

sentences.en: Obviously the most exciting story to write will be the one you want to read.
sentences.zh: 显然，最令人兴奋的故事将是您想读的故事。

sentences.en: The reason I mention this case explicitly is that so many people get it wrong.
sentences.zh: 我之所以明确提及这个案例，是因为很多人都误解了。

sentences.en: Instead of making what they want, they try to make what some imaginary, more sophisticated audience wants.
sentences.zh: 他们没有制作他们想要的东西，而是尝试制作一些想象中的、更复杂的观众想要的东西。

sentences.en: And once you go down that route, you're lost. [6]There are a lot of forces that will lead you astray when you're trying to figure out what to work on.
sentences.zh: 一旦你沿着这条路走下去，你就会迷路。 [6]当你试图弄清楚要做什么时，有很多力量会让你误入歧途。

sentences.en: Pretentiousness, fashion, fear, money, politics, other people's wishes, eminent frauds.
sentences.zh: 自命不凡、时尚、恐惧、金钱、政治、他人的愿望、显着的欺诈。

sentences.en: But if you stick to what you find genuinely interesting, you'll be proof against all of them.
sentences.zh: 但如果你坚持做你真正感兴趣的事情，你就会战胜所有这些。

sentences.en: If you're interested, you're not astray.
sentences.zh: 如果你有兴趣，你就不会迷路。

sentences.en: Following your interests may sound like a rather passive strategy, but in practice it usually means following them past all sorts of obstacles.
sentences.zh: 追随你的兴趣可能听起来像是一种相当被动的策略，但实际上，这通常意味着追随你的兴趣，克服各种障碍。

sentences.en: You usually have to risk rejection and failure.
sentences.zh: 你通常必须冒被拒绝和失败的风险。

sentences.en: So it does take a good deal of boldness.But while you need boldness, you don't usually need much planning.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实需要很大的勇气。但是，虽然你需要勇气，但通常不需要太多的计划。

sentences.en: In most cases the recipe for doing great work is simply: work hard on excitingly ambitious projects, and something good will come of it.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，做好工作的秘诀很简单：在令人兴奋的雄心勃勃的项目上努力工作，并且会带来好的结果。

sentences.en: Instead of making a plan and then executing it, you just try to preserve certain invariants.The trouble with planning is that it only works for achievements you can describe in advance.
sentences.zh: 您不必制定计划然后执行它，而只需尝试保留某些不变量。计划的问题在于它仅适用于您可以提前描述的成就。

sentences.en: You can win a gold medal or get rich by deciding to as a child and then tenaciously pursuing that goal, but you can't discover natural selection that way.I think for most people who want to do great work, the right strategy is not to plan too much.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过小时候的决定，然后顽强地追求这个目标来赢得金牌或致富，但你无法通过这种方式发现自然选择。我认为，对于大多数想要做出伟大工作的人来说，正确的策略是不要计划太多。

sentences.en: At each stage do whatever seems most interesting and gives you the best options for the future.
sentences.zh: 在每个阶段，做任何看起来最有趣的事情，并为你的未来提供最好的选择。

sentences.en: I call this approach "staying upwind."
sentences.zh: 我将这种方法称为“保持上风”。

sentences.en: This is how most people who've done great work seem to have done it.
sentences.zh: 大多数做出伟大工作的人似乎都是这样做的。

sentences.en: Even when you've found something exciting to work on, working on it is not always straightforward.
sentences.zh: 即使你发现了一些令人兴奋的事情可以做，但做起来并不总是那么简单。

sentences.en: There will be times when some new idea makes you leap out of bed in the morning and get straight to work.
sentences.zh: 有时，一些新想法会让你早上从床上跳起来直接开始工作。

sentences.en: But there will also be plenty of times when things aren't like that.You don't just put out your sail and get blown forward by inspiration.
sentences.zh: 但也有很多时候事情并非如此。你不会只是扬帆起航，被灵感吹向前方。

sentences.en: There are headwinds and currents and hidden shoals.
sentences.zh: 这里有逆风、洋流和隐藏的浅滩。

sentences.en: So there's a technique to working, just as there is to sailing.For example, while you must work hard, it's possible to work too hard, and if you do that you'll find you get diminishing returns: fatigue will make you stupid, and eventually even damage your health.
sentences.zh: 所以工作是有技巧的，就像航海一样。比如，虽然你必须努力工作，但也有可能工作过度，如果你这样做，你会发现你的收益递减：疲劳会让你变得愚蠢，最终甚至损害你的健康。

sentences.en: The point at which work yields diminishing returns depends on the type.
sentences.zh: 工作收益递减的点取决于工作类型。

sentences.en: Some of the hardest types you might only be able to do for four or five hours a day.Ideally those hours will be contiguous.
sentences.zh: 一些最困难的类型您可能每天只能做四到五个小时。理想情况下，这些时间是连续的。

sentences.en: To the extent you can, try to arrange your life so you have big blocks of time to work in.
sentences.zh: 在力所能及的范围内，尽量安排好你的生活，这样你就有大量的时间可以用来工作。

sentences.en: You'll shy away from hard tasks if you know you might be interrupted.It will probably be harder to start working than to keep working.
sentences.zh: 如果您知道自己可能会被打扰，您就会回避艰巨的任务。开始工作可能比继续工作更困难。

sentences.en: You'll often have to trick yourself to get over that initial threshold.
sentences.zh: 你经常需要欺骗自己才能跨过最初的门槛。

sentences.en: Don't worry about this; it's the nature of work, not a flaw in your character.
sentences.zh: 不用担心这个；这是工作的本质，而不是你性格上的缺陷。

sentences.en: Work has a sort of activation energy, both per day and per project.
sentences.zh: 工作有一种激活能量，无论是每天还是每个项目。

sentences.en: And since this threshold is fake in the sense that it's higher than the energy required to keep going, it's ok to tell yourself a lie of corresponding magnitude to get over it.It's usually a mistake to lie to yourself if you want to do great work, but this is one of the rare cases where it isn't.
sentences.zh: 由于这个阈值是假的，因为它高于继续前进所需的能量，所以可以告诉自己一个相应大小的谎言来克服它。如果你想做好工作，对自己撒谎通常是一个错误，但这是极少数情况之一。

sentences.en: When I'm reluctant to start work in the morning, I often trick myself by saying "I'll just read over what I've got so far."
sentences.zh: 当我早上不愿意开始工作时，我经常欺骗自己说：“我会读一下到目前为止所读到的内容。”

sentences.en: Five minutes later I've found something that seems mistaken or incomplete, and I'm off.Similar techniques work for starting new projects.
sentences.zh: 五分钟后，我发现了一些似乎错误或不完整的东西，然后我就离开了。类似的技术也适用于启动新项目。

sentences.en: It's ok to lie to yourself about how much work a project will entail, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，在一个项目需要多少工作量上对自己撒谎是可以的。

sentences.en: Lots of great things began with someone saying "How hard could it be?"This is one case where the young have an advantage.
sentences.zh: 很多伟大的事情都是从有人说“这能有多难？”开始的，这就是年轻人有优势的一个例子。

sentences.en: They're more optimistic, and even though one of the sources of their optimism is ignorance, in this case ignorance can sometimes beat knowledge.Try to finish what you start, though, even if it turns out to be more work than you expected.
sentences.zh: 他们更加乐观，尽管他们乐观的根源之一是无知，但在这种情况下，无知有时可以打败知识。尽管如此，尝试完成你开始的事情，即使结果比你预期的工作量要多。

sentences.en: Finishing things is not just an exercise in tidiness or self-discipline.
sentences.zh: 完成事情不仅仅是一种整洁或自律的练习。

sentences.en: In many projects a lot of the best work happens in what was meant to be the final stage.Another permissible lie is to exaggerate the importance of what you're working on, at least in your own mind.
sentences.zh: 在许多项目中，很多最好的工作都发生在最后阶段。另一个允许的谎言是夸大你正在做的事情的重要性，至少在你自己看来是这样。

sentences.en: If that helps you discover something new, it may turn out not to have been a lie after all. [7] Since there are two senses of starting work — per day and per project — there are also two forms of procrastination.
sentences.zh: 如果这能帮助你发现新的东西，那么它可能根本就不是谎言。 [7] 由于开始工作有两种意义——每天和每个项目——所以拖延也有两种形式。

sentences.en: Per-project procrastination is far the more dangerous.
sentences.zh: 每个项目的拖延更加危险。

sentences.en: You put off starting that ambitious project from year to year because the time isn't quite right.
sentences.zh: 你年复一年地推迟启动这个雄心勃勃的项目，因为时间不太合适。

sentences.en: When you're procrastinating in units of years, you can get a lot not done. [8]One reason per-project procrastination is so dangerous is that it usually camouflages itself as work.
sentences.zh: 当你以年为单位拖延时，你可能会做很多事情没有完成。 [8]每个项目的拖延如此危险的一个原因是它通常将自己伪装成工作。

sentences.en: You're not just sitting around doing nothing; you're working industriously on something else.
sentences.zh: 你不只是坐在那里无所事事；你正在勤奋地做其他事情。

sentences.en: So per-project procrastination doesn't set off the alarms that per-day procrastination does.
sentences.zh: 因此，按项目拖延不会像按天拖延那样引发警报。

sentences.en: You're too busy to notice it.The way to beat it is to stop occasionally and ask yourself: Am I working on what I most want to work on?
sentences.zh: 你太忙而没有注意到它。克服它的方法是偶尔停下来问自己：我正在做我最想做的事情吗？

sentences.en: When you're young it's ok if the answer is sometimes no, but this gets increasingly dangerous as you get older. [9] Great work usually entails spending what would seem to most people an unreasonable amount of time on a problem.
sentences.zh: 当你年轻的时候，如果答案有时是否定的，那也没关系，但随着年龄的增长，这会变得越来越危险。 [9] 伟大的工作通常需要在一个问题上花费对大多数人来说似乎不合理的时间。

sentences.en: You can't think of this time as a cost, or it will seem too high.
sentences.zh: 你不能把这个时间当成成本，不然会显得太高了。

sentences.en: You have to find the work sufficiently engaging as it's happening.There may be some jobs where you have to work diligently for years at things you hate before you get to the good part, but this is not how great work happens.
sentences.zh: 你必须发现这项工作足够有吸引力。在某些工作中，你可能必须在你讨厌的事情上勤奋工作数年才能获得好的部分，但这并不是伟大工作的发生方式。

sentences.en: Great work happens by focusing consistently on something you're genuinely interested in.
sentences.zh: 伟大的工作是通过持续专注于你真正感兴趣的事情而实现的。

sentences.en: When you pause to take stock, you're surprised how far you've come.The reason we're surprised is that we underestimate the cumulative effect of work.
sentences.zh: 当你停下来盘点时，你会惊讶于自己已经走了多远。我们感到惊讶的原因是我们低估了工作的累积效应。

sentences.en: Writing a page a day doesn't sound like much, but if you do it every day you'll write a book a year.
sentences.zh: 每天写一页听起来不多，但如果你每天都这样做，一年就可以写一本书。

sentences.en: That's the key: consistency.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键：一致性。

sentences.en: People who do great things don't get a lot done every day.
sentences.zh: 做伟大事情的人并不是每天都能完成很多事情。

sentences.en: They get something done, rather than nothing.If you do work that compounds, you'll get exponential growth.
sentences.zh: 他们完成了一些事情，而不是什么都不做。如果你做复合的工作，你就会得到指数级的增长。

sentences.en: Most people who do this do it unconsciously, but it's worth stopping to think about.
sentences.zh: 大多数这样做的人都是无意识的，但值得停下来思考一下。

sentences.en: Learning, for example, is an instance of this phenomenon: the more you learn about something, the easier it is to learn more.
sentences.zh: 例如，学习就是这种现象的一个例子：你对某事物了解得越多，就越容易学到更多。

sentences.en: Growing an audience is another: the more fans you have, the more new fans they'll bring you.The trouble with exponential growth is that the curve feels flat in the beginning.
sentences.zh: 增加观众是另一回事：你拥有的粉丝越多，他们就会为你带来越多的新粉丝。指数增长的问题在于，曲线一开始感觉很平坦。

sentences.en: It isn't; it's still a wonderful exponential curve.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此；它仍然是一条美妙的指数曲线。

sentences.en: But we can't grasp that intuitively, so we underrate exponential growth in its early stages.Something that grows exponentially can become so valuable that it's worth making an extraordinary effort to get it started.
sentences.zh: 但我们无法直观地理解这一点，因此我们低估了早期阶段的指数增长。指数增长的东西可以变得如此有价值，以至于值得付出非凡的努力来开始它。

sentences.en: But since we underrate exponential growth early on, this too is mostly done unconsciously: people push through the initial, unrewarding phase of learning something new because they know from experience that learning new things always takes an initial push, or they grow their audience one fan at a time because they have nothing better to do.
sentences.zh: 但由于我们早期低估了指数增长，这也大多是无意识地完成的：人们在学习新东西的最初、无回报的阶段中坚持下去，因为他们从经验中知道学习新东西总是需要最初的推动，或者他们一次培养一个粉丝，因为他们没有更好的事情可做。

sentences.en: If people consciously realized they could invest in exponential growth, many more would do it.
sentences.zh: 如果人们有意识地意识到他们可以投资于指数级增长，就会有更多人这样做。

sentences.en: Work doesn't just happen when you're trying to.
sentences.zh: 工作不会在你努力的时候发生。

sentences.en: There's a kind of undirected thinking you do when walking or taking a shower or lying in bed that can be very powerful.
sentences.zh: 当你走路、洗澡或躺在床上时，你会产生一种非常强大的无向思维。

sentences.en: By letting your mind wander a little, you'll often solve problems you were unable to solve by frontal attack.You have to be working hard in the normal way to benefit from this phenomenon, though.
sentences.zh: 通过让你的思维稍微走神，你通常会解决你通过正面攻击无法解决的问题。不过，你必须以正常的方式努力工作才能从这种现象中受益。

sentences.en: You can't just walk around daydreaming.
sentences.zh: 你不能只是到处走走做白日梦。

sentences.en: The daydreaming has to be interleaved with deliberate work that feeds it questions. [10]Everyone knows to avoid distractions at work, but it's also important to avoid them in the other half of the cycle.
sentences.zh: 白日梦必须与那些为其提出问题的深思熟虑的工作交织在一起。 [10]每个人都知道在工作中避免干扰，但在周期的另一半中避免干扰也很重要。

sentences.en: When you let your mind wander, it wanders to whatever you care about most at that moment.
sentences.zh: 当你让你的思绪游离时，它就会飘到你当时最关心的事情上。

sentences.en: So avoid the kind of distraction that pushes your work out of the top spot, or you'll waste this valuable type of thinking on the distraction instead.
sentences.zh: 因此，要避免那种让你的工作失去优势的干扰，否则你就会把这种宝贵的思考浪费在干扰上。

sentences.en: (Exception: Don't avoid love.)
sentences.zh: （例外：不要回避爱。）

sentences.en: Consciously cultivate your taste in the work done in your field.
sentences.zh: 有意识地培养你对自己领域工作的品味。

sentences.en: Until you know which is the best and what makes it so, you don't know what you're aiming for.And that is what you're aiming for, because if you don't try to be the best, you won't even be good.
sentences.zh: 除非你知道哪个是最好的以及是什么让它如此，否则你不知道自己的目标是什么。而这就是你的目标，因为如果你不努力成为最好的，你甚至都不会优秀。

sentences.en: This observation has been made by so many people in so many different fields that it might be worth thinking about why it's true.
sentences.zh: 许多不同领域的许多人都做出了这一观察，因此可能值得思考为什么它是正确的。

sentences.en: It could be because ambition is a phenomenon where almost all the error is in one direction — where almost all the shells that miss the target miss by falling short.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为野心是一种现象，几乎所有的错误都在一个方向上——几乎所有未击中目标的炮弹都因未能达到目标而错过。

sentences.en: Or it could be because ambition to be the best is a qualitatively different thing from ambition to be good.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是因为“成为最好的”的野心与“成为优秀的人”的野心有本质上的不同。

sentences.en: Or maybe being good is simply too vague a standard.
sentences.zh: 或者，也许“善良”这个标准太模糊了。

sentences.en: Probably all three are true. [11]Fortunately there's a kind of economy of scale here.
sentences.zh: 也许这三个都是真的。 [11]幸运的是，这里有一种规模经济。

sentences.en: Though it might seem like you'd be taking on a heavy burden by trying to be the best, in practice you often end up net ahead.
sentences.zh: 虽然看起来你会因为努力成为最好而承担沉重的负担，但实际上你常常最终会取得净领先。

sentences.en: It's exciting, and also strangely liberating.
sentences.zh: 这很令人兴奋，也有一种奇怪的解放感。

sentences.en: It simplifies things.
sentences.zh: 它简化了事情。

sentences.en: In some ways it's easier to try to be the best than to try merely to be good.One way to aim high is to try to make something that people will care about in a hundred years.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来说，努力做到最好比仅仅努力做到优秀更容易。志存高远的一种方法是努力做出一百年后人们会关心的东西。

sentences.en: Not because their opinions matter more than your contemporaries', but because something that still seems good in a hundred years is more likely to be genuinely good.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为他们的观点比同时代人的观点更重要，而是因为一百年后看起来仍然不错的东西更有可能是真正的好东西。

sentences.en: Don't try to work in a distinctive style.
sentences.zh: 不要尝试以独特的风格工作。

sentences.en: Just try to do the best job you can; you won't be able to help doing it in a distinctive way.Style is doing things in a distinctive way without trying to.
sentences.zh: 尽力把工作做到最好；你会情不自禁地以独特的方式做事。风格就是以独特的方式做事，而不是试图去做。

sentences.en: Trying to is affectation.Affectation is in effect to pretend that someone other than you is doing the work.
sentences.zh: 试图这样做就是做作。做作实际上是假装是别人在做这项工作，而不是你。

sentences.en: You adopt an impressive but fake persona, and while you're pleased with the impressiveness, the fakeness is what shows in the work. [12]The temptation to be someone else is greatest for the young.
sentences.zh: 你采用了一个令人印象深刻但虚假的角色，虽然你对这种印象很满意，但作品中却表现出了虚假。 [12]对于年轻人来说，成为别人的诱惑是最大的。

sentences.en: They often feel like nobodies.
sentences.zh: 他们常常感觉自己无名小卒。

sentences.en: But you never need to worry about that problem, because it's self-solving if you work on sufficiently ambitious projects.
sentences.zh: 但你永远不需要担心这个问题，因为如果你从事足够雄心勃勃的项目，它是可以自行解决的。

sentences.en: If you succeed at an ambitious project, you're not a nobody; you're the person who did it.
sentences.zh: 如果你在一个雄心勃勃的项目上取得了成功，那么你就不再是一个无名小卒；而是一个无名小卒。你就是做这件事的人。

sentences.en: So just do the work and your identity will take care of itself.
sentences.zh: 因此，只要做好工作，你的身份就会水到渠成。

sentences.en: "Avoid affectation" is a useful rule so far as it goes, but how would you express this idea positively?
sentences.zh: 就目前而言，“避免矫揉造作”是一条有用的规则，但你会如何积极地表达这个想法呢？

sentences.en: How would you say what to be, instead of what not to be?
sentences.zh: 你会如何说应该做什么，而不是不应该做什么？

sentences.en: The best answer is earnest.
sentences.zh: 最好的回答是认真的。

sentences.en: If you're earnest you avoid not just affectation but a whole set of similar vices.The core of being earnest is being intellectually honest.
sentences.zh: 如果你认真，你不仅可以避免做作，还可以避免一整套类似的恶习。认真的核心是在理智上诚实。

sentences.en: We're taught as children to be honest as an unselfish virtue — as a kind of sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 我们从小就被教导要诚实，这是一种无私的美德，也是一种牺牲。

sentences.en: But in fact it's a source of power too.
sentences.zh: 但事实上它也是一种力量的来源。

sentences.en: To see new ideas, you need an exceptionally sharp eye for the truth.
sentences.zh: 要看到新的想法，你需要有一双敏锐的眼睛来发现真相。

sentences.en: You're trying to see more truth than others have seen so far.
sentences.zh: 你正试图看到比其他人迄今为止看到的更多的真相。

sentences.en: And how can you have a sharp eye for the truth if you're intellectually dishonest?One way to avoid intellectual dishonesty is to maintain a slight positive pressure in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 如果你在智力上不诚实，你怎么能有敏锐的洞察力呢？避免智力上的不诚实的一种方法是在相反的方向上保持轻微的正压力。

sentences.en: Be aggressively willing to admit that you're mistaken.
sentences.zh: 积极主动地承认自己的错误。

sentences.en: Once you've admitted you were mistaken about something, you're free.
sentences.zh: 一旦你承认自己在某件事上犯了错误，你就自由了。

sentences.en: Till then you have to carry it. [13]Another more subtle component of earnestness is informality.
sentences.zh: 到那时你必须携带它。 [13]真诚的另一个更微妙的组成部分是非正式的。

sentences.en: Informality is much more important than its grammatically negative name implies.
sentences.zh: 非正式性比其语法上否定的名称所暗示的重要得多。

sentences.en: It's not merely the absence of something.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是缺少某些东西。

sentences.en: It means focusing on what matters instead of what doesn't.What formality and affectation have in common is that as well as doing the work, you're trying to seem a certain way as you're doing it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着专注于重要的事情，而不是不重要的事情。拘谨和矫揉造作的共同点是，除了工作之外，你还试图在工作中表现出某种特定的方式。

sentences.en: But any energy that goes into how you seem comes out of being good.
sentences.zh: 但任何影响你外表的能量都来自于善良。

sentences.en: That's one reason nerds have an advantage in doing great work: they expend little effort on seeming anything.
sentences.zh: 这就是书呆子在完成出色工作时具有优势的原因之一：他们很少花精力在外表上。

sentences.en: In fact that's basically the definition of a nerd.Nerds have a kind of innocent boldness that's exactly what you need in doing great work.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这基本上就是书呆子的定义。书呆子有一种天真的勇气，这正是你完成伟大工作所需要的。

sentences.en: It's not learned; it's preserved from childhood.
sentences.zh: 这不是学来的；它是从童年就保存下来的。

sentences.en: So hold onto it.
sentences.zh: 所以坚持下去。

sentences.en: Be the one who puts things out there rather than the one who sits back and offers sophisticated-sounding criticisms of them.
sentences.zh: 成为一个把事情摆出来的人，而不是一个袖手旁观并对其提出听起来复杂的批评的人。

sentences.en: "It's easy to criticize" is true in the most literal sense, and the route to great work is never easy.There may be some jobs where it's an advantage to be cynical and pessimistic, but if you want to do great work it's an advantage to be optimistic, even though that means you'll risk looking like a fool sometimes.
sentences.zh: “批评很容易”这句话从字面意义上来说是正确的，而通往伟大工作的道路从来都不是一帆风顺的。在某些工作中，愤世嫉俗和悲观可能是一种优势，但如果你想做好工作，乐观就是一种优势，尽管这意味着你有时会冒着看起来像个傻瓜的风险。

sentences.en: There's an old tradition of doing the opposite.
sentences.zh: 有一种反其道而行之的古老传统。

sentences.en: The Old Testament says it's better to keep quiet lest you look like a fool.
sentences.zh: 旧约说最好保持安静，以免看起来像个傻瓜。

sentences.en: But that's advice for seeming smart.
sentences.zh: 但这是显得聪明的建议。

sentences.en: If you actually want to discover new things, it's better to take the risk of telling people your ideas.Some people are naturally earnest, and with others it takes a conscious effort.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想发现新事物，最好冒险告诉别人你的想法。有些人天生很认真，而另一些人则需要有意识的努力。

sentences.en: Either kind of earnestness will suffice.
sentences.zh: 任何一种认真就足够了。

sentences.en: But I doubt it would be possible to do great work without being earnest.
sentences.zh: 但我怀疑，如果不认真，就不可能做出伟大的工作。

sentences.en: It's so hard to do even if you are.
sentences.zh: 即使你是这样，也很难做到。

sentences.en: You don't have enough margin for error to accommodate the distortions introduced by being affected, intellectually dishonest, orthodox, fashionable, or cool. [14] Great work is consistent not only with who did it, but with itself.
sentences.zh: 你没有足够的容错余地来适应因受影响、智力上的不诚实、正统、时尚或酷而带来的扭曲。 [14] 伟大的工作不仅与完成者一致，而且与其本身一致。

sentences.en: It's usually all of a piece.
sentences.zh: 通常都是一个整体。

sentences.en: So if you face a decision in the middle of working on something, ask which choice is more consistent.You may have to throw things away and redo them.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在做某件事的过程中面临一个决定，问问哪个选择更一致。你可能不得不扔掉东西并重做。

sentences.en: You won't necessarily have to, but you have to be willing to.
sentences.zh: 你不一定必须这样做，但你必须愿意这样做。

sentences.en: And that can take some effort; when there's something you need to redo, status quo bias and laziness will combine to keep you in denial about it.
sentences.zh: 这可能需要一些努力；当你需要重做某些事情时，现状偏见和懒惰会让你否认它。

sentences.en: To beat this ask: If I'd already made the change, would I want to revert to what I have now?Have the confidence to cut.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，请问：如果我已经做出了改变，我想恢​​复到现在的状态吗？有信心去削减。

sentences.en: Don't keep something that doesn't fit just because you're proud of it, or because it cost you a lot of effort.Indeed, in some kinds of work it's good to strip whatever you're doing to its essence.
sentences.zh: 不要仅仅因为你为之自豪，或者因为它花费了你很多努力而保留一些不合适的东西。事实上，在某些类型的工作中，剥离你正在做的事情的本质是件好事。

sentences.en: The result will be more concentrated; you'll understand it better; and you won't be able to lie to yourself about whether there's anything real there.Mathematical elegance may sound like a mere metaphor, drawn from the arts.
sentences.zh: 结果会更集中；你会更好地理解它；你无法对自己说谎，说那里是否有真实的东西。数学的优雅听起来可能只是一个来自艺术的隐喻。

sentences.en: That's what I thought when I first heard the term "elegant" applied to a proof.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次听到“优雅”一词应用于证明时，我就是这么想的。

sentences.en: But now I suspect it's conceptually prior — that the main ingredient in artistic elegance is mathematical elegance.
sentences.zh: 但现在我怀疑它在概念上是先验的——艺术优雅的主要成分是数学优雅。

sentences.en: At any rate it's a useful standard well beyond math.Elegance can be a long-term bet, though.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，它是一个远远超出数学范围的有用标准。不过，优雅可以是一个长期的赌注。

sentences.en: Laborious solutions will often have more prestige in the short term.
sentences.zh: 费力的解决方案往往会在短期内获得更高的威望。

sentences.en: They cost a lot of effort and they're hard to understand, both of which impress people, at least temporarily.Whereas some of the very best work will seem like it took comparatively little effort, because it was in a sense already there.
sentences.zh: 它们花费了大量的精力，而且很难理解，这两点都给人留下了深刻的印象，至少是暂时的。而一些最好的作品看起来似乎花费了相对较少的努力，因为它在某种意义上已经存在了。

sentences.en: It didn't have to be built, just seen.
sentences.zh: 它不必建造，只需观看即可。

sentences.en: It's a very good sign when it's hard to say whether you're creating something or discovering it.When you're doing work that could be seen as either creation or discovery, err on the side of discovery.
sentences.zh: 当很难说你是在创造某些东西还是在发现它时，这是一个非常好的迹象。当你正在做的工作可以被视为创造或发现时，最好选择发现。

sentences.en: Try thinking of yourself as a mere conduit through which the ideas take their natural shape.(Strangely enough, one exception is the problem of choosing a problem to work on.
sentences.zh: 试着把自己想象成一个简单的渠道，通过这个渠道，想法自然形成。（奇怪的是，一个例外是选择要解决的问题。

sentences.en: This is usually seen as search, but in the best case it's more like creating something.
sentences.zh: 这通常被视为搜索，但在最好的情况下它更像是创建一些东西。

sentences.en: In the best case you create the field in the process of exploring it.)Similarly, if you're trying to build a powerful tool, make it gratuitously unrestrictive.
sentences.zh: 在最好的情况下，您在探索它的过程中创建了该领域。）同样，如果您正在尝试构建一个强大的工具，请使其无缘无故地不受限制。

sentences.en: A powerful tool almost by definition will be used in ways you didn't expect, so err on the side of eliminating restrictions, even if you don't know what the benefit will be.Great work will often be tool-like in the sense of being something others build on.
sentences.zh: 一个强大的工具几乎从定义上讲就会以你意想不到的方式使用，所以即使你不知道会有什么好处，最好还是消除限制。伟大的工作往往是像工具一样的，因为它是其他人构建的东西。

sentences.en: So it's a good sign if you're creating ideas that others could use, or exposing questions that others could answer.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果您正在创造其他人可以使用的想法，或者提出其他人可以回答的问题，那么这是一个好兆头。

sentences.en: The best ideas have implications in many different areas.If you express your ideas in the most general form, they'll be truer than you intended.
sentences.zh: 最好的想法在许多不同的领域都有影响。如果你以最一般的形式表达你的想法，它们会比你想要的更真实。

sentences.en: True by itself is not enough, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，真实本身还不够。

sentences.en: Great ideas have to be true and new.
sentences.zh: 伟大的想法必须是真实的和新颖的。

sentences.en: And it takes a certain amount of ability to see new ideas even once you've learned enough to get to one of the frontiers of knowledge.In English we give this ability names like originality, creativity, and imagination.
sentences.zh: 即使你已经学到了足够多的知识以达到知识的前沿之一，也需要一定的能力才能看到​​新的想法。在英语中，我们给这种能力起名字，比如原创性、创造力和想象力。

sentences.en: And it seems reasonable to give it a separate name, because it does seem to some extent a separate skill.
sentences.zh: 给它一个单独的名称似乎是合理的，因为它在某种程度上似乎确实是一个单独的技能。

sentences.en: It's possible to have a great deal of ability in other respects — to have a great deal of what's often called technical ability — and yet not have much of this.I've never liked the term "creative process."
sentences.zh: 有可能在其他方面拥有大量的能力——拥有大量通常被称为技术能力的东西——但在这方面却没有太多。我从来不喜欢“创造性过程”这个词。

sentences.en: It seems misleading.
sentences.zh: 这似乎有误导性。

sentences.en: Originality isn't a process, but a habit of mind.
sentences.zh: 原创不是一个过程，而是一种思维习惯。

sentences.en: Original thinkers throw off new ideas about whatever they focus on, like an angle grinder throwing off sparks.
sentences.zh: 原创思想家对他们关注的任何事物都会抛出新的想法，就像角磨机抛出火花一样。

sentences.en: They can't help it.If the thing they're focused on is something they don't understand very well, these new ideas might not be good.
sentences.zh: 他们没办法。如果他们所关注的事情是他们不太理解的事情，那么这些新想法可能就不好。

sentences.en: One of the most original thinkers I know decided to focus on dating after he got divorced.
sentences.zh: 我认识的一位最具原创性的思想家在离婚后决定专注于约会。

sentences.en: He knew roughly as much about dating as the average 15 year old, and the results were spectacularly colorful.
sentences.zh: 他对约会的了解与一般 15 岁的人大致相同，而且约会的结果也非常丰富多彩。

sentences.en: But to see originality separated from expertise like that made its nature all the more clear.I don't know if it's possible to cultivate originality, but there are definitely ways to make the most of however much you have.
sentences.zh: 但将原创性与专业知识分开后，它的本质就更加清晰了。我不知道是否有可能培养原创性，但肯定有方法可以充分利用你所拥有的一切。

sentences.en: For example, you're much more likely to have original ideas when you're working on something.
sentences.zh: 例如，当你在做某事时，你更有可能产生原创想法。

sentences.en: Original ideas don't come from trying to have original ideas.
sentences.zh: 原创想法并不是来自尝试拥有原创想法。

sentences.en: They come from trying to build or understand something slightly too difficult. [15]Talking or writing about the things you're interested in is a good way to generate new ideas.
sentences.zh: 它们来自于尝试构建或理解一些稍微困难的东西。 [15]谈论或写下你感兴趣的事情是产生新想法的好方法。

sentences.en: When you try to put ideas into words, a missing idea creates a sort of vacuum that draws it out of you.
sentences.zh: 当你试图把想法变成文字时，一个缺失的想法会产生一种真空，将你的想法从你身上吸走。

sentences.en: Indeed, there's a kind of thinking that can only be done by writing.Changing your context can help.
sentences.zh: 确实，有一种思考只能通过写作来完成。改变你的背景会有所帮助。

sentences.en: If you visit a new place, you'll often find you have new ideas there.
sentences.zh: 如果你去一个新地方，你经常会发现那里有新的想法。

sentences.en: The journey itself often dislodges them.
sentences.zh: 旅程本身常常让他们感到流离失所。

sentences.en: But you may not have to go far to get this benefit.
sentences.zh: 但您可能不需要走很远就能获得这种好处。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's enough just to go for a walk. [16]It also helps to travel in topic space.
sentences.zh: 有时候，只是去散步就足够了。 [16]它也有助于在主题空间中旅行。

sentences.en: You'll have more new ideas if you explore lots of different topics, partly because it gives the angle grinder more surface area to work on, and partly because analogies are an especially fruitful source of new ideas.Don't divide your attention evenly between many topics though, or you'll spread yourself too thin.
sentences.zh: 如果你探索许多不同的主题，你就会有更多的新想法，部分原因是它为角磨机提供了更多的工作空间，部分原因是类比是新想法特别富有成效的来源。不过，不要将你的注意力均匀地分散在许多主题上，否则你会分散自己太分散。

sentences.en: You want to distribute it according to something more like a power law. [17] Be professionally curious about a few topics and idly curious about many more.Curiosity and originality are closely related.
sentences.zh: 你想根据更像幂律的东西来分配它。 [17] 对一些主题保持职业好奇，并对更多主题保持闲散好奇。好奇心和原创性密切相关。

sentences.en: Curiosity feeds originality by giving it new things to work on.
sentences.zh: 好奇心通过给予新的工作机会来滋养原创性。

sentences.en: But the relationship is closer than that.
sentences.zh: 但关系比这更密切。

sentences.en: Curiosity is itself a kind of originality; it's roughly to questions what originality is to answers.
sentences.zh: 好奇心本身就是一种原创性；粗略地说，问题的原创性就是答案的原创性。

sentences.en: And since questions at their best are a big component of answers, curiosity at its best is a creative force.
sentences.zh: 由于问题在最好的情况下是答案的重要组成部分，因此好奇心在最好的情况下是一种创造力。

sentences.en: Having new ideas is a strange game, because it usually consists of seeing things that were right under your nose.
sentences.zh: 产生新想法是一种奇怪的游戏，因为它通常包括看到就在你眼皮子底下的东西。

sentences.en: Once you've seen a new idea, it tends to seem obvious.
sentences.zh: 一旦你看到一个新想法，它往往看起来很明显。

sentences.en: Why did no one think of this before?When an idea seems simultaneously novel and obvious, it's probably a good one.Seeing something obvious sounds easy.
sentences.zh: 为什么以前没有人想到这一点？当一个想法看起来既新颖又显而易见时，它可能是一个好想法。看到显而易见的事情听起来很容易。

sentences.en: And yet empirically having new ideas is hard.
sentences.zh: 然而，凭经验获得新想法是很困难的。

sentences.en: What's the source of this apparent contradiction?
sentences.zh: 这种明显矛盾的根源是什么？

sentences.en: It's that seeing the new idea usually requires you to change the way you look at the world.
sentences.zh: 看到新想法通常需要你改变看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: We see the world through models that both help and constrain us.
sentences.zh: 我们通过既帮助又限制我们的模型来看待世界。

sentences.en: When you fix a broken model, new ideas become obvious.
sentences.zh: 当你修复损坏的模型时，新的想法就会变得显而易见。

sentences.en: But noticing and fixing a broken model is hard.
sentences.zh: 但发现并修复损坏的模型是很困难的。

sentences.en: That's how new ideas can be both obvious and yet hard to discover: they're easy to see after you do something hard.One way to discover broken models is to be stricter than other people.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么新想法既显而易见又难以发现：在你做了一些困难的事情之后，它们很容易被发现。发现损坏模型的一种方法是比其他人更严格。

sentences.en: Broken models of the world leave a trail of clues where they bash against reality.
sentences.zh: 破碎的世界模型留下了与现实相悖的线索。

sentences.en: Most people don't want to see these clues.
sentences.zh: 大多数人不想看到这些线索。

sentences.en: It would be an understatement to say that they're attached to their current model; it's what they think in; so they'll tend to ignore the trail of clues left by its breakage, however conspicuous it may seem in retrospect.To find new ideas you have to seize on signs of breakage instead of looking away.
sentences.zh: 轻描淡写地说，他们依附于当前的模式。这就是他们的想法；因此，他们往往会忽略其破损留下的线索，无论回想起来多么明显。要找到新想法，你必须抓住破损的迹象，而不是移开目光。

sentences.en: That's what Einstein did.
sentences.zh: 这就是爱因斯坦所做的。

sentences.en: He was able to see the wild implications of Maxwell's equations not so much because he was looking for new ideas as because he was stricter.The other thing you need is a willingness to break rules.
sentences.zh: 他能够看到麦克斯韦方程组的巨大含义，与其说是因为他在寻找新的想法，不如说是因为他更加严格。你需要的另一件事是愿意打破规则。

sentences.en: Paradoxical as it sounds, if you want to fix your model of the world, it helps to be the sort of person who's comfortable breaking rules.
sentences.zh: 尽管听起来很矛盾，但如果你想修复你的世界模型，成为那种乐于打破规则的人会有所帮助。

sentences.en: From the point of view of the old model, which everyone including you initially shares, the new model usually breaks at least implicit rules.Few understand the degree of rule-breaking required, because new ideas seem much more conservative once they succeed.
sentences.zh: 从包括你在内的每个人最初共享的旧模式的角度来看，新模式通常至少会打破隐含的规则。很少有人了解需要打破规则的程度，因为新想法一旦成功就显得保守得多。

sentences.en: They seem perfectly reasonable once you're using the new model of the world they brought with them.
sentences.zh: 一旦你使用他们带来的新世界模型，他们看起来就完全合理了。

sentences.en: But they didn't at the time; it took the greater part of a century for the heliocentric model to be generally accepted, even among astronomers, because it felt so wrong.Indeed, if you think about it, a good new idea has to seem bad to most people, or someone would have already explored it.
sentences.zh: 但他们当时并没有这么做；日心说模型花了大半个世纪的时间才被普遍接受，甚至在天文学家中也是如此，因为它感觉太错误了。事实上，如果你仔细想想，一个好的新想法对大多数人来说一定看起来很糟糕，否则就有人已经探索过它了。

sentences.en: So what you're looking for is ideas that seem crazy, but the right kind of crazy.
sentences.zh: 所以你要寻找的是看似疯狂但真正疯狂的想法。

sentences.en: How do you recognize these?
sentences.zh: 你如何认识这些？

sentences.en: You can't with certainty.
sentences.zh: 你不能肯定。

sentences.en: Often ideas that seem bad are bad.
sentences.zh: 通常看似糟糕的想法实际上是糟糕的。

sentences.en: But ideas that are the right kind of crazy tend to be exciting; they're rich in implications; whereas ideas that are merely bad tend to be depressing.There are two ways to be comfortable breaking rules: to enjoy breaking them, and to be indifferent to them.
sentences.zh: 但真正疯狂的想法往往会令人兴奋。它们蕴含着丰富的含义；反之，仅仅糟糕的想法往往会令人沮丧。有两种方法可以让你轻松地打破规则：享受打破规则的乐趣，以及对规则漠不关心。

sentences.en: I call these two cases being aggressively and passively independent-minded.The aggressively independent-minded are the naughty ones.
sentences.zh: 我把这两种情况称为积极的独立思想和消极的独立思想。积极的独立思想是顽皮的。

sentences.en: Rules don't merely fail to stop them; breaking rules gives them additional energy.
sentences.zh: 规则不仅不能阻止它们，而且还能阻止它们。打破规则会给他们额外的能量。

sentences.en: For this sort of person, delight at the sheer audacity of a project sometimes supplies enough activation energy to get it started.The other way to break rules is not to care about them, or perhaps even to know they exist.
sentences.zh: 对于这类人来说，对一个项目的纯粹大胆感到高兴有时会提供足够的激活能量来启动它。打破规则的另一种方法是不关心它们，甚至不知道它们的存在。

sentences.en: This is why novices and outsiders often make new discoveries; their ignorance of a field's assumptions acts as a source of temporary passive independent-mindedness.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么新手和局外人经常会有新的发现；他们对某个领域的假设的无知是暂时被动独立思想的根源。

sentences.en: Aspies also seem to have a kind of immunity to conventional beliefs.
sentences.zh: 阿斯皮似乎对传统信仰也有一定的免疫力。

sentences.en: Several I know say that this helps them to have new ideas.Strictness plus rule-breaking sounds like a strange combination.
sentences.zh: 我认识的几个人说这有助于他们产生新想法。严格加上打破规则听起来像是一个奇怪的组合。

sentences.en: In popular culture they're opposed.
sentences.zh: 在流行文化中，他们是反对的。

sentences.en: But popular culture has a broken model in this respect.
sentences.zh: 但流行文化在这方面的模式已经被打破。

sentences.en: It implicitly assumes that issues are trivial ones, and in trivial matters strictness and rule-breaking are opposed.
sentences.zh: 它隐含地假定问题是琐碎的，在琐碎的事情上反对严格和破坏规则。

sentences.en: But in questions that really matter, only rule-breakers can be truly strict.
sentences.zh: 但在真正重要的问题上，只有打破规则的人才能真正严格。

sentences.en: An overlooked idea often doesn't lose till the semifinals.
sentences.zh: 一个被忽视的想法往往直到半决赛才输。

sentences.en: You do see it, subconsciously, but then another part of your subconscious shoots it down because it would be too weird, too risky, too much work, too controversial.
sentences.zh: 你确实在潜意识中看到了它，但你潜意识的另一部分却将其否决，因为它太奇怪、太冒险、太多工作、太有争议。

sentences.en: This suggests an exciting possibility: if you could turn off such filters, you could see more new ideas.One way to do that is to ask what would be good ideas for someone else to explore.
sentences.zh: 这表明了一种令人兴奋的可能性：如果您可以关闭此类过滤器，您可以看到更多新想法。一种方法是询问其他人探索什么是好想法。

sentences.en: Then your subconscious won't shoot them down to protect you.You could also discover overlooked ideas by working in the other direction: by starting from what's obscuring them.
sentences.zh: 这样你的潜意识就不会击落它们来保护你。你还可以通过朝另一个方向努力来发现被忽视的想法：从掩盖它们的东西开始。

sentences.en: Every cherished but mistaken principle is surrounded by a dead zone of valuable ideas that are unexplored because they contradict it.Religions are collections of cherished but mistaken principles.
sentences.zh: 每一个被珍视但错误的原则都被有价值的思想的死区所包围，这些思想因为与它相矛盾而未被探索。宗教是被珍视但错误的原则的集合。

sentences.en: So anything that can be described either literally or metaphorically as a religion will have valuable unexplored ideas in its shadow.
sentences.zh: 因此，任何可以从字面上或隐喻上描述为宗教的事物，都将在其阴影下蕴藏着有价值的、未经探索的思想。

sentences.en: Copernicus and Darwin both made discoveries of this type. [18]What are people in your field religious about, in the sense of being too attached to some principle that might not be as self-evident as they think?
sentences.zh: 哥白尼和达尔文都做出了此类发现。 [18]在你的领域里，人们对什么有宗教信仰，即过于执着于某些可能并不像他们想象的那么不言自明的原则？

sentences.en: What becomes possible if you discard it?
sentences.zh: 如果你放弃它，会发生什么？

sentences.en: People show much more originality in solving problems than in deciding which problems to solve.
sentences.zh: 人们在解决问题时比在决定解决哪些问题时表现出更多的独创性。

sentences.en: Even the smartest can be surprisingly conservative when deciding what to work on.
sentences.zh: 即使是最聪明的人在决定做什么时也会出人意料地保守。

sentences.en: People who'd never dream of being fashionable in any other way get sucked into working on fashionable problems.One reason people are more conservative when choosing problems than solutions is that problems are bigger bets.
sentences.zh: 那些从来没有梦想以任何其他方式变得时尚的人会沉迷于解决时尚问题。人们在选择问题而不是解决方案时更加保守的一个原因是，问题是更大的赌注。

sentences.en: A problem could occupy you for years, while exploring a solution might only take days.
sentences.zh: 一个问题可能会花费你数年的时间，而探索解决方案可能只需要几天的时间。

sentences.en: But even so I think most people are too conservative.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此我认为大多数人都过于保守。

sentences.en: They're not merely responding to risk, but to fashion as well.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅要应对风险，还要应对时尚。

sentences.en: Unfashionable problems are undervalued.One of the most interesting kinds of unfashionable problem is the problem that people think has been fully explored, but hasn't.
sentences.zh: 不合时宜的问题被低估了。最有趣的一类不合时宜的问题是人们认为已经得到充分探索但实际上还没有得到充分探索的问题。

sentences.en: Great work often takes something that already exists and shows its latent potential.
sentences.zh: 伟大的作品往往需要一些已经存在的东西并展示其潜在的潜力。

sentences.en: Durer and Watt both did this.
sentences.zh: 丢勒和瓦特都做到了这一点。

sentences.en: So if you're interested in a field that others think is tapped out, don't let their skepticism deter you.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你对别人认为已经开发出来的领域感兴趣，不要让他们的怀疑阻止你。

sentences.en: People are often wrong about this.Working on an unfashionable problem can be very pleasing.
sentences.zh: 人们在这一点上常常是错误的。解决一个不流行的问题可能会非常令人愉快。

sentences.en: There's no hype or hurry.
sentences.zh: 没有炒作或匆忙。

sentences.en: Opportunists and critics are both occupied elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 机会主义者和批评家都忙于别处。

sentences.en: The existing work often has an old-school solidity.
sentences.zh: 现有的作品通常具有老式的坚固性。

sentences.en: And there's a satisfying sense of economy in cultivating ideas that would otherwise be wasted.But the most common type of overlooked problem is not explicitly unfashionable in the sense of being out of fashion.
sentences.zh: 培养那些本来会被浪费的想法会带来一种令人满意的节约感。但最常见的被忽视的问题并不是从过时的意义上来说明显不流行。

sentences.en: It just doesn't seem to matter as much as it actually does.
sentences.zh: 它看起来并不像实际那么重要。

sentences.en: How do you find these?
sentences.zh: 你如何找到这些？

sentences.en: By being self-indulgent — by letting your curiosity have its way, and tuning out, at least temporarily, the little voice in your head that says you should only be working on "important" problems.You do need to work on important problems, but almost everyone is too conservative about what counts as one.
sentences.zh: 通过自我放纵——让你的好奇心发挥作用，至少暂时忽略你头脑中那个说你应该只研究“重要”问题的小声音。你确实需​​要研究重要的问题，但几乎每个人都对什么算作一个问题过于保守。

sentences.en: And if there's an important but overlooked problem in your neighborhood, it's probably already on your subconscious radar screen.
sentences.zh: 如果您的社区存在一个重要但被忽视的问题，它可能已经出现在您的潜意识雷达屏幕上。

sentences.en: So try asking yourself: if you were going to take a break from "serious" work to work on something just because it would be really interesting, what would you do?
sentences.zh: 所以试着问问自己：如果你打算从“严肃”的工作中休息一下，去做某件事，只是因为它真的很有趣，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: The answer is probably more important than it seems.Originality in choosing problems seems to matter even more than originality in solving them.
sentences.zh: 答案可能比看起来更重要。选择问题的独创性似乎比解决问题的独创性更重要。

sentences.en: That's what distinguishes the people who discover whole new fields.
sentences.zh: 这就是发现全新领域的人们的独特之处。

sentences.en: So what might seem to be merely the initial step — deciding what to work on — is in a sense the key to the whole game.
sentences.zh: 因此，看似只是第一步——决定做什么——在某种意义上是整个游戏的关键。

sentences.en: Few grasp this.
sentences.zh: 很少有人明白这一点。

sentences.en: One of the biggest misconceptions about new ideas is about the ratio of question to answer in their composition.
sentences.zh: 对新想法最大的误解之一是其作文中问题与答案的比例。

sentences.en: People think big ideas are answers, but often the real insight was in the question.Part of the reason we underrate questions is the way they're used in schools.
sentences.zh: 人们认为伟大的想法就是答案，但真正的洞察力往往存在于问题中。我们低估问题的部分原因是它们在学校中的使用方式。

sentences.en: In schools they tend to exist only briefly before being answered, like unstable particles.
sentences.zh: 在学校里，它们往往只存在很短的时间，然后就得到答案，就像不稳定的粒子一样。

sentences.en: But a really good question can be much more than that.
sentences.zh: 但一个真正好的问题可以远不止于此。

sentences.en: A really good question is a partial discovery.
sentences.zh: 一个真正好的问题是部分发现。

sentences.en: How do new species arise?
sentences.zh: 新物种是如何产生的？

sentences.en: Is the force that makes objects fall to earth the same as the one that keeps planets in their orbits?
sentences.zh: 使物体坠落地球的力与使行星保持在其轨道上的力相同吗？

sentences.en: By even asking such questions you were already in excitingly novel territory.Unanswered questions can be uncomfortable things to carry around with you.
sentences.zh: 通过提出这样的问题，您已经进入了令人兴奋的新领域。未回答的问题可能会让您感到不舒服。

sentences.en: But the more you're carrying, the greater the chance of noticing a solution — or perhaps even more excitingly, noticing that two unanswered questions are the same.Sometimes you carry a question for a long time.
sentences.zh: 但你承载的越多，注意到解决方案的机会就越大，或者更令人兴奋的是，注意到两个未回答的问题是相同的。有时，你会长时间承载一个问题。

sentences.en: Great work often comes from returning to a question you first noticed years before — in your childhood, even — and couldn't stop thinking about.
sentences.zh: 伟大的工作往往来自于回到你几年前第一次注意到的问题——甚至是在你的童年——并且无法停止思考。

sentences.en: People talk a lot about the importance of keeping your youthful dreams alive, but it's just as important to keep your youthful questions alive. [19]This is one of the places where actual expertise differs most from the popular picture of it.
sentences.zh: 人们经常谈论保持年轻时的梦想的重要性，但保持年轻时的问题也同样重要。 [19]这是实际专业知识与流行图片最不同的地方之一。

sentences.en: In the popular picture, experts are certain.
sentences.zh: 在流行的图景中，专家们是肯定的。

sentences.en: But actually the more puzzled you are, the better, so long as (a) the things you're puzzled about matter, and (b) no one else understands them either.Think about what's happening at the moment just before a new idea is discovered.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你越困惑越好，只要（a）你感到困惑的事情很重要，并且（b）其他人也没有理解它们。想想在发现新想法之前的那一刻发生了什么。

sentences.en: Often someone with sufficient expertise is puzzled about something.
sentences.zh: 具有足够专业知识的人常常会对某些事情感到困惑。

sentences.en: Which means that originality consists partly of puzzlement — of confusion!
sentences.zh: 这意味着原创性部分地包含着困惑——混乱！

sentences.en: You have to be comfortable enough with the world being full of puzzles that you're willing to see them, but not so comfortable that you don't want to solve them. [20]It's a great thing to be rich in unanswered questions.
sentences.zh: 你必须对这个充满谜题的世界感到足够舒服，以至于你愿意看到它们，但又不能太舒服以至于你不想解决它们。 [20]有大量未解答的问题是一件好事。

sentences.en: And this is one of those situations where the rich get richer, because the best way to acquire new questions is to try answering existing ones.
sentences.zh: 这是富人变得更富的情况之一，因为获得新问题的最佳方法是尝试回答现有问题。

sentences.en: Questions don't just lead to answers, but also to more questions.
sentences.zh: 问题不仅会带来答案，还会引发更多问题。

sentences.en: The best questions grow in the answering.
sentences.zh: 最好的问题在回答中成长。

sentences.en: You notice a thread protruding from the current paradigm and try pulling on it, and it just gets longer and longer.
sentences.zh: 你注意到一条线从当前的范式中伸出，并尝试拉动它，它只会变得越来越长。

sentences.en: So don't require a question to be obviously big before you try answering it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在尝试回答问题之前，不要要求问题明显很大。

sentences.en: You can rarely predict that.
sentences.zh: 你很少能预测到这一点。

sentences.en: It's hard enough even to notice the thread, let alone to predict how much will unravel if you pull on it.It's better to be promiscuously curious — to pull a little bit on a lot of threads, and see what happens.
sentences.zh: 甚至要注意到这条线都已经很困难了，更不用说预测如果你拉动它，它会散开多少。最好保持混杂的好奇心——在很多条线上拉一点，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Big things start small.
sentences.zh: 大事从小事做起。

sentences.en: The initial versions of big things were often just experiments, or side projects, or talks, which then grew into something bigger.
sentences.zh: 大事情的最初版本通常只是实验、副项目或谈话，然后发展成为更大的事情。

sentences.en: So start lots of small things.Being prolific is underrated.
sentences.zh: 所以要从很多小事做起。多产是被低估的。

sentences.en: The more different things you try, the greater the chance of discovering something new.
sentences.zh: 你尝试的不同事物越多，发现新事物的机会就越大。

sentences.en: Understand, though, that trying lots of things will mean trying lots of things that don't work.
sentences.zh: 但要明白，尝试很多事情就意味着尝试很多行不通的事情。

sentences.en: You can't have a lot of good ideas without also having a lot of bad ones. [21]Though it sounds more responsible to begin by studying everything that's been done before, you'll learn faster and have more fun by trying stuff.
sentences.zh: 你不可能在拥有很多好想法的同时也有很多坏想法。 [21]虽然从研究以前做过的所有事情开始听起来更负责任，但通过尝试你会学得更快并获得更多乐趣。

sentences.en: And you'll understand previous work better when you do look at it.
sentences.zh: 当你真正看到以前的作品时，你会更好地理解它。

sentences.en: So err on the side of starting.
sentences.zh: 所以最好还是开始吧。

sentences.en: Which is easier when starting means starting small; those two ideas fit together like two puzzle pieces.How do you get from starting small to doing something great?
sentences.zh: 当开始意味着从小事做起时，哪一个更容易？这两个想法就像两块拼图一样组合在一起。你如何从小事做起，成就伟大事业？

sentences.en: By making successive versions.
sentences.zh: 通过制作连续的版本。

sentences.en: Great things are almost always made in successive versions.
sentences.zh: 伟大的事物几乎总是由连续的版本制成的。

sentences.en: You start with something small and evolve it, and the final version is both cleverer and more ambitious than anything you could have planned.It's particularly useful to make successive versions when you're making something for people — to get an initial version in front of them quickly, and then evolve it based on their response.Begin by trying the simplest thing that could possibly work.
sentences.zh: 你从一些小东西开始，然后不断改进它，最终的版本比你计划的任何东西都更聪明、更雄心勃勃。当你为人们制作东西时，制作连续的版本特别有用——快速地在他们面前得到一个初始版本，然后根据他们的反应改进它。从尝试可能有效的最简单的事情开始。

sentences.en: Surprisingly often, it does.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，事实往往如此。

sentences.en: If it doesn't, this will at least get you started.Don't try to cram too much new stuff into any one version.
sentences.zh: 如果没有，这至少会让您入门。不要试图在任何一个版本中塞入太多新内容。

sentences.en: There are names for doing this with the first version (taking too long to ship) and the second (the second system effect), but these are both merely instances of a more general principle.An early version of a new project will sometimes be dismissed as a toy.
sentences.zh: 对于第一个版本（发布时间太长）和第二个版本（第二个系统效果）有一些名称，但这些都只是更一般原则的实例。新项目的早期版本有时会被视为玩具而被抛弃。

sentences.en: It's a good sign when people do this.
sentences.zh: 当人们这样做时，这是一个好兆头。

sentences.en: That means it has everything a new idea needs except scale, and that tends to follow. [22]The alternative to starting with something small and evolving it is to plan in advance what you're going to do.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它拥有新想法所需的一切，除了规模之外，而且规模往往会随之而来。 [22]从一些小事情开始并不断发展的另一种选择是提前计划你要做什么。

sentences.en: And planning does usually seem the more responsible choice.
sentences.zh: 规划通常看起来确实是更负责任的选择。

sentences.en: It sounds more organized to say "we're going to do x and then y and then z" than "we're going to try x and see what happens."
sentences.zh: 说“我们要做 x，然后是 y，然后是 z”，这听起来比“我们要尝试 x，看看会发生什么”更有条理。

sentences.en: And it is more organized; it just doesn't work as well.Planning per se isn't good.
sentences.zh: 而且更有组织性；它只是不太有效。计划本身并不好。

sentences.en: It's sometimes necessary, but it's a necessary evil — a response to unforgiving conditions.
sentences.zh: 有时这是必要的，但它是一种必要的罪恶——对无情条件的反应。

sentences.en: It's something you have to do because you're working with inflexible media, or because you need to coordinate the efforts of a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这是你必须做的事情，因为你正在与不灵活的媒体合作，或者因为你需要协调很多人的努力。

sentences.en: If you keep projects small and use flexible media, you don't have to plan as much, and your designs can evolve instead.
sentences.zh: 如果您保持项目较小并使用灵活的媒体，则无需进行太多计划，您的设计也可以不断发展。

sentences.en: Take as much risk as you can afford.
sentences.zh: 承担尽可能多的风险。

sentences.en: In an efficient market, risk is proportionate to reward, so don't look for certainty, but for a bet with high expected value.
sentences.zh: 在有效市场中，风险与回报成正比，因此不要寻求确定性，而要寻求具有高预期价值的赌注。

sentences.en: If you're not failing occasionally, you're probably being too conservative.Though conservatism is usually associated with the old, it's the young who tend to make this mistake.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是偶尔失败，那么你可能太保守了。虽然保守主义通常与老年人联系在一起，但年轻人往往会犯这个错误。

sentences.en: Inexperience makes them fear risk, but it's when you're young that you can afford the most.Even a project that fails can be valuable.
sentences.zh: 缺乏经验让他们害怕风险，但年轻的时候才是最能承担得起的。即使一个失败的项目也可能很有价值。

sentences.en: In the process of working on it, you'll have crossed territory few others have seen, and encountered questions few others have asked.
sentences.zh: 在研究的过程中，你会跨越很少有人见过的领域，并遇到很少有人问过的问题。

sentences.en: And there's probably no better source of questions than the ones you encounter in trying to do something slightly too hard.
sentences.zh: 可能没有比你在尝试做稍微困难的事情时遇到的问题更好的来源了。

sentences.en: Use the advantages of youth when you have them, and the advantages of age once you have those.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有年轻的优势时，就利用它；当你拥有这些优势时，就利用年龄的优势。

sentences.en: The advantages of youth are energy, time, optimism, and freedom.
sentences.zh: 年轻的优势是精力、时间、乐观、自由。

sentences.en: The advantages of age are knowledge, efficiency, money, and power.
sentences.zh: 年龄的优势是知识、效率、金钱和权力。

sentences.en: With effort you can acquire some of the latter when young and keep some of the former when old.The old also have the advantage of knowing which advantages they have.
sentences.zh: 通过努力，你可以在年轻时获得后者的一些，并在年老时保留前者的一些。老年人的优势还在于知道自己拥有哪些优势。

sentences.en: The young often have them without realizing it.
sentences.zh: 年轻人常常在没有意识到的情况下拥有它们。

sentences.en: The biggest is probably time.
sentences.zh: 最大的可能是时间。

sentences.en: The young have no idea how rich they are in time.
sentences.zh: 年轻人不知道自己的时间有多丰富。

sentences.en: The best way to turn this time to advantage is to use it in slightly frivolous ways: to learn about something you don't need to know about, just out of curiosity, or to try building something just because it would be cool, or to become freakishly good at something.That "slightly" is an important qualification.
sentences.zh: 把这段时间变成优势的最好方法是以稍微无聊的方式来利用它：出于好奇而学习一些你不需要知道的东西，或者仅仅因为它很酷而尝试构建一些东西，或者变得异常擅长某件事。这个“稍微”是一个重要的资格。

sentences.en: Spend time lavishly when you're young, but don't simply waste it.
sentences.zh: 年轻时要大肆挥霍时间，但不要简单地浪费它。

sentences.en: There's a big difference between doing something you worry might be a waste of time and doing something you know for sure will be.
sentences.zh: 做一些你担心可能会浪费时间的事情和做一些你肯定会浪费时间的事情之间有很大的区别。

sentences.en: The former is at least a bet, and possibly a better one than you think. [23]The most subtle advantage of youth, or more precisely of inexperience, is that you're seeing everything with fresh eyes.
sentences.zh: 前者至少是一个赌注，而且可能比你想象的更好。 [23]年轻的最微妙的优势，或者更准确地说，缺乏经验的优势，是你能用新鲜的眼光看待一切。

sentences.en: When your brain embraces an idea for the first time, sometimes the two don't fit together perfectly.
sentences.zh: 当你的大脑第一次接受一个想法时，有时两者并不完美地结合在一起。

sentences.en: Usually the problem is with your brain, but occasionally it's with the idea.
sentences.zh: 通常问题出在你的大脑上，但有时问题出在想法上。

sentences.en: A piece of it sticks out awkwardly and jabs you when you think about it.
sentences.zh: 当你想到它时，它的一块笨拙地伸出来并刺伤你。

sentences.en: People who are used to the idea have learned to ignore it, but you have the opportunity not to. [24]So when you're learning about something for the first time, pay attention to things that seem wrong or missing.
sentences.zh: 习惯了这个想法的人已经学会了忽视它，但你有机会不这样做。 [24]因此，当您第一次学习某些东西时，请注意那些看似错误或缺失的内容。

sentences.en: You'll be tempted to ignore them, since there's a 99% chance the problem is with you.
sentences.zh: 您可能会想忽略它们，因为 99% 的可能性问题出在您身上。

sentences.en: And you may have to set aside your misgivings temporarily to keep progressing.
sentences.zh: 你可能必须暂时放下疑虑才能继续进步。

sentences.en: But don't forget about them.
sentences.zh: 但不要忘记他们。

sentences.en: When you've gotten further into the subject, come back and check if they're still there.
sentences.zh: 当您进一步了解该主题后，请回来检查它们是否仍然存在。
