sentences.en: If they're still viable in the light of your present knowledge, they probably represent an undiscovered idea.
sentences.zh: 如果根据您目前的知识它们仍然可行，那么它们可能代表了一个未被发现的想法。

sentences.en: One of the most valuable kinds of knowledge you get from experience is to know what you don't have to worry about.
sentences.zh: 从经验中获得的最有价值的知识之一就是知道什么是你不必担心的。

sentences.en: The young know all the things that could matter, but not their relative importance.
sentences.zh: 年轻人知道所有可能重要的事情，但不知道它们的相对重要性。

sentences.en: So they worry equally about everything, when they should worry much more about a few things and hardly at all about the rest.But what you don't know is only half the problem with inexperience.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们对所有事情都同样担心，而实际上，他们应该更多地担心几件事，而几乎不关心其他事情。但是，你不知道的只是缺乏经验问题的一半。

sentences.en: The other half is what you do know that ain't so.
sentences.zh: 另一半是你所知道的，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: You arrive at adulthood with your head full of nonsense — bad habits you've acquired and false things you've been taught — and you won't be able to do great work till you clear away at least the nonsense in the way of whatever type of work you want to do.Much of the nonsense left in your head is left there by schools.
sentences.zh: 当你成年时，你的脑子里充满了废话——你养成的坏习惯和你被教导的错误的东西——你将无法做出伟大的工作，除非你至少清除了你想做的任何类型工作中的废话。你脑子里留下的大部分废话都是学校留下的。

sentences.en: We're so used to schools that we unconsciously treat going to school as identical with learning, but in fact schools have all sorts of strange qualities that warp our ideas about learning and thinking.For example, schools induce passivity.
sentences.zh: 我们已经习惯了学校，以至于不知不觉中把上学和学习等同起来，但事实上，学校有各种奇怪的品质，扭曲着我们的学习和思维观念。例如，学校会导致被动性。

sentences.en: Since you were a small child, there was an authority at the front of the class telling all of you what you had to learn and then measuring whether you did.
sentences.zh: 因为你还是个小孩子，所以班级前面有一位权威告诉你们所有人必须学习什么，然后衡量你们是否做到了。

sentences.en: But neither classes nor tests are intrinsic to learning; they're just artifacts of the way schools are usually designed.The sooner you overcome this passivity, the better.
sentences.zh: 但课程和考试都不是学习的本质；它们都不是学习的本质。它们只是学校通常设计方式的产物。越早克服这种被动性越好。

sentences.en: If you're still in school, try thinking of your education as your project, and your teachers as working for you rather than vice versa.
sentences.zh: 如果您还在上学，请尝试将您的教育视为您的项目，并将您的老师视为为您工作，而不是反之亦然。

sentences.en: That may seem a stretch, but it's not merely some weird thought experiment.
sentences.zh: 这似乎有点夸张，但这不仅仅是一些奇怪的思想实验。

sentences.en: It's the truth economically, and in the best case it's the truth intellectually as well.
sentences.zh: 这在经济上是真理，在最好的情况下，在智力上也是真理。

sentences.en: The best teachers don't want to be your bosses.
sentences.zh: 最好的老师不想成为你的老板。

sentences.en: They'd prefer it if you pushed ahead, using them as a source of advice, rather than being pulled by them through the material.Schools also give you a misleading impression of what work is like.
sentences.zh: 如果你继续前进，将他们作为建议的来源，而不是被他们通过材料拉动，他们会更喜欢你。学校也会给你一种关于工作是什么样子的误导性印象。

sentences.en: In school they tell you what the problems are, and they're almost always soluble using no more than you've been taught so far.
sentences.zh: 在学校里，他们会告诉你问题是什么，而且这些问题几乎总是可以用你目前所学的内容来解决。

sentences.en: In real life you have to figure out what the problems are, and you often don't know if they're soluble at all.But perhaps the worst thing schools do to you is train you to win by hacking the test.
sentences.zh: 在现实生活中，你必须弄清楚问题是什么，而且你常常不知道它们是否可以解决。但也许学校对你做的最糟糕的事情就是训练你通过破解考试来获胜。

sentences.en: You can't do great work by doing that.
sentences.zh: 这样做你不可能做出伟大的工作。

sentences.en: You can't trick God.
sentences.zh: 你无法欺骗上帝。

sentences.en: So stop looking for that kind of shortcut.
sentences.zh: 所以不要再寻找那种捷径了。

sentences.en: The way to beat the system is to focus on problems and solutions that others have overlooked, not to skimp on the work itself.
sentences.zh: 击败系统的方法是专注于其他人忽视的问题和解决方案，而不是吝啬于工作本身。

sentences.en: Don't think of yourself as dependent on some gatekeeper giving you a "big break."
sentences.zh: 不要认为自己依赖某个看门人给你“大突破”。

sentences.en: Even if this were true, the best way to get it would be to focus on doing good work rather than chasing influential people.And don't take rejection by committees to heart.
sentences.zh: 即使这是真的，实现这一目标的最佳方法是专注于做好工作，而不是追逐有影响力的人。并且不要将委员会的拒绝放在心上。

sentences.en: The qualities that impress admissions officers and prize committees are quite different from those required to do great work.
sentences.zh: 给招生官员和评奖委员会留下深刻印象的品质与出色工作所需的品质有很大不同。

sentences.en: The decisions of selection committees are only meaningful to the extent that they're part of a feedback loop, and very few are.
sentences.zh: 选拔委员会的决定只有在它们成为反馈循环的一部分时才有意义，而很少有这样的决定。

sentences.en: People new to a field will often copy existing work.
sentences.zh: 刚接触某个领域的人经常会抄袭现有的作品。

sentences.en: There's nothing inherently bad about that.
sentences.zh: 这本身并没有什么坏处。

sentences.en: There's no better way to learn how something works than by trying to reproduce it.
sentences.zh: 要了解某事物是如何工作的，没有比尝试重现它更好的方法了。

sentences.en: Nor does copying necessarily make your work unoriginal.
sentences.zh: 抄袭也不一定会使你的作品失去原创性。

sentences.en: Originality is the presence of new ideas, not the absence of old ones.There's a good way to copy and a bad way.
sentences.zh: 原创性是新想法的存在，而不是旧想法的缺失。复制有好的方法，也有坏的方法。

sentences.en: If you're going to copy something, do it openly instead of furtively, or worse still, unconsciously.
sentences.zh: 如果你要复制某些东西，请公开地进行，而不是偷偷地进行，或者更糟糕的是，无意识地进行。

sentences.en: This is what's meant by the famously misattributed phrase "Great artists steal."
sentences.zh: 这就是著名的错误说法“伟大的艺术家偷窃”的含义。

sentences.en: The really dangerous kind of copying, the kind that gives copying a bad name, is the kind that's done without realizing it, because you're nothing more than a train running on tracks laid down by someone else.
sentences.zh: 真正危险的抄袭，也就是给抄袭带来坏名声的抄袭，是在没有意识到的情况下进行的，因为你只不过是一列在别人铺设的轨道上行驶的火车。

sentences.en: But at the other extreme, copying can be a sign of superiority rather than subordination. [25]In many fields it's almost inevitable that your early work will be in some sense based on other people's.
sentences.zh: 但在另一个极端，抄袭可能是优越而非从属的标志。 [25]在许多领域，你的早期工作在某种意义上几乎不可避免地基于其他人的工作。

sentences.en: Projects rarely arise in a vacuum.
sentences.zh: 项目很少是凭空出现的。

sentences.en: They're usually a reaction to previous work.
sentences.zh: 它们通常是对以前工作的反应。

sentences.en: When you're first starting out, you don't have any previous work; if you're going to react to something, it has to be someone else's.
sentences.zh: 当你刚开始工作时，你之前没有任何工作；如果你要对某件事做出反应，那它必须是别人的。

sentences.en: Once you're established, you can react to your own.
sentences.zh: 一旦你确定了，你就可以对自己的反应做出反应。

sentences.en: But while the former gets called derivative and the latter doesn't, structurally the two cases are more similar than they seem.Oddly enough, the very novelty of the most novel ideas sometimes makes them seem at first to be more derivative than they are.
sentences.zh: 但是，虽然前者被称为衍生性的，而后者则不然，从结构上来说，这两种情况比看起来更相似。奇怪的是，最新颖的想法的新颖性有时会让它们乍一看比实际情况更衍生。

sentences.en: New discoveries often have to be conceived initially as variations of existing things, even by their discoverers, because there isn't yet the conceptual vocabulary to express them.There are definitely some dangers to copying, though.
sentences.zh: 新发现通常必须最初被设想为现有事物的变体，即使是它们的发现者，因为还没有表达它们的概念词汇。不过，复制肯定存在一些危险。

sentences.en: One is that you'll tend to copy old things — things that were in their day at the frontier of knowledge, but no longer are.And when you do copy something, don't copy every feature of it.
sentences.zh: 一是你会倾向于复制旧的东西——那些当时处于知识前沿的东西，但现在已经不再是了。当你确实复制某些东西时，不要复制它的每一个特征。

sentences.en: Some will make you ridiculous if you do.
sentences.zh: 如果你这样做，有些人会让你感到可笑。

sentences.en: Don't copy the manner of an eminent 50 year old professor if you're 18, for example, or the idiom of a Renaissance poem hundreds of years later.Some of the features of things you admire are flaws they succeeded despite.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你才 18 岁，就不要模仿 50 岁的著名教授的举止，或者数百年后文艺复兴时期诗歌的习语。你所欣赏的事物的某些特征是它们尽管存在缺陷却取得了成功。

sentences.en: Indeed, the features that are easiest to imitate are the most likely to be the flaws.This is particularly true for behavior.
sentences.zh: 事实上，最容易模仿的特征最有可能是缺陷。对于行为来说尤其如此。

sentences.en: Some talented people are jerks, and this sometimes makes it seem to the inexperienced that being a jerk is part of being talented.
sentences.zh: 有些有才华的人是混蛋，这有时会让没有经验的人觉得混蛋也是有才华的一部分。

sentences.en: It isn't; being talented is merely how they get away with it.One of the most powerful kinds of copying is to copy something from one field into another.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此；最有力的复制方式之一就是将某些东西从一个领域复制到另一个领域。

sentences.en: History is so full of chance discoveries of this type that it's probably worth giving chance a hand by deliberately learning about other kinds of work.
sentences.zh: 历史上充满了这种类型的偶然发现，因此可能值得通过刻意学习其他类型的工作来帮助机会。

sentences.en: You can take ideas from quite distant fields if you let them be metaphors.Negative examples can be as inspiring as positive ones.
sentences.zh: 如果你让它们成为隐喻，你就可以从相当遥远的领域获取想法。负面例子可以像正面例子一样鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: In fact you can sometimes learn more from things done badly than from things done well; sometimes it only becomes clear what's needed when it's missing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有时你可以从做得不好的事情中学到比做得好的事情更多的东西；有时只有当缺少什么时才清楚需要什么。

sentences.en: If a lot of the best people in your field are collected in one place, it's usually a good idea to visit for a while.
sentences.zh: 如果你所在领域的许多最优秀的人都聚集在一个地方，那么参观一段时间通常是个好主意。

sentences.en: It will increase your ambition, and also, by showing you that these people are human, increase your self-confidence. [26]If you're earnest you'll probably get a warmer welcome than you might expect.
sentences.zh: 它会增加你的野心，并且通过向你展示这些人是人，增加你的自信心。 [26]如果你很认真，你可能会受到比你想象的更热烈的欢迎。

sentences.en: Most people who are very good at something are happy to talk about it with anyone who's genuinely interested.
sentences.zh: 大多数非常擅长某件事的人都乐意与任何真正感兴趣的人谈论它。

sentences.en: If they're really good at their work, then they probably have a hobbyist's interest in it, and hobbyists always want to talk about their hobbies.It may take some effort to find the people who are really good, though.
sentences.zh: 如果他们真的很擅长自己的工作，那么他们可能会有业余爱好者的兴趣，而业余爱好者总是想谈论他们的爱好。不过，可能需要付出一些努力才能找到真正擅长的人。

sentences.en: Doing great work has such prestige that in some places, particularly universities, there's a polite fiction that everyone is engaged in it.
sentences.zh: 出色的工作具有很高的声望，以至于在某些地方，特别是大学，有一种礼貌的说法，认为每个人都在从事这项工作。

sentences.en: And that is far from true.
sentences.zh: 但这远非事实。

sentences.en: People within universities can't say so openly, but the quality of the work being done in different departments varies immensely.
sentences.zh: 大学内部的人不能公开这么说，但不同部门所做工作的质量差异很大。

sentences.en: Some departments have people doing great work; others have in the past; others never have.
sentences.zh: 有些部门的员工工作出色，有些部门的员工工作表现出色；其他人过去曾有过；其他人从来没有。

sentences.en: Seek out the best colleagues.
sentences.zh: 寻找最好的同事。

sentences.en: There are a lot of projects that can't be done alone, and even if you're working on one that can be, it's good to have other people to encourage you and to bounce ideas off.Colleagues don't just affect your work, though; they also affect you.
sentences.zh: 有很多项目是无法独自完成的，即使您正在从事一个可以完成的项目，有其他人鼓励您并交换想法也是件好事。不过，同事不仅会影响您的工作，还会影响您的工作。他们也会影响你。

sentences.en: So work with people you want to become like, because you will.Quality is more important than quantity in colleagues.
sentences.zh: 因此，与你想成为的人一起工作，因为你会的。同事的质量比数量更重要。

sentences.en: It's better to have one or two great ones than a building full of pretty good ones.
sentences.zh: 拥有一两个优秀的人比拥有一栋充满相当好的人的建筑要好。

sentences.en: In fact it's not merely better, but necessary, judging from history: the degree to which great work happens in clusters suggests that one's colleagues often make the difference between doing great work and not.How do you know when you have sufficiently good colleagues?
sentences.zh: 事实上，从历史来看，这不仅更好，而且是必要的：伟大工作在集群中发生的程度表明，一个人的同事往往会决定是否做好工作。你怎么知道你的同事是否足够好？

sentences.en: In my experience, when you do, you know.
sentences.zh: 根据我的经验，当你这样做时，你就知道了。

sentences.en: Which means if you're unsure, you probably don't.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果您不确定，您可能就不确定。

sentences.en: But it may be possible to give a more concrete answer than that.
sentences.zh: 但也许可以给出比这更具体的答案。

sentences.en: Here's an attempt: sufficiently good colleagues offer surprising insights.
sentences.zh: 这是一种尝试：足够优秀的同事提供令人惊讶的见解。

sentences.en: They can see and do things that you can't.
sentences.zh: 他们可以看到并做你看不到的事情。

sentences.en: So if you have a handful of colleagues good enough to keep you on your toes in this sense, you're probably over the threshold.Most of us can benefit from collaborating with colleagues, but some projects require people on a larger scale, and starting one of those is not for everyone.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你有几个足够好的同事让你在这个意义上保持警惕，那么你可能已经跨过了门槛。我们大多数人都可以从与同事的合作中受益，但有些项目需要更大规模的人员，而启动其中一个项目并不适合所有人。

sentences.en: If you want to run a project like that, you'll have to become a manager, and managing well takes aptitude and interest like any other kind of work.
sentences.zh: 如果你想管理这样的项目，你就必须成为一名经理，而像任何其他类型的工作一样，良好的管理需要天赋和兴趣。

sentences.en: If you don't have them, there is no middle path: you must either force yourself to learn management as a second language, or avoid such projects. [27] Husband your morale.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有它们，就没有中间道路：你必须强迫自己学习管理作为第二语言，或者避免此类项目。 [27] 丈夫你的士气。

sentences.en: It's the basis of everything when you're working on ambitious projects.
sentences.zh: 当您从事雄心勃勃的项目时，它是一切的基础。

sentences.en: You have to nurture and protect it like a living organism.Morale starts with your view of life.
sentences.zh: 你必须像一个活的有机体一样培育和保护它。士气始于你的人生观。

sentences.en: You're more likely to do great work if you're an optimist, and more likely to if you think of yourself as lucky than if you think of yourself as a victim.Indeed, work can to some extent protect you from your problems.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个乐观主义者，你更有可能做出出色的工作；如果你认为自己很幸运，那么你更有可能做得很好，而不是认为自己是受害者。事实上，工作可以在某种程度上保护你免受问题的困扰。

sentences.en: If you choose work that's pure, its very difficulties will serve as a refuge from the difficulties of everyday life.
sentences.zh: 如果你选择纯粹的工作，它的困难就会成为你逃避日常生活困难的避难所。

sentences.en: If this is escapism, it's a very productive form of it, and one that has been used by some of the greatest minds in history.Morale compounds via work: high morale helps you do good work, which increases your morale and helps you do even better work.
sentences.zh: 如果这就是逃避现实，那么它就是一种非常富有成效的形式，历史上一些最伟大的思想家都曾使用过这种形式。通过工作提高士气：高昂的士气可以帮助你做好工作，从而提高你的士气并帮助你做得更好。

sentences.en: But this cycle also operates in the other direction: if you're not doing good work, that can demoralize you and make it even harder to.
sentences.zh: 但这个循环也会向另一个方向运作：如果你没有做好工作，这会让你士气低落，让工作变得更加困难。

sentences.en: Since it matters so much for this cycle to be running in the right direction, it can be a good idea to switch to easier work when you're stuck, just so you start to get something done.One of the biggest mistakes ambitious people make is to allow setbacks to destroy their morale all at once, like a balloon bursting.
sentences.zh: 由于这个循环朝着正确的方向运行非常重要，因此当你陷入困境时，转向更轻松的工作可能是一个好主意，这样你就可以开始完成某件事。雄心勃勃的人犯的最大错误之一就是让挫折一下子摧毁他们的士气，就像气球爆炸一样。

sentences.en: You can inoculate yourself against this by explicitly considering setbacks a part of your process.
sentences.zh: 您可以通过明确地将挫折视为流程的一部分来使自己免受这种影响。

sentences.en: Solving hard problems always involves some backtracking.Doing great work is a depth-first search whose root node is the desire to.
sentences.zh: 解决难题总是涉及一些回溯。伟大的工作是深度优先搜索，其根节点是愿望。

sentences.en: So "If at first you don't succeed, try, try again" isn't quite right.
sentences.zh: 所以“如果一开始你没有成功，就尝试，再尝试”并不完全正确。

sentences.en: It should be: If at first you don't succeed, either try again, or backtrack and then try again."Never give up" is also not quite right.
sentences.zh: 应该是：如果一开始没有成功，要么再试一次，要么原路返回，然后再试一次。“永不放弃”也不太正确。

sentences.en: Obviously there are times when it's the right choice to eject.
sentences.zh: 显然，有时候弹出是正确的选择。

sentences.en: A more precise version would be: Never let setbacks panic you into backtracking more than you need to.
sentences.zh: 更精确的版本是：永远不要让挫折让你惊慌失措，让你回溯到不必要的程度。

sentences.en: Corollary: Never abandon the root node.It's not necessarily a bad sign if work is a struggle, any more than it's a bad sign to be out of breath while running.
sentences.zh: 推论：永远不要放弃根节点。如果工作是一场斗争，这并不一定是一个坏兆头，就像跑步时气喘吁吁并不是一个坏兆头一样。

sentences.en: It depends how fast you're running.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你跑得有多快。

sentences.en: So learn to distinguish good pain from bad.
sentences.zh: 所以要学会区分好的疼痛和坏的疼痛。

sentences.en: Good pain is a sign of effort; bad pain is a sign of damage.
sentences.zh: 好的疼痛是努力的标志；好的疼痛是努力的标志。剧烈的疼痛是损伤的迹象。

sentences.en: An audience is a critical component of morale.
sentences.zh: 观众是士气的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: If you're a scholar, your audience may be your peers; in the arts, it may be an audience in the traditional sense.
sentences.zh: 如果你是学者，你的听众可能是你的同行；在艺术上，可能是传统意义上的观众。

sentences.en: Either way it doesn't need to be big.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，它不需要很大。

sentences.en: The value of an audience doesn't grow anything like linearly with its size.
sentences.zh: 观众的价值不会随着其规模的增长而线性增长。

sentences.en: Which is bad news if you're famous, but good news if you're just starting out, because it means a small but dedicated audience can be enough to sustain you.
sentences.zh: 如果你很有名，这就是个坏消息，但如果你刚刚起步，这就是个好消息，因为这意味着少量但专注的观众足以支撑你。

sentences.en: If a handful of people genuinely love what you're doing, that's enough.To the extent you can, avoid letting intermediaries come between you and your audience.
sentences.zh: 如果少数人真正喜欢你正在做的事情，那就足够了。尽可能避免让中间人介入你和你的受众之间。

sentences.en: In some types of work this is inevitable, but it's so liberating to escape it that you might be better off switching to an adjacent type if that will let you go direct. [28]The people you spend time with will also have a big effect on your morale.
sentences.zh: 在某些类型的工作中，这是不可避免的，但逃避它是如此自由，如果可以让你直接进行，你最好切换到相邻的类型。 [28]与你共度时光的人也会对你的士气产生很大影响。

sentences.en: You'll find there are some who increase your energy and others who decrease it, and the effect someone has is not always what you'd expect.
sentences.zh: 你会发现有些人会增加你的能量，有些人会减少你的能量，而有些人所产生的效果并不总是你所期望的。

sentences.en: Seek out the people who increase your energy and avoid those who decrease it.
sentences.zh: 寻找那些能增加你能量的人，避开那些减少你能量的人。

sentences.en: Though of course if there's someone you need to take care of, that takes precedence.Don't marry someone who doesn't understand that you need to work, or sees your work as competition for your attention.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果有人需要你照顾，那就优先。不要嫁给一个不明白你需要工作，或者认为你的工作是对你注意力的竞争的人。

sentences.en: If you're ambitious, you need to work; it's almost like a medical condition; so someone who won't let you work either doesn't understand you, or does and doesn't care.Ultimately morale is physical.
sentences.zh: 如果你有野心，你需要努力；这几乎就像一种健康状况；所以不让你工作的人要么不理解你，要么关心但不在乎。归根结底，士气是物质的。

sentences.en: You think with your body, so it's important to take care of it.
sentences.zh: 你用你的身体思考，所以照顾好它很重要。

sentences.en: That means exercising regularly, eating and sleeping well, and avoiding the more dangerous kinds of drugs.
sentences.zh: 这意味着定期锻炼、良好饮食和睡眠，并避免使用更危险的药物。

sentences.en: Running and walking are particularly good forms of exercise because they're good for thinking. [29]People who do great work are not necessarily happier than everyone else, but they're happier than they'd be if they didn't.
sentences.zh: 跑步和步行是特别好的锻炼方式，因为它们有利于思考。 [29]工作出色的人不一定比其他人更快乐，但他们比不工作时更快乐。

sentences.en: In fact, if you're smart and ambitious, it's dangerous not to be productive.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你聪明又雄心勃勃，那么不高效就会很危险。

sentences.en: People who are smart and ambitious but don't achieve much tend to become bitter.
sentences.zh: 聪明而有野心但没有取得多大成就的人往往会变得痛苦。

sentences.en: It's ok to want to impress other people, but choose the right people.
sentences.zh: 想给别人留下深刻印象是可以的，但要选择合适的人。

sentences.en: The opinion of people you respect is signal.
sentences.zh: 你尊重的人的意见是信号。

sentences.en: Fame, which is the opinion of a much larger group you might or might not respect, just adds noise.The prestige of a type of work is at best a trailing indicator and sometimes completely mistaken.
sentences.zh: 名声是一个更大的群体的意见，你可能尊重也可能不尊重，只会增加噪音。一种工作的声望充其量只是一个跟踪指标，有时甚至是完全错误的。

sentences.en: If you do anything well enough, you'll make it prestigious.
sentences.zh: 如果你把一件事做得足够好，你就会让它享有声望。

sentences.en: So the question to ask about a type of work is not how much prestige it has, but how well it could be done.Competition can be an effective motivator, but don't let it choose the problem for you; don't let yourself get drawn into chasing something just because others are.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于一类工作，要问的问题不是它有多少声望，而是它能做得多好。竞争可以是一种有效的激励因素，但不要让它为你选择问题；竞争可以是一种有效的激励因素。不要因为别人追逐某样东西而让自己陷入其中。

sentences.en: In fact, don't let competitors make you do anything much more specific than work harder.Curiosity is the best guide.
sentences.zh: 事实上，不要让竞争对手让你做任何比更加努力工作更具体的事情。好奇心是最好的向导。

sentences.en: Your curiosity never lies, and it knows more than you do about what's worth paying attention to.
sentences.zh: 你的好奇心永远不会说谎，它比你更了解什么是值得关注的。

sentences.en: Notice how often that word has come up.
sentences.zh: 请注意这个词出现的频率。

sentences.en: If you asked an oracle the secret to doing great work and the oracle replied with a single word, my bet would be on "curiosity."That doesn't translate directly to advice.
sentences.zh: 如果你向神谕询问完成伟大工作的秘诀，而神谕只回答了一个词，我的赌注就是“好奇心”。这并不能直接转化为建议。

sentences.en: It's not enough just to be curious, and you can't command curiosity anyway.
sentences.zh: 仅仅有好奇心是不够的，而且你无论如何也无法控制好奇心。

sentences.en: But you can nurture it and let it drive you.Curiosity is the key to all four steps in doing great work: it will choose the field for you, get you to the frontier, cause you to notice the gaps in it, and drive you to explore them.
sentences.zh: 但你可以培养它并让它驱动你。好奇心是完成伟大工作的所有四个步骤的关键：它会为你选择领域，带你到达前沿，让你注意到其中的差距，并驱使你探索它们。

sentences.en: The whole process is a kind of dance with curiosity.
sentences.zh: 整个过程就像是一种好奇心的舞蹈。

sentences.en: Believe it or not, I tried to make this essay as short as I could.
sentences.zh: 不管你相信与否，我试图让这篇文章尽可能简短。

sentences.en: But its length at least means it acts as a filter.
sentences.zh: 但它的长度至少意味着它可以起到过滤器的作用。

sentences.en: If you made it this far, you must be interested in doing great work.
sentences.zh: 如果你做到了这一步，你一定有兴趣去做伟大的工作。

sentences.en: And if so you're already further along than you might realize, because the set of people willing to want to is small.The factors in doing great work are factors in the literal, mathematical sense, and they are: ability, interest, effort, and luck.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，那么你已经比你意识到的走得更远了，因为愿意这样做的人很少。 做出伟大工作的因素是字面和数学意义上的因素，它们是：能力、兴趣、努力和运气。

sentences.en: Luck by definition you can't do anything about, so we can ignore that.
sentences.zh: 运气的定义是你无能为力，所以我们可以忽略它。

sentences.en: And we can assume effort, if you do in fact want to do great work.
sentences.zh: 如果你确实想做好工作，我们可以假设你付出了努力。

sentences.en: So the problem boils down to ability and interest.
sentences.zh: 所以问题归结为能力和兴趣。

sentences.en: Can you find a kind of work where your ability and interest will combine to yield an explosion of new ideas?Here there are grounds for optimism.
sentences.zh: 你能找到一种工作，让你的能力和兴趣结合起来，产生大量的新想法吗？这里有理由乐观。

sentences.en: There are so many different ways to do great work, and even more that are still undiscovered.
sentences.zh: 完成伟大工作的方法有很多，甚至还有更多尚未被发现。

sentences.en: Out of all those different types of work, the one you're most suited for is probably a pretty close match.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些不同类型的工作中，您最适合的工作可能是非常接近的。

sentences.en: Probably a comically close match.
sentences.zh: 可能是一场滑稽的势均力敌的比赛。

sentences.en: It's just a question of finding it, and how far into it your ability and interest can take you.
sentences.zh: 问题只是找到它，以及你的能力和兴趣能带你走多远。

sentences.en: And you can only answer that by trying.Many more people could try to do great work than do.
sentences.zh: 你只能通过尝试来回答这个问题。尝试去做伟大工作的人比实际做的人多得多。

sentences.en: What holds them back is a combination of modesty and fear.
sentences.zh: 阻碍他们的是谦虚和恐惧的结合。

sentences.en: It seems presumptuous to try to be Newton or Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 试图成为牛顿或莎士比亚似乎是自以为是。

sentences.en: It also seems hard; surely if you tried something like that, you'd fail.
sentences.zh: 看起来也很难；当然，如果你尝试这样的事情，你就会失败。

sentences.en: Presumably the calculation is rarely explicit.
sentences.zh: 据推测，计算很少是明确的。

sentences.en: Few people consciously decide not to try to do great work.
sentences.zh: 很少有人有意识地决定不尝试去做伟大的工作。

sentences.en: But that's what's going on subconsciously; they shy away from the question.So I'm going to pull a sneaky trick on you.
sentences.zh: 但这就是潜意识里发生的事情；他们回避这个问题。所以我要对你耍个鬼把戏。

sentences.en: Do you want to do great work, or not?
sentences.zh: 你想做出伟大的工作吗？

sentences.en: Now you have to decide consciously.
sentences.zh: 现在你必须有意识地做出决定。

sentences.en: Sorry about that.
sentences.zh: 对此感到抱歉。

sentences.en: I wouldn't have done it to a general audience.
sentences.zh: 我不会对普通观众这样做。

sentences.en: But we already know you're interested.Don't worry about being presumptuous.
sentences.zh: 但我们已经知道您感兴趣。不必担心自以为是。

sentences.en: You don't have to tell anyone.
sentences.zh: 你不必告诉任何人。

sentences.en: And if it's too hard and you fail, so what?
sentences.zh: 如果太难而你失败了，那又怎样？

sentences.en: Lots of people have worse problems than that.
sentences.zh: 很多人都有比这更严重的问题。

sentences.en: In fact you'll be lucky if it's the worst problem you have.Yes, you'll have to work hard.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果这是你遇到的最糟糕的问题，你会很幸运。是的，你必须努力工作。

sentences.en: But again, lots of people have to work hard.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，很多人都必须努力工作。

sentences.en: And if you're working on something you find very interesting, which you necessarily will if you're on the right path, the work will probably feel less burdensome than a lot of your peers'.The discoveries are out there, waiting to be made.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在做一些你觉得非常有趣的事情（如果你走在正确的道路上，你必然会这样做），那么这项工作可能会比你的许多同行感觉更轻松。发现就在那里，等待着被发现。

sentences.en: Why not by you?
sentences.zh: 为什么不由你呢？

sentences.en: Notes[1] I don't think you could give a precise definition of what counts as great work.
sentences.zh: 注释[1] 我认为您无法对什么是伟大的工作给出准确的定义。

sentences.en: Doing great work means doing something important so well that you expand people's ideas of what's possible.
sentences.zh: 出色的工作意味着将重要的事情做得很好，从而扩展人们对可能性的想法。

sentences.en: But there's no threshold for importance.
sentences.zh: 但重要性没有门槛。

sentences.en: It's a matter of degree, and often hard to judge at the time anyway.
sentences.zh: 这是一个程度问题，而且当时通常很难判断。

sentences.en: So I'd rather people focused on developing their interests rather than worrying about whether they're important or not.
sentences.zh: 所以我宁愿人们专注于发展自己的兴趣，而不是担心它们是否重要。

sentences.en: Just try to do something amazing, and leave it to future generations to say if you succeeded.[2] A lot of standup comedy is based on noticing anomalies in everyday life.
sentences.zh: 尝试做一些令人惊奇的事情，并让后代来判断你是否成功。[2]许多单口喜剧都是基于注意到日常生活中的异常现象。

sentences.en: "Did you ever notice...?"
sentences.zh: “你有没有注意到……？”

sentences.en: New ideas come from doing this about nontrivial things.
sentences.zh: 新的想法来自于对不平凡的事情这样做。

sentences.en: Which may help explain why people's reaction to a new idea is often the first half of laughing: Ha![3] That second qualifier is critical.
sentences.zh: 这可能有助于解释为什么人们对新想法的反应往往是前半部分大笑：哈！[3] 第二个限定词至关重要。

sentences.en: If you're excited about something most authorities discount, but you can't give a more precise explanation than "they don't get it," then you're starting to drift into the territory of cranks.[4] Finding something to work on is not simply a matter of finding a match between the current version of you and a list of known problems.
sentences.zh: 如果你对大多数权威机构忽视的东西感到兴奋，但你无法给出比“他们不明白”更精确的解释，那么你就开始陷入怪人的领域。 [4]找到需要解决的问题并不仅仅是在你当前的版本和一系列已知问题之间找到匹配的问题。

sentences.en: You'll often have to coevolve with the problem.
sentences.zh: 你常常必须与问题共同发展。

sentences.en: That's why it can sometimes be so hard to figure out what to work on.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有时很难弄清楚该做什么。

sentences.en: The search space is huge.
sentences.zh: 搜索空间巨大。

sentences.en: It's the cartesian product of all possible types of work, both known and yet to be discovered, and all possible future versions of you.There's no way you could search this whole space, so you have to rely on heuristics to generate promising paths through it and hope the best matches will be clustered.
sentences.zh: 它是所有可能类型的工作（包括已知的和尚未发现的）以及您所有可能的未来版本的笛卡尔积。您无法搜索整个空间，因此您必须依靠启发式方法来生成有希望的路径，并希望能够聚集最佳匹配。

sentences.en: Which they will not always be; different types of work have been collected together as much by accidents of history as by the intrinsic similarities between them.[5] There are many reasons curious people are more likely to do great work, but one of the more subtle is that, by casting a wide net, they're more likely to find the right thing to work on in the first place.[6] It can also be dangerous to make things for an audience you feel is less sophisticated than you, if that causes you to talk down to them.
sentences.zh: 但他们不会永远如此；不同类型的作品之所以被聚集在一起，既是因为历史的偶然，也是因为它们之间的内在相似性。 [5]好奇的人更有可能做出出色的工作，原因有很多，但其中一个更微妙的原因是，通过广泛撒网，他们更有可能首先找到正确的事情。 [6]如果为你认为不如你成熟的观众制作东西会导致你居高临下地与他们交谈，那么这也可能是危险的。

sentences.en: You can make a lot of money doing that, if you do it in a sufficiently cynical way, but it's not the route to great work.
sentences.zh: 如果你以一种足够愤世嫉俗的方式去做的话，你可以赚很多钱，但这并不是通往伟大工作的道路。

sentences.en: Not that anyone using this m.o.
sentences.zh: 并不是说有人使用这个 m.o.

sentences.en: would care.[7] This idea I learned from Hardy's A Mathematician's Apology, which I recommend to anyone ambitious to do great work, in any field.[8] Just as we overestimate what we can do in a day and underestimate what we can do over several years, we overestimate the damage done by procrastinating for a day and underestimate the damage done by procrastinating for several years.[9] You can't usually get paid for doing exactly what you want, especially early on.
sentences.zh: 会关心的。[7]这个想法是我从哈代的《数学家的道歉》中学到的，我向任何有志于在任何领域做出伟大工作的人推荐这本书。 [8]正如我们高估一天能做的事情，低估几年能做的事情一样，我们高估了拖延一天造成的损害，却低估了拖延几年造成的损害。 [9]你通常无法因为完全按照自己的意愿去做而获得报酬，尤其是在早期。

sentences.en: There are two options: get paid for doing work close to what you want and hope to push it closer, or get paid for doing something else entirely and do your own projects on the side.
sentences.zh: 有两种选择：通过做接近你想要的事情并希望更接近你想要的事情来获得报酬，或者通过完全做其他事情来获得报酬并兼职做你自己的项目。

sentences.en: Both can work, but both have drawbacks: in the first approach your work is compromised by default, and in the second you have to fight to get time to do it.[10] If you set your life up right, it will deliver the focus-relax cycle automatically.
sentences.zh: 两者都可以工作，但都有缺点：在第一种方法中，默认情况下你的工作会受到影响，而在第二种方法中，你必须争取时间来完成它。[10]如果你的生活安排得当，它会自动实现专注-放松的循环。

sentences.en: The perfect setup is an office you work in and that you walk to and from.[11] There may be some very unworldly people who do great work without consciously trying to.
sentences.zh: 完美的设置是您工作并步行往返的办公室。[11]可能有一些非常不谙世事的人，在没有有意识地努力的情况下却做出了伟大的工作。

sentences.en: If you want to expand this rule to cover that case, it becomes: Don't try to be anything except the best.[12] This gets more complicated in work like acting, where the goal is to adopt a fake persona.
sentences.zh: 如果你想扩展这条​​规则来涵盖这种情况，它就会变成：除了最好之外，不要试图成为任何人。[12]这在表演等工作中变得更加复杂，其目标是采用假角色。

sentences.en: But even here it's possible to be affected.
sentences.zh: 但即使在这里也可能受到影响。

sentences.en: Perhaps the rule in such fields should be to avoid unintentional affectation.[13] It's safe to have beliefs that you treat as unquestionable if and only if they're also unfalsifiable.
sentences.zh: 也许这些领域的规则应该是避免无意识的矫揉造作。 [13]当且仅当它们也是不可证伪的时，你认为无可置疑的信念才是安全的。

sentences.en: For example, it's safe to have the principle that everyone should be treated equally under the law, because a sentence with a "should" in it isn't really a statement about the world and is therefore hard to disprove.
sentences.zh: 例如，遵循法律面前人人平等的原则是安全的，因为带有“应该”的句子实际上并不是关于世界的陈述，因此很难反驳。

sentences.en: And if there's no evidence that could disprove one of your principles, there can't be any facts you'd need to ignore in order to preserve it.[14] Affectation is easier to cure than intellectual dishonesty.
sentences.zh: 如果没有证据可以反驳你的一项原则，那么你就不需要为了维护它而忽略任何事实。 [14]矫揉造作比理智上的不诚实更容易治愈。

sentences.en: Affectation is often a shortcoming of the young that burns off in time, while intellectual dishonesty is more of a character flaw.[15] Obviously you don't have to be working at the exact moment you have the idea, but you'll probably have been working fairly recently.[16] Some say psychoactive drugs have a similar effect.
sentences.zh: 矫揉造作往往是年轻人的一个缺点，随着时间的推移就会消失，而智力上的不诚实则更多的是一种性格缺陷。 [15]显然，您不必在产生想法的那一刻开始工作，但您可能最近才开始工作。[16]有人说精神药物也有类似的效果。

sentences.en: I'm skeptical, but also almost totally ignorant of their effects.[17] For example you might give the nth most important topic (m-1)/m^n of your attention, for some m > 1.
sentences.zh: 我对此表示怀疑，但也几乎完全不知道它们的影响。[17]例如，您可能会给出您关注的第 n 个最重要的主题 (m-1)/m^n，其中 m > 1。

sentences.en: You couldn't allocate your attention so precisely, of course, but this at least gives an idea of a reasonable distribution.[18] The principles defining a religion have to be mistaken.
sentences.zh: 当然，你无法如此精确地分配注意力，但这至少给出了合理分配的想法。[18]定义宗教的原则一定是错误的。

sentences.en: Otherwise anyone might adopt them, and there would be nothing to distinguish the adherents of the religion from everyone else.[19] It might be a good exercise to try writing down a list of questions you wondered about in your youth.
sentences.zh: 否则任何人都可能采用它们，并且没有任何东西可以将宗教信徒与其他人区分开来。 [19]尝试写下你年轻时想知道的问题清单可能是一个很好的练习。

sentences.en: You might find you're now in a position to do something about some of them.[20] The connection between originality and uncertainty causes a strange phenomenon: because the conventional-minded are more certain than the independent-minded, this tends to give them the upper hand in disputes, even though they're generally stupider.
sentences.zh: 您可能会发现您现在可以对其中一些问题采取一些措施。[20]原创性和不确定性之间的联系导致了一种奇怪的现象：因为传统思维的人比独立思维的人更有确定性，这往往使他们在争论中占据上风，尽管他们通常更愚蠢。

sentences.en: The best lack all conviction, while the worst Are full of passionate intensity. [21] Derived from Linus Pauling's "If you want to have good ideas, you must have many ideas."[22] Attacking a project as a "toy" is similar to attacking a statement as "inappropriate."
sentences.zh: 最好的人缺乏坚定的信念，而最差的人则充满激情。 [21] 源自莱纳斯·鲍林（Linus Pauling）的“如果你想有好的想法，你必须有很多想法。”[22] 将项目攻击为“玩具”类似于将声明攻击为“不恰当”。

sentences.en: It means that no more substantial criticism can be made to stick.[23] One way to tell whether you're wasting time is to ask if you're producing or consuming.
sentences.zh: 这意味着无法再提出更多实质性的批评。[23]判断你是否在浪费时间的一种方法是询问你是否在生产或消费。

sentences.en: Writing computer games is less likely to be a waste of time than playing them, and playing games where you create something is less likely to be a waste of time than playing games where you don't.[24] Another related advantage is that if you haven't said anything publicly yet, you won't be biased toward evidence that supports your earlier conclusions.
sentences.zh: 编写电脑游戏比玩电脑游戏更不可能浪费时间，而玩自己创造的游戏比玩自己不创造的游戏更不可能浪费时间。 [24]另一个相关的优势是，如果您还没有公开发表任何言论，您就不会偏向支持您之前结论的证据。

sentences.en: With sufficient integrity you could achieve eternal youth in this respect, but few manage to.
sentences.zh: 只要有足够的正直，你就可以在这方面实现永葆青春，但很少有人能做到。

sentences.en: For most people, having previously published opinions has an effect similar to ideology, just in quantity 1.[25] In the early 1630s Daniel Mytens made a painting of Henrietta Maria handing a laurel wreath to Charles I.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数人来说，之前发表过的观点具有类似于意识形态的效果，只是数量为 1。 [25] 1630 年代初期，丹尼尔·迈滕斯 (Daniel Mytens) 创作了一幅亨利埃塔·玛丽亚 (Henrietta Maria) 向查理一世递上月桂花环的画作。

sentences.en: Van Dyck then painted his own version to show how much better he was.[26] I'm being deliberately vague about what a place is.
sentences.zh: 范戴克随后画了他自己的版本，以显示他有多好。[26]我故意对“地方”一词含糊其辞。

sentences.en: As of this writing, being in the same physical place has advantages that are hard to duplicate, but that could change.[27] This is false when the work the other people have to do is very constrained, as with SETI@home or Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 截至撰写本文时，处于同一物理位置具有难以复制的优势，但这种情况可能会改变。 [27]当其他人必须做的工作非常有限时，就像 SETI@home 或比特币一样，这是错误的。

sentences.en: It may be possible to expand the area in which it's false by defining similarly restricted protocols with more freedom of action in the nodes.[28] Corollary: Building something that enables people to go around intermediaries and engage directly with their audience is probably a good idea.[29] It may be helpful always to walk or run the same route, because that frees attention for thinking.
sentences.zh: 通过定义类似的限制协议并在节点中提供更多的行动自由度，可以扩大错误的范围。 [28]推论：构建一些使人们能够绕过中介并直接与受众互动的东西可能是一个好主意。 [29]始终走或跑同一条路线可能会有所帮助，因为这样可以释放注意力以进行思考。

sentences.en: It feels that way to me, and there is some historical evidence for it.Thanks to Trevor Blackwell, Daniel Gackle, Pam Graham, Tom Howard, Patrick Hsu, Steve Huffman, Jessica Livingston, Henry Lloyd-Baker, Bob Metcalfe, Ben Miller, Robert Morris, Michael Nielsen, Courtenay Pipkin, Joris Poort, Mieke Roos, Rajat Suri, Harj Taggar, Garry Tan, and my younger son for suggestions and for reading drafts.
sentences.zh: 我感觉就是这样，而且有一些历史证据。感谢 Trevor Blackwell、Daniel Gackle、Pam Graham、Tom Howard、Patrick Hsu、Steve Huffman、Jessica Livingston、Henry Lloyd-Baker、Bob Metcalfe、Ben Miller、Robert Morris、Michael Nielsen、Courtenay Pipkin、Joris Poort、Mieke Roos、Rajat Suri、Harj Taggar、Garry Tan 和我的小儿子的建议和帮助阅读草稿。

blocks.html_en: If you collected lists of techniques for doing great work in a lot of different fields, what would the intersection look like? I decided to find out by making it.

sentences.en: If you collected lists of techniques for doing great work in a lot of different fields, what would the intersection look like?
sentences.zh: 如果您收集了在许多不同领域做出出色工作的技术列表，那么交集会是什么样子？

sentences.en: I decided to find out by making it.
sentences.zh: 我决定通过制作来找出答案。

blocks.html_en: Partly my goal was to create a guide that could be used by someone working in any field. But I was also curious about the shape of the intersection. And one thing this exercise shows is that it does have a definite shape; it's not just a point labelled "work hard."

sentences.en: Partly my goal was to create a guide that could be used by someone working in any field.
sentences.zh: 我的部分目标是创建一个可供任何领域工作的人使用的指南。

sentences.en: But I was also curious about the shape of the intersection.
sentences.zh: 但我也对十字路口的形状感到好奇。

sentences.en: And one thing this exercise shows is that it does have a definite shape; it's not just a point labelled "work hard."
sentences.zh: 这个练习表明的一件事是它确实有一个明确的形状；这不仅仅是一个标有“努力工作”的点。

blocks.html_en: The following recipe assumes you're very ambitious.

sentences.en: The following recipe assumes you're very ambitious.
sentences.zh: 以下食谱假设您非常雄心勃勃。

blocks.html_en: The first step is to decide what to work on. The work you choose needs to have three qualities: it has to be something you have a natural aptitude for, that you have a deep interest in, and that offers scope to do great work.

sentences.en: The first step is to decide what to work on.
sentences.zh: 第一步是决定要做什么。

sentences.en: The work you choose needs to have three qualities: it has to be something you have a natural aptitude for, that you have a deep interest in, and that offers scope to do great work.
sentences.zh: 你选择的工作需要具备三个品质：它必须是你有天赋的东西，你对此有浓厚的兴趣，并且提供了完成伟大工作的空间。

blocks.html_en: In practice you don't have to worry much about the third criterion. Ambitious people are if anything already too conservative about it. So all you need to do is find something you have an aptitude for and great interest in.

sentences.en: In practice you don't have to worry much about the third criterion.
sentences.zh: 实际上，您不必太担心第三个标准。

sentences.en: Ambitious people are if anything already too conservative about it.
sentences.zh: 雄心勃勃的人对此已经过于保守了。

sentences.en: So all you need to do is find something you have an aptitude for and great interest in.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要做的就是找到你有天赋并且非常感兴趣的东西。

blocks.html_en: That sounds straightforward, but it's often quite difficult. When you're young you don't know what you're good at or what different kinds of work are like. Some kinds of work you end up doing may not even exist yet. So while some people know what they want to do at 14, most have to figure it out.

sentences.en: That sounds straightforward, but it's often quite difficult.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很简单，但通常非常困难。

sentences.en: When you're young you don't know what you're good at or what different kinds of work are like.
sentences.zh: 当你年轻的时候，你不知道自己擅长什么，也不知道不同种类的工作是什么样的。

sentences.en: Some kinds of work you end up doing may not even exist yet.
sentences.zh: 你最终要做的某些工作可能还不存在。

sentences.en: So while some people know what they want to do at 14, most have to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然有些人知道自己 14 岁时想做什么，但大多数人都必须弄清楚。

blocks.html_en: The way to figure out what to work on is by working. If you're not sure what to work on, guess. But pick something and get going. You'll probably guess wrong some of the time, but that's fine. It's good to know about multiple things; some of the biggest discoveries come from noticing connections between different fields.

sentences.en: The way to figure out what to work on is by working.
sentences.zh: 弄清楚要做什么的方法就是通过工作。

sentences.en: If you're not sure what to work on, guess.
sentences.zh: 如果您不确定要做什么，请猜测。

sentences.en: But pick something and get going.
sentences.zh: 但选择一些东西然后开始吧。

sentences.en: You'll probably guess wrong some of the time, but that's fine.
sentences.zh: 有时你可能会猜错，但这没关系。

sentences.en: It's good to know about multiple things; some of the biggest discoveries come from noticing connections between different fields.
sentences.zh: 了解多种事物是件好事；一些最大的发现来自于注意到不同领域之间的联系。

blocks.html_en: Develop a habit of working on your own projects. Don't let "work" mean something other people tell you to do. If you do manage to do great work one day, it will probably be on a project of your own. It may be within some bigger project, but you'll be driving your part of it.

sentences.en: Develop a habit of working on your own projects.
sentences.zh: 养成从事自己项目的习惯。

sentences.en: Don't let "work" mean something other people tell you to do.
sentences.zh: 不要让“工作”意味着别人告诉你做的事情。

sentences.en: If you do manage to do great work one day, it will probably be on a project of your own.
sentences.zh: 如果有一天你确实能做出出色的工作，那很可能是在你自己的一个项目上。

sentences.en: It may be within some bigger project, but you'll be driving your part of it.
sentences.zh: 它可能在一些更大的项目中，但你将推动你的部分。

blocks.html_en: What should your projects be? Whatever seems to you excitingly ambitious. As you grow older and your taste in projects evolves, exciting and important will converge. At 7 it may seem excitingly ambitious to build huge things out of Lego, then at 14 to teach yourself calculus, till at 21 you're starting to explore unanswered questions in physics. But always preserve excitingness.

sentences.en: What should your projects be?
sentences.zh: 你的项目应该是什么？

sentences.en: Whatever seems to you excitingly ambitious.
sentences.zh: 任何在你看来令人兴奋的雄心勃勃的事情。

sentences.en: As you grow older and your taste in projects evolves, exciting and important will converge.
sentences.zh: 随着年龄的增长和对项目的品味的变化，令人兴奋和重要的事情将会融合在一起。

sentences.en: At 7 it may seem excitingly ambitious to build huge things out of Lego, then at 14 to teach yourself calculus, till at 21 you're starting to explore unanswered questions in physics.
sentences.zh: 7 岁的时候，用乐高搭建巨大的东西似乎是令人兴奋的雄心勃勃，然后 14 岁的时候自学微积分，直到 21 岁开始探索物理学中尚未解答的问题。

sentences.en: But always preserve excitingness.
sentences.zh: 但始终保持兴奋。

blocks.html_en: There's a kind of excited curiosity that's both the engine and the rudder of great work. It will not only drive you, but if you let it have its way, will also show you what to work on.

sentences.en: There's a kind of excited curiosity that's both the engine and the rudder of great work.
sentences.zh: 有一种兴奋的好奇心，它既是伟大工作的引擎，也是伟大工作的舵。

sentences.en: It will not only drive you, but if you let it have its way, will also show you what to work on.
sentences.zh: 它不仅会驱动你，而且如果你顺其自然，它也会告诉你应该做什么。

blocks.html_en: What are you excessively curious about — curious to a degree that would bore most other people? That's what you're looking for.

sentences.en: What are you excessively curious about — curious to a degree that would bore most other people?
sentences.zh: 你对什么过度好奇——好奇到让大多数人感到厌烦的程度？

sentences.en: That's what you're looking for.
sentences.zh: 这就是您要寻找的。

blocks.html_en: Once you've found something you're excessively interested in, the next step is to learn enough about it to get you to one of the frontiers of knowledge. Knowledge expands fractally, and from a distance its edges look smooth, but once you learn enough to get close to one, they turn out to be full of gaps.

sentences.en: Once you've found something you're excessively interested in, the next step is to learn enough about it to get you to one of the frontiers of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 一旦你发现了你非常感兴趣的东西，下一步就是充分了解它，让你到达知识的前沿之一。

sentences.en: Knowledge expands fractally, and from a distance its edges look smooth, but once you learn enough to get close to one, they turn out to be full of gaps.
sentences.zh: 知识以分形方式扩展，从远处看，它的边缘看起来很光滑，但一旦你学到足够多的东西来接近它，就会发现它们充满了间隙。

blocks.html_en: The next step is to notice them. This takes some skill, because your brain wants to ignore such gaps in order to make a simpler model of the world. Many discoveries have come from asking questions about things that everyone else took for granted.

sentences.en: The next step is to notice them.
sentences.zh: 下一步是注意它们。

sentences.en: This takes some skill, because your brain wants to ignore such gaps in order to make a simpler model of the world.
sentences.zh: 这需要一些技巧，因为你的大脑想要忽略这些差距，以便建立一个更简单的世界模型。

sentences.en: Many discoveries have come from asking questions about things that everyone else took for granted.
sentences.zh: 许多发现都来自于对其他人认为理所当然的事情提出问题。

blocks.html_en: If the answers seem strange, so much the better. Great work often has a tincture of strangeness. You see this from painting to math. It would be affected to try to manufacture it, but if it appears, embrace it.

sentences.en: If the answers seem strange, so much the better.
sentences.zh: 如果答案看起来很奇怪，那就更好了。

sentences.en: Great work often has a tincture of strangeness.
sentences.zh: 伟大的作品常常带有一丝陌生的味道。

sentences.en: You see this from painting to math.
sentences.zh: 从绘画到数学你都能看到这一点。

sentences.en: It would be affected to try to manufacture it, but if it appears, embrace it.
sentences.zh: 尝试制造它会受到影响，但如果它出现，就拥抱它。

blocks.html_en: Boldly chase outlier ideas, even if other people aren't interested in them — in fact, especially if they aren't. If you're excited about some possibility that everyone else ignores, and you have enough expertise to say precisely what they're all overlooking, that's as good a bet as you'll find.

sentences.en: Boldly chase outlier ideas, even if other people aren't interested in them — in fact, especially if they aren't.
sentences.zh: 大胆地追寻离奇的想法，即使其他人对此不感兴趣——事实上，尤其是如果他们不感兴趣的话。

sentences.en: If you're excited about some possibility that everyone else ignores, and you have enough expertise to say precisely what they're all overlooking, that's as good a bet as you'll find.
sentences.zh: 如果你对其他人都忽略的某种可能性感到兴奋，并且你有足够的专业知识来准确地说出他们都忽略的事情，那么这就是你会发现的最好的选择。

blocks.html_en: Four steps: choose a field, learn enough to get to the frontier, notice gaps, explore promising ones. This is how practically everyone who's done great work has done it, from painters to physicists.

sentences.en: Four steps: choose a field, learn enough to get to the frontier, notice gaps, explore promising ones.
sentences.zh: 四个步骤：选择一个领域，学习足够的知识以达到前沿，注意到差距，探索有前途的领域。

sentences.en: This is how practically everyone who's done great work has done it, from painters to physicists.
sentences.zh: 实际上，从画家到物理学家，每个做出伟大工作的人都是这样做的。

blocks.html_en: Steps two and four will require hard work. It may not be possible to prove that you have to work hard to do great things, but the empirical evidence is on the scale of the evidence for mortality. That's why it's essential to work on something you're deeply interested in. Interest will drive you to work harder than mere diligence ever could.

sentences.en: Steps two and four will require hard work.
sentences.zh: 第二步和第四步需要努力。

sentences.en: It may not be possible to prove that you have to work hard to do great things, but the empirical evidence is on the scale of the evidence for mortality.
sentences.zh: 也许无法证明你必须努力工作才能做伟大的事情，但经验证据的规模与死亡率的证据相当。

sentences.en: That's why it's essential to work on something you're deeply interested in.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么从事您感兴趣的事情至关重要。

sentences.en: Interest will drive you to work harder than mere diligence ever could.
sentences.zh: 兴趣会促使你比单纯的勤奋更加努力地工作。

blocks.html_en: The three most powerful motives are curiosity, delight, and the desire to do something impressive. Sometimes they converge, and that combination is the most powerful of all.

sentences.en: The three most powerful motives are curiosity, delight, and the desire to do something impressive.
sentences.zh: 三个最强大的动机是好奇心、快乐和想做一些令人印象深刻的事情的愿望。

sentences.en: Sometimes they converge, and that combination is the most powerful of all.
sentences.zh: 有时它们会融合在一起，而这种组合是最强大的。

blocks.html_en: The big prize is to discover a new fractal bud. You notice a crack in the surface of knowledge, pry it open, and there's a whole world inside.

sentences.en: The big prize is to discover a new fractal bud.
sentences.zh: 最大的奖励是发现一个新的分形芽。

sentences.en: You notice a crack in the surface of knowledge, pry it open, and there's a whole world inside.
sentences.zh: 你注意到知识表面有一条裂缝，把它撬开，里面有一个完整的世界。

blocks.html_en: Let's talk a little more about the complicated business of figuring out what to work on. The main reason it's hard is that you can't tell what most kinds of work are like except by doing them. Which means the four steps overlap: you may have to work at something for years before you know how much you like it or how good you are at it. And in the meantime you're not doing, and thus not learning about, most other kinds of work. So in the worst case you choose late based on very incomplete information.

sentences.en: Let's talk a little more about the complicated business of figuring out what to work on.
sentences.zh: 让我们多谈谈弄清楚要做什么的复杂事情。

sentences.en: The main reason it's hard is that you can't tell what most kinds of work are like except by doing them.
sentences.zh: 其困难的主要原因是，除非亲自去做，否则你无法辨别大多数类型的工作是什么样的。

sentences.en: Which means the four steps overlap: you may have to work at something for years before you know how much you like it or how good you are at it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这四个步骤是重叠的：你可能需要在某件事上工作多年才能知道你有多喜欢它或者你有多擅长它。

sentences.en: And in the meantime you're not doing, and thus not learning about, most other kinds of work.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，你并没有做，因此也没有学习大多数其他类型的工作。

sentences.en: So in the worst case you choose late based on very incomplete information.
sentences.zh: 因此，在最坏的情况下，您会根据非常不完整的信息选择延迟。

blocks.html_en: The nature of ambition exacerbates this problem. Ambition comes in two forms, one that precedes interest in the subject and one that grows out of it. Most people who do great work have a mix, and the more you have of the former, the harder it will be to decide what to do.

sentences.en: The nature of ambition exacerbates this problem.
sentences.zh: 野心的本质加剧了这个问题。

sentences.en: Ambition comes in two forms, one that precedes interest in the subject and one that grows out of it.
sentences.zh: 野心有两种形式，一种是先于对某个学科的兴趣，另一种则源于对该学科的兴趣。

sentences.en: Most people who do great work have a mix, and the more you have of the former, the harder it will be to decide what to do.
sentences.zh: 大多数出色工作的人都是混合的，而且前者越多，就越难决定做什么。

blocks.html_en: The educational systems in most countries pretend it's easy. They expect you to commit to a field long before you could know what it's really like. And as a result an ambitious person on an optimal trajectory will often read to the system as an instance of breakage.

sentences.en: The educational systems in most countries pretend it's easy.
sentences.zh: 大多数国家的教育系统都假装这很容易。

sentences.en: They expect you to commit to a field long before you could know what it's really like.
sentences.zh: 他们希望你早在知道某个领域到底是什么样子之前就投入其中。

sentences.en: And as a result an ambitious person on an optimal trajectory will often read to the system as an instance of breakage.
sentences.zh: 因此，一个处于最佳轨道上的雄心勃勃的人经常会将系统视为破坏的例子。

blocks.html_en: It would be better if they at least admitted it — if they admitted that the system not only can't do much to help you figure out what to work on, but is designed on the assumption that you'll somehow magically guess as a teenager. They don't tell you, but I will: when it comes to figuring out what to work on, you're on your own. Some people get lucky and do guess correctly, but the rest will find themselves scrambling diagonally across tracks laid down on the assumption that everyone does.

sentences.en: It would be better if they at least admitted it — if they admitted that the system not only can't do much to help you figure out what to work on, but is designed on the assumption that you'll somehow magically guess as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 如果他们至少承认这一点那就更好了——如果他们承认这个系统不仅不能帮助你弄清楚该做什么，而且它的设计假设你在青少年时期会以某种方式神奇地猜测。

sentences.en: They don't tell you, but I will: when it comes to figuring out what to work on, you're on your own.
sentences.zh: 他们不会告诉你，但我会告诉你：当谈到弄清楚要做什么时，你得靠自己。

sentences.en: Some people get lucky and do guess correctly, but the rest will find themselves scrambling diagonally across tracks laid down on the assumption that everyone does.
sentences.zh: 有些人很幸运，确实猜对了，但其他人会发现自己在假设每个人都这样做的情况下沿着对角线爬行。

blocks.html_en: What should you do if you're young and ambitious but don't know what to work on? What you should not do is drift along passively, assuming the problem will solve itself. You need to take action. But there is no systematic procedure you can follow. When you read biographies of people who've done great work, it's remarkable how much luck is involved. They discover what to work on as a result of a chance meeting, or by reading a book they happen to pick up. So you need to make yourself a big target for luck, and the way to do that is to be curious. Try lots of things, meet lots of people, read lots of books, ask lots of questions.

sentences.en: What should you do if you're young and ambitious but don't know what to work on?
sentences.zh: 如果你年轻、有抱负但不知道该做什么，你该怎么办？

sentences.en: What you should not do is drift along passively, assuming the problem will solve itself.
sentences.zh: 你不应该做的是被动地随波逐流，假设问题会自行解决。

sentences.en: You need to take action.
sentences.zh: 你需要采取行动。

sentences.en: But there is no systematic procedure you can follow.
sentences.zh: 但没有可以遵循的系统程序。

sentences.en: When you read biographies of people who've done great work, it's remarkable how much luck is involved.
sentences.zh: 当你阅读那些做出了伟大工作的人的传记时，你会发现其中涉及到多少运气。

sentences.en: They discover what to work on as a result of a chance meeting, or by reading a book they happen to pick up.
sentences.zh: 他们通过一次偶然的机会，或者通过读一本他们偶然拿起的书来发现要做什么。

sentences.en: So you need to make yourself a big target for luck, and the way to do that is to be curious.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要让自己成为一个幸运的大目标，而做到这一点的方法就是保持好奇心。

sentences.en: Try lots of things, meet lots of people, read lots of books, ask lots of questions.
sentences.zh: 尝试很多事情，认识很多人，读很多书，问很多问题。

blocks.html_en: When in doubt, optimize for interestingness. Fields change as you learn more about them. What mathematicians do, for example, is very different from what you do in high school math classes. So you need to give different types of work a chance to show you what they're like. But a field should become increasingly interesting as you learn more about it. If it doesn't, it's probably not for you.

sentences.en: When in doubt, optimize for interestingness.
sentences.zh: 如有疑问，请针对兴趣进行优化。

sentences.en: Fields change as you learn more about them.
sentences.zh: 当您了解更多领域时，领域就会发生变化。

sentences.en: What mathematicians do, for example, is very different from what you do in high school math classes.
sentences.zh: 例如，数学家所做的事情与你在高中数学课上所做的事情非常不同。

sentences.en: So you need to give different types of work a chance to show you what they're like.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要给不同类型的工作一个机会来展示它们是什么样的。

sentences.en: But a field should become increasingly interesting as you learn more about it.
sentences.zh: 但当你对某个领域了解得越多时，它就会变得越来越有趣。

sentences.en: If it doesn't, it's probably not for you.
sentences.zh: 如果没有，它可能不适合你。

blocks.html_en: Don't worry if you find you're interested in different things than other people. The stranger your tastes in interestingness, the better. Strange tastes are often strong ones, and a strong taste for work means you'll be productive. And you're more likely to find new things if you're looking where few have looked before.

sentences.en: Don't worry if you find you're interested in different things than other people.
sentences.zh: 如果您发现自己对与其他人不同的事物感兴趣，请不要担心。

sentences.en: The stranger your tastes in interestingness, the better.
sentences.zh: 你的兴趣爱好越陌生越好。

sentences.en: Strange tastes are often strong ones, and a strong taste for work means you'll be productive.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的品味往往很强烈，而强烈的工作品味意味着你会富有成效。

sentences.en: And you're more likely to find new things if you're looking where few have looked before.
sentences.zh: 如果您正在寻找以前很少有人关注过的地方，那么您更有可能发现新事物。

blocks.html_en: One sign that you're suited for some kind of work is when you like even the parts that other people find tedious or frightening.

sentences.en: One sign that you're suited for some kind of work is when you like even the parts that other people find tedious or frightening.
sentences.zh: 您适合某种工作的一个标志是，您甚至喜欢其他人认为乏味或令人恐惧的部分。

blocks.html_en: But fields aren't people; you don't owe them any loyalty. If in the course of working on one thing you discover another that's more exciting, don't be afraid to switch.

sentences.en: But fields aren't people; you don't owe them any loyalty.
sentences.zh: 但田野不是人，而是田野。你不欠他们任何忠诚。

sentences.en: If in the course of working on one thing you discover another that's more exciting, don't be afraid to switch.
sentences.zh: 如果在做一件事的过程中你发现另一件事更令人兴奋，不要害怕改变。

blocks.html_en: If you're making something for people, make sure it's something they actually want. The best way to do this is to make something you yourself want. Write the story you want to read; build the tool you want to use. Since your friends probably have similar interests, this will also get you your initial audience.

sentences.en: If you're making something for people, make sure it's something they actually want.
sentences.zh: 如果你要为人们做一些东西，请确保这是他们真正想要的东西。

sentences.en: The best way to do this is to make something you yourself want.
sentences.zh: 做到这一点的最好方法就是做一些你自己想要的东西。

sentences.en: Write the story you want to read; build the tool you want to use.
sentences.zh: 写下你想读的故事；构建您想要使用的工具。

sentences.en: Since your friends probably have similar interests, this will also get you your initial audience.
sentences.zh: 由于您的朋友可能有相似的兴趣，这也将为您带来最初的受众。

blocks.html_en: This should follow from the excitingness rule. Obviously the most exciting story to write will be the one you want to read. The reason I mention this case explicitly is that so many people get it wrong. Instead of making what they want, they try to make what some imaginary, more sophisticated audience wants. And once you go down that route, you're lost.

sentences.en: This should follow from the excitingness rule.
sentences.zh: 这应该遵循令人兴奋的规则。

sentences.en: Obviously the most exciting story to write will be the one you want to read.
sentences.zh: 显然，最令人兴奋的故事将是您想读的故事。

sentences.en: The reason I mention this case explicitly is that so many people get it wrong.
sentences.zh: 我之所以明确提及这个案例，是因为很多人都误解了。

sentences.en: Instead of making what they want, they try to make what some imaginary, more sophisticated audience wants.
sentences.zh: 他们没有制作他们想要的东西，而是尝试制作一些想象中的、更复杂的观众想要的东西。

sentences.en: And once you go down that route, you're lost.
sentences.zh: 一旦你沿着这条路走下去，你就会迷路。

blocks.html_en: There are a lot of forces that will lead you astray when you're trying to figure out what to work on. Pretentiousness, fashion, fear, money, politics, other people's wishes, eminent frauds. But if you stick to what you find genuinely interesting, you'll be proof against all of them. If you're interested, you're not astray.

sentences.en: There are a lot of forces that will lead you astray when you're trying to figure out what to work on.
sentences.zh: 当你试图弄清楚要做什么时，有很多力量会让你误入歧途。

sentences.en: Pretentiousness, fashion, fear, money, politics, other people's wishes, eminent frauds.
sentences.zh: 自命不凡、时尚、恐惧、金钱、政治、他人的愿望、显着的欺诈。

sentences.en: But if you stick to what you find genuinely interesting, you'll be proof against all of them.
sentences.zh: 但如果你坚持做你真正感兴趣的事情，你就会战胜所有这些。

sentences.en: If you're interested, you're not astray.
sentences.zh: 如果你有兴趣，你就不会迷路。

blocks.html_en: Following your interests may sound like a rather passive strategy, but in practice it usually means following them past all sorts of obstacles. You usually have to risk rejection and failure. So it does take a good deal of boldness.

sentences.en: Following your interests may sound like a rather passive strategy, but in practice it usually means following them past all sorts of obstacles.
sentences.zh: 追随你的兴趣可能听起来像是一种相当被动的策略，但实际上，这通常意味着追随你的兴趣，克服各种障碍。

sentences.en: You usually have to risk rejection and failure.
sentences.zh: 你通常必须冒被拒绝和失败的风险。

sentences.en: So it does take a good deal of boldness.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实需要很大的勇气。

blocks.html_en: But while you need boldness, you don't usually need much planning. In most cases the recipe for doing great work is simply: work hard on excitingly ambitious projects, and something good will come of it. Instead of making a plan and then executing it, you just try to preserve certain invariants.

sentences.en: But while you need boldness, you don't usually need much planning.
sentences.zh: 但是，虽然您需要勇气，但通常不需要太多计划。

sentences.en: In most cases the recipe for doing great work is simply: work hard on excitingly ambitious projects, and something good will come of it.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，做好工作的秘诀很简单：在令人兴奋的雄心勃勃的项目上努力工作，并且会带来好的结果。

sentences.en: Instead of making a plan and then executing it, you just try to preserve certain invariants.
sentences.zh: 您只需尝试保留某些不变量，而不是制定计划然后执行它。

blocks.html_en: The trouble with planning is that it only works for achievements you can describe in advance. You can win a gold medal or get rich by deciding to as a child and then tenaciously pursuing that goal, but you can't discover natural selection that way.

sentences.en: The trouble with planning is that it only works for achievements you can describe in advance.
sentences.zh: 计划的问题在于它只适用于你可以提前描述的成就。

sentences.en: You can win a gold medal or get rich by deciding to as a child and then tenaciously pursuing that goal, but you can't discover natural selection that way.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过小时候的决定并顽强地追求这个目标来赢得金牌或致富，但你无法通过这种方式发现自然选择。

blocks.html_en: I think for most people who want to do great work, the right strategy is not to plan too much. At each stage do whatever seems most interesting and gives you the best options for the future. I call this approach "staying upwind." This is how most people who've done great work seem to have done it.

sentences.en: I think for most people who want to do great work, the right strategy is not to plan too much.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于大多数想要做好工作的人来说，正确的策略是不要计划太多。

sentences.en: At each stage do whatever seems most interesting and gives you the best options for the future.
sentences.zh: 在每个阶段，做任何看起来最有趣的事情，并为你的未来提供最好的选择。

sentences.en: I call this approach "staying upwind."
sentences.zh: 我将这种方法称为“保持上风”。

sentences.en: This is how most people who've done great work seem to have done it.
sentences.zh: 大多数做出伟大工作的人似乎都是这样做的。

blocks.html_en: Even when you've found something exciting to work on, working on it is not always straightforward. There will be times when some new idea makes you leap out of bed in the morning and get straight to work. But there will also be plenty of times when things aren't like that.

sentences.en: Even when you've found something exciting to work on, working on it is not always straightforward.
sentences.zh: 即使你发现了一些令人兴奋的事情可以做，但做起来并不总是那么简单。

sentences.en: There will be times when some new idea makes you leap out of bed in the morning and get straight to work.
sentences.zh: 有时，一些新想法会让你早上从床上跳起来直接开始工作。

sentences.en: But there will also be plenty of times when things aren't like that.
sentences.zh: 但也有很多时候事情并非如此。

blocks.html_en: You don't just put out your sail and get blown forward by inspiration. There are headwinds and currents and hidden shoals. So there's a technique to working, just as there is to sailing.

sentences.en: You don't just put out your sail and get blown forward by inspiration.
sentences.zh: 你不只是扬起风帆，被灵感吹向前方。

sentences.en: There are headwinds and currents and hidden shoals.
sentences.zh: 这里有逆风、洋流和隐藏的浅滩。

sentences.en: So there's a technique to working, just as there is to sailing.
sentences.zh: 所以工作是有技巧的，就像航海有技巧一样。

blocks.html_en: For example, while you must work hard, it's possible to work too hard, and if you do that you'll find you get diminishing returns: fatigue will make you stupid, and eventually even damage your health. The point at which work yields diminishing returns depends on the type. Some of the hardest types you might only be able to do for four or five hours a day.

sentences.en: For example, while you must work hard, it's possible to work too hard, and if you do that you'll find you get diminishing returns: fatigue will make you stupid, and eventually even damage your health.
sentences.zh: 例如，虽然你必须努力工作，但也有可能工作得太辛苦，如果你这样做，你会发现你的回报递减：疲劳会让你变得愚蠢，最终甚至损害你的健康。

sentences.en: The point at which work yields diminishing returns depends on the type.
sentences.zh: 工作收益递减的点取决于工作类型。

sentences.en: Some of the hardest types you might only be able to do for four or five hours a day.
sentences.zh: 一些最难的类型你可能每天只能做四到五个小时。

blocks.html_en: Ideally those hours will be contiguous. To the extent you can, try to arrange your life so you have big blocks of time to work in. You'll shy away from hard tasks if you know you might be interrupted.

sentences.en: Ideally those hours will be contiguous.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，这些时间是连续的。

sentences.en: To the extent you can, try to arrange your life so you have big blocks of time to work in.
sentences.zh: 在力所能及的范围内，尽量安排好你的生活，这样你就有大量的时间可以用来工作。

sentences.en: You'll shy away from hard tasks if you know you might be interrupted.
sentences.zh: 如果您知道自己可能会被打扰，您就会回避艰巨的任务。

blocks.html_en: It will probably be harder to start working than to keep working. You'll often have to trick yourself to get over that initial threshold. Don't worry about this; it's the nature of work, not a flaw in your character. Work has a sort of activation energy, both per day and per project. And since this threshold is fake in the sense that it's higher than the energy required to keep going, it's ok to tell yourself a lie of corresponding magnitude to get over it.

sentences.en: It will probably be harder to start working than to keep working.
sentences.zh: 开始工作可能比继续工作更困难。

sentences.en: You'll often have to trick yourself to get over that initial threshold.
sentences.zh: 你经常需要欺骗自己才能跨过最初的门槛。

sentences.en: Don't worry about this; it's the nature of work, not a flaw in your character.
sentences.zh: 不用担心这个；这是工作的本质，而不是你性格上的缺陷。

sentences.en: Work has a sort of activation energy, both per day and per project.
sentences.zh: 工作有一种激活能量，无论是每天还是每个项目。

sentences.en: And since this threshold is fake in the sense that it's higher than the energy required to keep going, it's ok to tell yourself a lie of corresponding magnitude to get over it.
sentences.zh: 由于这个阈值是假的，因为它高于继续前进所需的能量，所以可以告诉自己相应大小的谎言来克服它。

blocks.html_en: It's usually a mistake to lie to yourself if you want to do great work, but this is one of the rare cases where it isn't. When I'm reluctant to start work in the morning, I often trick myself by saying "I'll just read over what I've got so far." Five minutes later I've found something that seems mistaken or incomplete, and I'm off.

sentences.en: It's usually a mistake to lie to yourself if you want to do great work, but this is one of the rare cases where it isn't.
sentences.zh: 如果你想做好工作，对自己撒谎通常是错误的，但这是极少数情况并非如此的情况之一。

sentences.en: When I'm reluctant to start work in the morning, I often trick myself by saying "I'll just read over what I've got so far."
sentences.zh: 当我早上不愿意开始工作时，我经常欺骗自己说：“我会读一下到目前为止所读到的内容。”

sentences.en: Five minutes later I've found something that seems mistaken or incomplete, and I'm off.
sentences.zh: 五分钟后，我发现了一些似乎错误或不完整的东西，然后我就离开了。

blocks.html_en: Similar techniques work for starting new projects. It's ok to lie to yourself about how much work a project will entail, for example. Lots of great things began with someone saying "How hard could it be?"

sentences.en: Similar techniques work for starting new projects.
sentences.zh: 类似的技术也适用于启动新项目。

sentences.en: It's ok to lie to yourself about how much work a project will entail, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，在一个项目需要多少工作量上对自己撒谎是可以的。

sentences.en: Lots of great things began with someone saying "How hard could it be?"
sentences.zh: 许多伟大的事情都是从有人说“这能有多难？”开始的。

blocks.html_en: This is one case where the young have an advantage. They're more optimistic, and even though one of the sources of their optimism is ignorance, in this case ignorance can sometimes beat knowledge.

sentences.en: This is one case where the young have an advantage.
sentences.zh: 这是年轻人具有优势的一个例子。

sentences.en: They're more optimistic, and even though one of the sources of their optimism is ignorance, in this case ignorance can sometimes beat knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他们更加乐观，尽管他们乐观的根源之一是无知，但在这种情况下，无知有时可以击败知识。

blocks.html_en: Try to finish what you start, though, even if it turns out to be more work than you expected. Finishing things is not just an exercise in tidiness or self-discipline. In many projects a lot of the best work happens in what was meant to be the final stage.

sentences.en: Try to finish what you start, though, even if it turns out to be more work than you expected.
sentences.zh: 不过，尝试完成你开始做的事情，即使结果比你预期的要多。

sentences.en: Finishing things is not just an exercise in tidiness or self-discipline.
sentences.zh: 完成事情不仅仅是一种整洁或自律的练习。

sentences.en: In many projects a lot of the best work happens in what was meant to be the final stage.
sentences.zh: 在许多项目中，许多最好的工作都发生在最后阶段。

blocks.html_en: Another permissible lie is to exaggerate the importance of what you're working on, at least in your own mind. If that helps you discover something new, it may turn out not to have been a lie after all.

sentences.en: Another permissible lie is to exaggerate the importance of what you're working on, at least in your own mind.
sentences.zh: 另一个允许的谎言是夸大你正在做的事情的重要性，至少在你自己看来是这样。

sentences.en: If that helps you discover something new, it may turn out not to have been a lie after all.
sentences.zh: 如果这能帮助你发现新的东西，那么它可能根本就不是谎言。

blocks.html_en: Since there are two senses of starting work — per day and per project — there are also two forms of procrastination. Per-project procrastination is far the more dangerous. You put off starting that ambitious project from year to year because the time isn't quite right. When you're procrastinating in units of years, you can get a lot not done.

sentences.en: Since there are two senses of starting work — per day and per project — there are also two forms of procrastination.
sentences.zh: 由于开始工作有两种感觉——每天和每个项目——所以拖延也有两种形式。

sentences.en: Per-project procrastination is far the more dangerous.
sentences.zh: 每个项目的拖延更加危险。

sentences.en: You put off starting that ambitious project from year to year because the time isn't quite right.
sentences.zh: 你年复一年地推迟启动这个雄心勃勃的项目，因为时间不太合适。

sentences.en: When you're procrastinating in units of years, you can get a lot not done.
sentences.zh: 当你以年为单位拖延时，你可能会做很多事情没有完成。

blocks.html_en: One reason per-project procrastination is so dangerous is that it usually camouflages itself as work. You're not just sitting around doing nothing; you're working industriously on something else. So per-project procrastination doesn't set off the alarms that per-day procrastination does. You're too busy to notice it.

sentences.en: One reason per-project procrastination is so dangerous is that it usually camouflages itself as work.
sentences.zh: 每个项目的拖延如此危险的原因之一是它通常将自己伪装成工作。

sentences.en: You're not just sitting around doing nothing; you're working industriously on something else.
sentences.zh: 你不只是坐在那里无所事事；你正在勤奋地做其他事情。

sentences.en: So per-project procrastination doesn't set off the alarms that per-day procrastination does.
sentences.zh: 因此，按项目拖延不会像按天拖延那样引发警报。

sentences.en: You're too busy to notice it.
sentences.zh: 你太忙了，没有注意到它。

blocks.html_en: The way to beat it is to stop occasionally and ask yourself: Am I working on what I most want to work on? When you're young it's ok if the answer is sometimes no, but this gets increasingly dangerous as you get older.

sentences.en: The way to beat it is to stop occasionally and ask yourself: Am I working on what I most want to work on?
sentences.zh: 战胜它的方法是偶尔停下来问自己：我正在做我最想做的事情吗？

sentences.en: When you're young it's ok if the answer is sometimes no, but this gets increasingly dangerous as you get older.
sentences.zh: 当你年轻的时候，如果答案有时是否定的，那也没关系，但随着年龄的增长，这会变得越来越危险。

blocks.html_en: Great work usually entails spending what would seem to most people an unreasonable amount of time on a problem. You can't think of this time as a cost, or it will seem too high. You have to find the work sufficiently engaging as it's happening.

sentences.en: Great work usually entails spending what would seem to most people an unreasonable amount of time on a problem.
sentences.zh: 伟大的工作通常需要在一个问题上花费对大多数人来说似乎不合理的时间。

sentences.en: You can't think of this time as a cost, or it will seem too high.
sentences.zh: 你不能把这个时间当成成本，不然会显得太高了。

sentences.en: You have to find the work sufficiently engaging as it's happening.
sentences.zh: 你必须发现这项工作在发生时足够有吸引力。

blocks.html_en: There may be some jobs where you have to work diligently for years at things you hate before you get to the good part, but this is not how great work happens. Great work happens by focusing consistently on something you're genuinely interested in. When you pause to take stock, you're surprised how far you've come.

sentences.en: There may be some jobs where you have to work diligently for years at things you hate before you get to the good part, but this is not how great work happens.
sentences.zh: 在某些工作中，你可能必须在你讨厌的事情上勤奋工作数年才能获得好的部分，但这并不是伟大工作的发生方式。

sentences.en: Great work happens by focusing consistently on something you're genuinely interested in.
sentences.zh: 伟大的工作是通过持续专注于你真正感兴趣的事情而实现的。

sentences.en: When you pause to take stock, you're surprised how far you've come.
sentences.zh: 当你停下来盘点一下时，你会惊讶地发现自己已经走了这么远。

blocks.html_en: The reason we're surprised is that we underestimate the cumulative effect of work. Writing a page a day doesn't sound like much, but if you do it every day you'll write a book a year. That's the key: consistency. People who do great things don't get a lot done every day. They get something done, rather than nothing.

sentences.en: The reason we're surprised is that we underestimate the cumulative effect of work.
sentences.zh: 我们感到惊讶的原因是我们低估了工作的累积效应。

sentences.en: Writing a page a day doesn't sound like much, but if you do it every day you'll write a book a year.
sentences.zh: 每天写一页听起来不多，但如果你每天都这样做，一年就可以写一本书。

sentences.en: That's the key: consistency.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键：一致性。

sentences.en: People who do great things don't get a lot done every day.
sentences.zh: 做伟大事情的人并不是每天都能完成很多事情。

sentences.en: They get something done, rather than nothing.
sentences.zh: 他们有所作为，而不是无所作为。

blocks.html_en: If you do work that compounds, you'll get exponential growth. Most people who do this do it unconsciously, but it's worth stopping to think about. Learning, for example, is an instance of this phenomenon: the more you learn about something, the easier it is to learn more. Growing an audience is another: the more fans you have, the more new fans they'll bring you.

sentences.en: If you do work that compounds, you'll get exponential growth.
sentences.zh: 如果你做复合性的工作，你就会获得指数级的增长。

sentences.en: Most people who do this do it unconsciously, but it's worth stopping to think about.
sentences.zh: 大多数这样做的人都是无意识的，但值得停下来思考一下。

sentences.en: Learning, for example, is an instance of this phenomenon: the more you learn about something, the easier it is to learn more.
sentences.zh: 例如，学习就是这种现象的一个例子：你对某事物了解得越多，就越容易学到更多。

sentences.en: Growing an audience is another: the more fans you have, the more new fans they'll bring you.
sentences.zh: 增加观众是另一回事：你拥有的粉丝越多，他们就会为你带来越多的新粉丝。

blocks.html_en: The trouble with exponential growth is that the curve feels flat in the beginning. It isn't; it's still a wonderful exponential curve. But we can't grasp that intuitively, so we underrate exponential growth in its early stages.

sentences.en: The trouble with exponential growth is that the curve feels flat in the beginning.
sentences.zh: 指数增长的问题在于，曲线一开始感觉平坦。

sentences.en: It isn't; it's still a wonderful exponential curve.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此；它仍然是一条美妙的指数曲线。

sentences.en: But we can't grasp that intuitively, so we underrate exponential growth in its early stages.
sentences.zh: 但我们无法直观地理解这一点，因此我们低估了早期的指数增长。

blocks.html_en: Something that grows exponentially can become so valuable that it's worth making an extraordinary effort to get it started. But since we underrate exponential growth early on, this too is mostly done unconsciously: people push through the initial, unrewarding phase of learning something new because they know from experience that learning new things always takes an initial push, or they grow their audience one fan at a time because they have nothing better to do. If people consciously realized they could invest in exponential growth, many more would do it.

sentences.en: Something that grows exponentially can become so valuable that it's worth making an extraordinary effort to get it started.
sentences.zh: 呈指数级增长的东西可能会变得非常有价值，以至于值得付出非凡的努力来开始它。

sentences.en: But since we underrate exponential growth early on, this too is mostly done unconsciously: people push through the initial, unrewarding phase of learning something new because they know from experience that learning new things always takes an initial push, or they grow their audience one fan at a time because they have nothing better to do.
sentences.zh: 但由于我们早期低估了指数增长，这也大多是无意识地完成的：人们在学习新东西的最初、无回报的阶段中坚持下去，因为他们从经验中知道学习新东西总是需要最初的推动，或者他们一次培养一个粉丝，因为他们没有更好的事情可做。

sentences.en: If people consciously realized they could invest in exponential growth, many more would do it.
sentences.zh: 如果人们有意识地意识到他们可以投资于指数级增长，就会有更多人这样做。

blocks.html_en: Work doesn't just happen when you're trying to. There's a kind of undirected thinking you do when walking or taking a shower or lying in bed that can be very powerful. By letting your mind wander a little, you'll often solve problems you were unable to solve by frontal attack.

sentences.en: Work doesn't just happen when you're trying to.
sentences.zh: 工作不会在你努力的时候发生。

sentences.en: There's a kind of undirected thinking you do when walking or taking a shower or lying in bed that can be very powerful.
sentences.zh: 当你走路、洗澡或躺在床上时，你会产生一种非常强大的无向思维。

sentences.en: By letting your mind wander a little, you'll often solve problems you were unable to solve by frontal attack.
sentences.zh: 通过让你的思绪稍微游离一下，你通常会解决正面攻击无法解决的问题。
