blocks.html_en: You have to be working hard in the normal way to benefit from this phenomenon, though. You can't just walk around daydreaming. The daydreaming has to be interleaved with deliberate work that feeds it questions.

sentences.en: You have to be working hard in the normal way to benefit from this phenomenon, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，你必须以正常的方式努力工作才能从这种现象中受益。

sentences.en: You can't just walk around daydreaming.
sentences.zh: 你不能只是到处走走做白日梦。

sentences.en: The daydreaming has to be interleaved with deliberate work that feeds it questions.
sentences.zh: 白日梦必须与那些为其提出问题的深思熟虑的工作交织在一起。

blocks.html_en: Everyone knows to avoid distractions at work, but it's also important to avoid them in the other half of the cycle. When you let your mind wander, it wanders to whatever you care about most at that moment. So avoid the kind of distraction that pushes your work out of the top spot, or you'll waste this valuable type of thinking on the distraction instead. (Exception: Don't avoid love.)

sentences.en: Everyone knows to avoid distractions at work, but it's also important to avoid them in the other half of the cycle.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道在工作中避免分心，但在周期的另一半中避免分心也很重要。

sentences.en: When you let your mind wander, it wanders to whatever you care about most at that moment.
sentences.zh: 当你让你的思绪游离时，它就会飘到你当时最关心的事情上。

sentences.en: So avoid the kind of distraction that pushes your work out of the top spot, or you'll waste this valuable type of thinking on the distraction instead.
sentences.zh: 因此，要避免那种让你的工作失去优势的干扰，否则你就会把这种宝贵的思考浪费在干扰上。

sentences.en: (Exception: Don't avoid love.)
sentences.zh: （例外：不要回避爱。）

blocks.html_en: Consciously cultivate your taste in the work done in your field. Until you know which is the best and what makes it so, you don't know what you're aiming for.

sentences.en: Consciously cultivate your taste in the work done in your field.
sentences.zh: 有意识地培养你对自己领域工作的品味。

sentences.en: Until you know which is the best and what makes it so, you don't know what you're aiming for.
sentences.zh: 除非您知道哪一个是最好的以及是什么让它如此，否则您不知道自己的目标是什么。

blocks.html_en: And that is what you're aiming for, because if you don't try to be the best, you won't even be good. This observation has been made by so many people in so many different fields that it might be worth thinking about why it's true. It could be because ambition is a phenomenon where almost all the error is in one direction — where almost all the shells that miss the target miss by falling short. Or it could be because ambition to be the best is a qualitatively different thing from ambition to be good. Or maybe being good is simply too vague a standard. Probably all three are true.

sentences.en: And that is what you're aiming for, because if you don't try to be the best, you won't even be good.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的目标，因为如果你不努力成为最好的，你就不会优秀。

sentences.en: This observation has been made by so many people in so many different fields that it might be worth thinking about why it's true.
sentences.zh: 许多不同领域的许多人都做出了这一观察，因此可能值得思考为什么它是正确的。

sentences.en: It could be because ambition is a phenomenon where almost all the error is in one direction — where almost all the shells that miss the target miss by falling short.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为野心是一种现象，几乎所有的错误都在一个方向上——几乎所有未击中目标的炮弹都因未能达到目标而错过。

sentences.en: Or it could be because ambition to be the best is a qualitatively different thing from ambition to be good.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是因为“成为最好的”的野心与“成为优秀的人”的野心有本质上的不同。

sentences.en: Or maybe being good is simply too vague a standard.
sentences.zh: 或者，也许“善良”这个标准太模糊了。

sentences.en: Probably all three are true.
sentences.zh: 也许这三个都是真的。

blocks.html_en: Fortunately there's a kind of economy of scale here. Though it might seem like you'd be taking on a heavy burden by trying to be the best, in practice you often end up net ahead. It's exciting, and also strangely liberating. It simplifies things. In some ways it's easier to try to be the best than to try merely to be good.

sentences.en: Fortunately there's a kind of economy of scale here.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，这里有一种规模经济。

sentences.en: Though it might seem like you'd be taking on a heavy burden by trying to be the best, in practice you often end up net ahead.
sentences.zh: 虽然看起来你会因为努力成为最好而承担沉重的负担，但实际上你常常最终会取得净领先。

sentences.en: It's exciting, and also strangely liberating.
sentences.zh: 这很令人兴奋，也有一种奇怪的解放感。

sentences.en: It simplifies things.
sentences.zh: 它简化了事情。

sentences.en: In some ways it's easier to try to be the best than to try merely to be good.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，努力成为最好的人比仅仅努力成为优秀的人更容易。

blocks.html_en: One way to aim high is to try to make something that people will care about in a hundred years. Not because their opinions matter more than your contemporaries', but because something that still seems good in a hundred years is more likely to be genuinely good.

sentences.en: One way to aim high is to try to make something that people will care about in a hundred years.
sentences.zh: 实现远大目标的一种方法是尝试做出一百年后人们会关心的东西。

sentences.en: Not because their opinions matter more than your contemporaries', but because something that still seems good in a hundred years is more likely to be genuinely good.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为他们的观点比同时代人的观点更重要，而是因为一百年后看起来仍然不错的东西更有可能是真正的好东西。

blocks.html_en: Don't try to work in a distinctive style. Just try to do the best job you can; you won't be able to help doing it in a distinctive way.

sentences.en: Don't try to work in a distinctive style.
sentences.zh: 不要尝试以独特的风格工作。

sentences.en: Just try to do the best job you can; you won't be able to help doing it in a distinctive way.
sentences.zh: 尽力把工作做到最好；你将无法帮助以一种独特的方式来做这件事。

blocks.html_en: Style is doing things in a distinctive way without trying to. Trying to is affectation.

sentences.en: Style is doing things in a distinctive way without trying to.
sentences.zh: 风格是以一种独特的方式做事而不是尝试。

sentences.en: Trying to is affectation.
sentences.zh: 尝试就是做作。

blocks.html_en: Affectation is in effect to pretend that someone other than you is doing the work. You adopt an impressive but fake persona, and while you're pleased with the impressiveness, the fakeness is what shows in the work.

sentences.en: Affectation is in effect to pretend that someone other than you is doing the work.
sentences.zh: 装腔作势实际上是假装是别人在做这项工作，而不是你。

sentences.en: You adopt an impressive but fake persona, and while you're pleased with the impressiveness, the fakeness is what shows in the work.
sentences.zh: 你采用了一个令人印象深刻但虚假的角色，虽然你对这种印象很满意，但作品中却表现出了虚假。

blocks.html_en: The temptation to be someone else is greatest for the young. They often feel like nobodies. But you never need to worry about that problem, because it's self-solving if you work on sufficiently ambitious projects. If you succeed at an ambitious project, you're not a nobody; you're the person who did it. So just do the work and your identity will take care of itself.

sentences.en: The temptation to be someone else is greatest for the young.
sentences.zh: 对于年轻人来说，成为别人的诱惑是最大的。

sentences.en: They often feel like nobodies.
sentences.zh: 他们常常感觉自己无名小卒。

sentences.en: But you never need to worry about that problem, because it's self-solving if you work on sufficiently ambitious projects.
sentences.zh: 但你永远不需要担心这个问题，因为如果你从事足够雄心勃勃的项目，它是可以自行解决的。

sentences.en: If you succeed at an ambitious project, you're not a nobody; you're the person who did it.
sentences.zh: 如果你在一个雄心勃勃的项目上取得了成功，那么你就不再是一个无名小卒；而是一个无名小卒。你就是做这件事的人。

sentences.en: So just do the work and your identity will take care of itself.
sentences.zh: 因此，只要做好工作，你的身份就会水到渠成。

blocks.html_en: "Avoid affectation" is a useful rule so far as it goes, but how would you express this idea positively? How would you say what to be, instead of what not to be? The best answer is earnest. If you're earnest you avoid not just affectation but a whole set of similar vices.

sentences.en: "Avoid affectation" is a useful rule so far as it goes, but how would you express this idea positively?
sentences.zh: 就目前而言，“避免矫揉造作”是一条有用的规则，但你会如何积极地表达这个想法呢？

sentences.en: How would you say what to be, instead of what not to be?
sentences.zh: 你会如何说应该做什么，而不是不应该做什么？

sentences.en: The best answer is earnest.
sentences.zh: 最好的回答是认真的。

sentences.en: If you're earnest you avoid not just affectation but a whole set of similar vices.
sentences.zh: 如果你真诚，你不仅可以避免做作，还可以避免一整套类似的恶习。

blocks.html_en: The core of being earnest is being intellectually honest. We're taught as children to be honest as an unselfish virtue — as a kind of sacrifice. But in fact it's a source of power too. To see new ideas, you need an exceptionally sharp eye for the truth. You're trying to see more truth than others have seen so far. And how can you have a sharp eye for the truth if you're intellectually dishonest?

sentences.en: The core of being earnest is being intellectually honest.
sentences.zh: 认真的核心是理智上的诚实。

sentences.en: We're taught as children to be honest as an unselfish virtue — as a kind of sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 我们从小就被教导要诚实，这是一种无私的美德，也是一种牺牲。

sentences.en: But in fact it's a source of power too.
sentences.zh: 但事实上它也是一种力量的来源。

sentences.en: To see new ideas, you need an exceptionally sharp eye for the truth.
sentences.zh: 要看到新的想法，你需要有一双敏锐的眼睛来发现真相。

sentences.en: You're trying to see more truth than others have seen so far.
sentences.zh: 你正试图看到比其他人迄今为止看到的更多的真相。

sentences.en: And how can you have a sharp eye for the truth if you're intellectually dishonest?
sentences.zh: 如果你在智力上不诚实，你怎么能有敏锐的洞察力呢？

blocks.html_en: One way to avoid intellectual dishonesty is to maintain a slight positive pressure in the opposite direction. Be aggressively willing to admit that you're mistaken. Once you've admitted you were mistaken about something, you're free. Till then you have to carry it.

sentences.en: One way to avoid intellectual dishonesty is to maintain a slight positive pressure in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 避免智力欺诈的一种方法是在相反方向保持轻微的正压力。

sentences.en: Be aggressively willing to admit that you're mistaken.
sentences.zh: 积极主动地承认自己的错误。

sentences.en: Once you've admitted you were mistaken about something, you're free.
sentences.zh: 一旦你承认自己在某件事上犯了错误，你就自由了。

sentences.en: Till then you have to carry it.
sentences.zh: 到那时你必须携带它。

blocks.html_en: Another more subtle component of earnestness is informality. Informality is much more important than its grammatically negative name implies. It's not merely the absence of something. It means focusing on what matters instead of what doesn't.

sentences.en: Another more subtle component of earnestness is informality.
sentences.zh: 真诚的另一个更微妙的组成部分是非正式的。

sentences.en: Informality is much more important than its grammatically negative name implies.
sentences.zh: 非正式性比其语法上否定的名称所暗示的重要得多。

sentences.en: It's not merely the absence of something.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是缺少某些东西。

sentences.en: It means focusing on what matters instead of what doesn't.
sentences.zh: 这意味着专注于重要的事情，而不是不重要的事情。

blocks.html_en: What formality and affectation have in common is that as well as doing the work, you're trying to seem a certain way as you're doing it. But any energy that goes into how you seem comes out of being good. That's one reason nerds have an advantage in doing great work: they expend little effort on seeming anything. In fact that's basically the definition of a nerd.

sentences.en: What formality and affectation have in common is that as well as doing the work, you're trying to seem a certain way as you're doing it.
sentences.zh: 拘谨和矫揉造作的共同点是，除了工作之外，你还试图在工作中表现出某种特定的方式。

sentences.en: But any energy that goes into how you seem comes out of being good.
sentences.zh: 但任何影响你外表的能量都来自于善良。

sentences.en: That's one reason nerds have an advantage in doing great work: they expend little effort on seeming anything.
sentences.zh: 这就是书呆子在完成出色工作时具有优势的原因之一：他们很少花精力在外表上。

sentences.en: In fact that's basically the definition of a nerd.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这基本上就是书呆子的定义。

blocks.html_en: Nerds have a kind of innocent boldness that's exactly what you need in doing great work. It's not learned; it's preserved from childhood. So hold onto it. Be the one who puts things out there rather than the one who sits back and offers sophisticated-sounding criticisms of them. "It's easy to criticize" is true in the most literal sense, and the route to great work is never easy.

sentences.en: Nerds have a kind of innocent boldness that's exactly what you need in doing great work.
sentences.zh: 书呆子有一种天真的勇气，这正是你完成伟大工作所需要的。

sentences.en: It's not learned; it's preserved from childhood.
sentences.zh: 这不是学来的；它是从童年就保存下来的。

sentences.en: So hold onto it.
sentences.zh: 所以坚持下去。

sentences.en: Be the one who puts things out there rather than the one who sits back and offers sophisticated-sounding criticisms of them.
sentences.zh: 成为一个把事情摆出来的人，而不是一个袖手旁观并对其提出听起来复杂的批评的人。

sentences.en: "It's easy to criticize" is true in the most literal sense, and the route to great work is never easy.
sentences.zh: “批评很容易”这句话从字面上看是对的，而通往伟大工作的道路从来都不是一帆风顺的。

blocks.html_en: There may be some jobs where it's an advantage to be cynical and pessimistic, but if you want to do great work it's an advantage to be optimistic, even though that means you'll risk looking like a fool sometimes. There's an old tradition of doing the opposite. The Old Testament says it's better to keep quiet lest you look like a fool. But that's advice for seeming smart. If you actually want to discover new things, it's better to take the risk of telling people your ideas.

sentences.en: There may be some jobs where it's an advantage to be cynical and pessimistic, but if you want to do great work it's an advantage to be optimistic, even though that means you'll risk looking like a fool sometimes.
sentences.zh: 在某些工作中，愤世嫉俗和悲观可能是一种优势，但如果你想做好工作，乐观是一种优势，尽管这意味着你有时会冒着看起来像个傻瓜的风险。

sentences.en: There's an old tradition of doing the opposite.
sentences.zh: 有一种反其道而行之的古老传统。

sentences.en: The Old Testament says it's better to keep quiet lest you look like a fool.
sentences.zh: 旧约说最好保持安静，以免看起来像个傻瓜。

sentences.en: But that's advice for seeming smart.
sentences.zh: 但这是显得聪明的建议。

sentences.en: If you actually want to discover new things, it's better to take the risk of telling people your ideas.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想发现新事物，最好冒险告诉别人你的想法。

blocks.html_en: Some people are naturally earnest, and with others it takes a conscious effort. Either kind of earnestness will suffice. But I doubt it would be possible to do great work without being earnest. It's so hard to do even if you are. You don't have enough margin for error to accommodate the distortions introduced by being affected, intellectually dishonest, orthodox, fashionable, or cool.

sentences.en: Some people are naturally earnest, and with others it takes a conscious effort.
sentences.zh: 有些人天生就很认真，而另一些人则需要有意识的努力。

sentences.en: Either kind of earnestness will suffice.
sentences.zh: 任何一种认真就足够了。

sentences.en: But I doubt it would be possible to do great work without being earnest.
sentences.zh: 但我怀疑，如果不认真，就不可能做出伟大的工作。

sentences.en: It's so hard to do even if you are.
sentences.zh: 即使你是这样，也很难做到。

sentences.en: You don't have enough margin for error to accommodate the distortions introduced by being affected, intellectually dishonest, orthodox, fashionable, or cool.
sentences.zh: 你没有足够的容错余地来适应因受影响、智力上的不诚实、正统、时尚或酷而带来的扭曲。

blocks.html_en: Great work is consistent not only with who did it, but with itself. It's usually all of a piece. So if you face a decision in the middle of working on something, ask which choice is more consistent.

sentences.en: Great work is consistent not only with who did it, but with itself.
sentences.zh: 伟大的作品不仅与完成它的人一致，而且与它本身一致。

sentences.en: It's usually all of a piece.
sentences.zh: 通常都是一个整体。

sentences.en: So if you face a decision in the middle of working on something, ask which choice is more consistent.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在做某件事的过程中面临一个决定，问问哪个选择更一致。

blocks.html_en: You may have to throw things away and redo them. You won't necessarily have to, but you have to be willing to. And that can take some effort; when there's something you need to redo, status quo bias and laziness will combine to keep you in denial about it. To beat this ask: If I'd already made the change, would I want to revert to what I have now?

sentences.en: You may have to throw things away and redo them.
sentences.zh: 你可能不得不扔掉一些东西并重做它们。

sentences.en: You won't necessarily have to, but you have to be willing to.
sentences.zh: 你不一定必须这样做，但你必须愿意这样做。

sentences.en: And that can take some effort; when there's something you need to redo, status quo bias and laziness will combine to keep you in denial about it.
sentences.zh: 这可能需要一些努力；当你需要重做某些事情时，现状偏见和懒惰会让你否认它。

sentences.en: To beat this ask: If I'd already made the change, would I want to revert to what I have now?
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，请问：如果我已经做出了改变，我是否想恢复到现在的状态？

blocks.html_en: Have the confidence to cut. Don't keep something that doesn't fit just because you're proud of it, or because it cost you a lot of effort.

sentences.en: Have the confidence to cut.
sentences.zh: 有信心去剪。

sentences.en: Don't keep something that doesn't fit just because you're proud of it, or because it cost you a lot of effort.
sentences.zh: 不要仅仅因为一些不合适的东西让你感到自豪，或者因为它花费了你很多努力而保留它。

blocks.html_en: Indeed, in some kinds of work it's good to strip whatever you're doing to its essence. The result will be more concentrated; you'll understand it better; and you won't be able to lie to yourself about whether there's anything real there.

sentences.en: Indeed, in some kinds of work it's good to strip whatever you're doing to its essence.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在某些工作中，剥离你正在做的事情的本质是件好事。

sentences.en: The result will be more concentrated; you'll understand it better; and you won't be able to lie to yourself about whether there's anything real there.
sentences.zh: 结果会更集中；你会更好地理解它；你无法欺骗自己是否存在真实的东西。

blocks.html_en: Mathematical elegance may sound like a mere metaphor, drawn from the arts. That's what I thought when I first heard the term "elegant" applied to a proof. But now I suspect it's conceptually prior — that the main ingredient in artistic elegance is mathematical elegance. At any rate it's a useful standard well beyond math.

sentences.en: Mathematical elegance may sound like a mere metaphor, drawn from the arts.
sentences.zh: 数学的优雅听起来可能只是一个源自艺术的隐喻。

sentences.en: That's what I thought when I first heard the term "elegant" applied to a proof.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次听到“优雅”一词应用于证明时，我就是这么想的。

sentences.en: But now I suspect it's conceptually prior — that the main ingredient in artistic elegance is mathematical elegance.
sentences.zh: 但现在我怀疑它在概念上是先验的——艺术优雅的主要成分是数学优雅。

sentences.en: At any rate it's a useful standard well beyond math.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，它是一个远远超出数学范围的有用标准。

blocks.html_en: Elegance can be a long-term bet, though. Laborious solutions will often have more prestige in the short term. They cost a lot of effort and they're hard to understand, both of which impress people, at least temporarily.

sentences.en: Elegance can be a long-term bet, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，优雅可以是一个长期的赌注。

sentences.en: Laborious solutions will often have more prestige in the short term.
sentences.zh: 费力的解决方案往往会在短期内获得更高的威望。

sentences.en: They cost a lot of effort and they're hard to understand, both of which impress people, at least temporarily.
sentences.zh: 它们花费了大量的精力，而且很难理解，但这两点都给人留下了深刻的印象，至少是暂时的。

blocks.html_en: Whereas some of the very best work will seem like it took comparatively little effort, because it was in a sense already there. It didn't have to be built, just seen. It's a very good sign when it's hard to say whether you're creating something or discovering it.

sentences.en: Whereas some of the very best work will seem like it took comparatively little effort, because it was in a sense already there.
sentences.zh: 然而，一些最好的作品看起来似乎花费了相对较少的努力，因为它在某种意义上已经存在了。

sentences.en: It didn't have to be built, just seen.
sentences.zh: 它不必建造，只需观看即可。

sentences.en: It's a very good sign when it's hard to say whether you're creating something or discovering it.
sentences.zh: 当很难说你是在创造某些东西还是在发现它时，这是一个非常好的迹象。

blocks.html_en: When you're doing work that could be seen as either creation or discovery, err on the side of discovery. Try thinking of yourself as a mere conduit through which the ideas take their natural shape.

sentences.en: When you're doing work that could be seen as either creation or discovery, err on the side of discovery.
sentences.zh: 当你从事的工作既可以被视为创造，也可以被视为发现时，宁可犯探索的错误。

sentences.en: Try thinking of yourself as a mere conduit through which the ideas take their natural shape.
sentences.zh: 试着把自己想象成一个简单的渠道，通过这个渠道，想法自然形成。

blocks.html_en: (Strangely enough, one exception is the problem of choosing a problem to work on. This is usually seen as search, but in the best case it's more like creating something. In the best case you create the field in the process of exploring it.)

sentences.en: (Strangely enough, one exception is the problem of choosing a problem to work on.
sentences.zh: （奇怪的是，一个例外是选择要解决的问题的问题。

sentences.en: This is usually seen as search, but in the best case it's more like creating something.
sentences.zh: 这通常被视为搜索，但在最好的情况下它更像是创建一些东西。

sentences.en: In the best case you create the field in the process of exploring it.)
sentences.zh: 在最好的情况下，您在探索它的过程中创建了该领域。）

blocks.html_en: Similarly, if you're trying to build a powerful tool, make it gratuitously unrestrictive. A powerful tool almost by definition will be used in ways you didn't expect, so err on the side of eliminating restrictions, even if you don't know what the benefit will be.

sentences.en: Similarly, if you're trying to build a powerful tool, make it gratuitously unrestrictive.
sentences.zh: 同样，如果您想构建一个强大的工具，请使其不受限制。

sentences.en: A powerful tool almost by definition will be used in ways you didn't expect, so err on the side of eliminating restrictions, even if you don't know what the benefit will be.
sentences.zh: 一个强大的工具几乎从定义上讲就会以您意想不到的方式使用，所以最好宁可消除限制，即使您不知道这样做会带来什么好处。

blocks.html_en: Great work will often be tool-like in the sense of being something others build on. So it's a good sign if you're creating ideas that others could use, or exposing questions that others could answer. The best ideas have implications in many different areas.

sentences.en: Great work will often be tool-like in the sense of being something others build on.
sentences.zh: 伟大的作品往往就像工具一样，是其他人构建的基础。

sentences.en: So it's a good sign if you're creating ideas that others could use, or exposing questions that others could answer.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果您正在创造其他人可以使用的想法，或者提出其他人可以回答的问题，那么这是一个好兆头。

sentences.en: The best ideas have implications in many different areas.
sentences.zh: 最好的想法在许多不同领域都有影响。

blocks.html_en: If you express your ideas in the most general form, they'll be truer than you intended.

sentences.en: If you express your ideas in the most general form, they'll be truer than you intended.
sentences.zh: 如果你以最一般的形式表达你的想法，它们会比你想要的更真实。

blocks.html_en: True by itself is not enough, of course. Great ideas have to be true and new. And it takes a certain amount of ability to see new ideas even once you've learned enough to get to one of the frontiers of knowledge.

sentences.en: True by itself is not enough, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，真实本身还不够。

sentences.en: Great ideas have to be true and new.
sentences.zh: 伟大的想法必须是真实的和新颖的。

sentences.en: And it takes a certain amount of ability to see new ideas even once you've learned enough to get to one of the frontiers of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 即使您已经学到了足够多的知识以达到知识的前沿之一，也需要一定的能力才能看到​​新的想法。

blocks.html_en: In English we give this ability names like originality, creativity, and imagination. And it seems reasonable to give it a separate name, because it does seem to some extent a separate skill. It's possible to have a great deal of ability in other respects — to have a great deal of what's often called technical ability — and yet not have much of this.

sentences.en: In English we give this ability names like originality, creativity, and imagination.
sentences.zh: 在英语中，我们给这种能力起一些名字，比如原创性、创造力和想象力。

sentences.en: And it seems reasonable to give it a separate name, because it does seem to some extent a separate skill.
sentences.zh: 给它一个单独的名称似乎是合理的，因为它在某种程度上似乎确实是一个单独的技能。

sentences.en: It's possible to have a great deal of ability in other respects — to have a great deal of what's often called technical ability — and yet not have much of this.
sentences.zh: 有可能在其他方面拥有大量的能力——拥有大量通常所谓的技术能力——但在这方面却没有太多。

blocks.html_en: I've never liked the term "creative process." It seems misleading. Originality isn't a process, but a habit of mind. Original thinkers throw off new ideas about whatever they focus on, like an angle grinder throwing off sparks. They can't help it.

sentences.en: I've never liked the term "creative process."
sentences.zh: 我从来不喜欢“创意过程”这个词。

sentences.en: It seems misleading.
sentences.zh: 这似乎有误导性。

sentences.en: Originality isn't a process, but a habit of mind.
sentences.zh: 原创不是一个过程，而是一种思维习惯。

sentences.en: Original thinkers throw off new ideas about whatever they focus on, like an angle grinder throwing off sparks.
sentences.zh: 原创思想家对他们关注的任何事物都会抛出新的想法，就像角磨机抛出火花一样。

sentences.en: They can't help it.
sentences.zh: 他们无能为力。

blocks.html_en: If the thing they're focused on is something they don't understand very well, these new ideas might not be good. One of the most original thinkers I know decided to focus on dating after he got divorced. He knew roughly as much about dating as the average 15 year old, and the results were spectacularly colorful. But to see originality separated from expertise like that made its nature all the more clear.

sentences.en: If the thing they're focused on is something they don't understand very well, these new ideas might not be good.
sentences.zh: 如果他们关注的事情是他们不太理解的事情，那么这些新想法可能不好。

sentences.en: One of the most original thinkers I know decided to focus on dating after he got divorced.
sentences.zh: 我认识的一位最具原创性的思想家在离婚后决定专注于约会。

sentences.en: He knew roughly as much about dating as the average 15 year old, and the results were spectacularly colorful.
sentences.zh: 他对约会的了解与一般 15 岁的人大致相同，而且约会的结果也非常丰富多彩。

sentences.en: But to see originality separated from expertise like that made its nature all the more clear.
sentences.zh: 但看到原创性与专业知识如此分离，它的本质就变得更加清晰。

blocks.html_en: I don't know if it's possible to cultivate originality, but there are definitely ways to make the most of however much you have. For example, you're much more likely to have original ideas when you're working on something. Original ideas don't come from trying to have original ideas. They come from trying to build or understand something slightly too difficult.

sentences.en: I don't know if it's possible to cultivate originality, but there are definitely ways to make the most of however much you have.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是否有可能培养原创性，但肯定有方法可以充分利用你所拥有的一切。

sentences.en: For example, you're much more likely to have original ideas when you're working on something.
sentences.zh: 例如，当你在做某事时，你更有可能产生原创想法。

sentences.en: Original ideas don't come from trying to have original ideas.
sentences.zh: 原创想法并不是来自尝试拥有原创想法。

sentences.en: They come from trying to build or understand something slightly too difficult.
sentences.zh: 它们来自于尝试构建或理解一些稍微困难的东西。

blocks.html_en: Talking or writing about the things you're interested in is a good way to generate new ideas. When you try to put ideas into words, a missing idea creates a sort of vacuum that draws it out of you. Indeed, there's a kind of thinking that can only be done by writing.

sentences.en: Talking or writing about the things you're interested in is a good way to generate new ideas.
sentences.zh: 谈论或写下你感兴趣的事情是产生新想法的好方法。

sentences.en: When you try to put ideas into words, a missing idea creates a sort of vacuum that draws it out of you.
sentences.zh: 当你试图把想法变成文字时，一个缺失的想法会产生一种真空，将你的想法从你身上吸走。

sentences.en: Indeed, there's a kind of thinking that can only be done by writing.
sentences.zh: 确实，有一种思考只能通过写作来完成。

blocks.html_en: Changing your context can help. If you visit a new place, you'll often find you have new ideas there. The journey itself often dislodges them. But you may not have to go far to get this benefit. Sometimes it's enough just to go for a walk.

sentences.en: Changing your context can help.
sentences.zh: 改变你的背景会有帮助。

sentences.en: If you visit a new place, you'll often find you have new ideas there.
sentences.zh: 如果你去一个新地方，你经常会发现那里有新的想法。

sentences.en: The journey itself often dislodges them.
sentences.zh: 旅程本身常常让他们感到流离失所。

sentences.en: But you may not have to go far to get this benefit.
sentences.zh: 但您可能不需要走很远就能获得这种好处。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's enough just to go for a walk.
sentences.zh: 有时候，只是去散步就足够了。

blocks.html_en: It also helps to travel in topic space. You'll have more new ideas if you explore lots of different topics, partly because it gives the angle grinder more surface area to work on, and partly because analogies are an especially fruitful source of new ideas.

sentences.en: It also helps to travel in topic space.
sentences.zh: 它还有助于在主题空间中旅行。

sentences.en: You'll have more new ideas if you explore lots of different topics, partly because it gives the angle grinder more surface area to work on, and partly because analogies are an especially fruitful source of new ideas.
sentences.zh: 如果您探索许多不同的主题，您将会有更多的新想法，部分原因是它为角磨机提供了更多的工作空间，部分原因是类比是新想法特别富有成效的来源。

blocks.html_en: Don't divide your attention evenly between many topics though, or you'll spread yourself too thin. You want to distribute it according to something more like a power law.

sentences.en: Don't divide your attention evenly between many topics though, or you'll spread yourself too thin.
sentences.zh: 不过，不要将你的注意力平均分配到许多主题上，否则你的注意力就会分散。

sentences.en: You want to distribute it according to something more like a power law.
sentences.zh: 你想根据更像幂律的东西来分配它。

blocks.html_en: Curiosity and originality are closely related. Curiosity feeds originality by giving it new things to work on. But the relationship is closer than that. Curiosity is itself a kind of originality; it's roughly to questions what originality is to answers. And since questions at their best are a big component of answers, curiosity at its best is a creative force.

sentences.en: Curiosity and originality are closely related.
sentences.zh: 好奇心和原创性密切相关。

sentences.en: Curiosity feeds originality by giving it new things to work on.
sentences.zh: 好奇心通过给予新的工作机会来滋养原创性。

sentences.en: But the relationship is closer than that.
sentences.zh: 但关系比这更密切。

sentences.en: Curiosity is itself a kind of originality; it's roughly to questions what originality is to answers.
sentences.zh: 好奇心本身就是一种原创性；粗略地说，问题的原创性就是答案的原创性。

sentences.en: And since questions at their best are a big component of answers, curiosity at its best is a creative force.
sentences.zh: 由于问题在最好的情况下是答案的重要组成部分，因此好奇心在最好的情况下是一种创造力。

blocks.html_en: Having new ideas is a strange game, because it usually consists of seeing things that were right under your nose. Once you've seen a new idea, it tends to seem obvious. Why did no one think of this before?

sentences.en: Having new ideas is a strange game, because it usually consists of seeing things that were right under your nose.
sentences.zh: 产生新想法是一种奇怪的游戏，因为它通常包括看到就在你眼皮子底下的东西。

sentences.en: Once you've seen a new idea, it tends to seem obvious.
sentences.zh: 一旦你看到一个新想法，它往往看起来很明显。

sentences.en: Why did no one think of this before?
sentences.zh: 为什么以前没有人想到这一点？

blocks.html_en: When an idea seems simultaneously novel and obvious, it's probably a good one.

sentences.en: When an idea seems simultaneously novel and obvious, it's probably a good one.
sentences.zh: 当一个想法看起来既新颖又明显时，它可能是一个好想法。

blocks.html_en: Seeing something obvious sounds easy. And yet empirically having new ideas is hard. What's the source of this apparent contradiction? It's that seeing the new idea usually requires you to change the way you look at the world. We see the world through models that both help and constrain us. When you fix a broken model, new ideas become obvious. But noticing and fixing a broken model is hard. That's how new ideas can be both obvious and yet hard to discover: they're easy to see after you do something hard.

sentences.en: Seeing something obvious sounds easy.
sentences.zh: 看到明显的东西听起来很容易。

sentences.en: And yet empirically having new ideas is hard.
sentences.zh: 然而，凭经验获得新想法是很困难的。

sentences.en: What's the source of this apparent contradiction?
sentences.zh: 这种明显矛盾的根源是什么？

sentences.en: It's that seeing the new idea usually requires you to change the way you look at the world.
sentences.zh: 看到新想法通常需要你改变看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: We see the world through models that both help and constrain us.
sentences.zh: 我们通过既帮助又限制我们的模型来看待世界。

sentences.en: When you fix a broken model, new ideas become obvious.
sentences.zh: 当你修复损坏的模型时，新的想法就会变得显而易见。

sentences.en: But noticing and fixing a broken model is hard.
sentences.zh: 但发现并修复损坏的模型是很困难的。

sentences.en: That's how new ideas can be both obvious and yet hard to discover: they're easy to see after you do something hard.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么新想法既显而易见又难以发现：在你做了一些困难的事情之后，它们很容易被发现。

blocks.html_en: One way to discover broken models is to be stricter than other people. Broken models of the world leave a trail of clues where they bash against reality. Most people don't want to see these clues. It would be an understatement to say that they're attached to their current model; it's what they think in; so they'll tend to ignore the trail of clues left by its breakage, however conspicuous it may seem in retrospect.

sentences.en: One way to discover broken models is to be stricter than other people.
sentences.zh: 发现损坏模型的一种方法是比其他人更严格。

sentences.en: Broken models of the world leave a trail of clues where they bash against reality.
sentences.zh: 破碎的世界模型留下了与现实相悖的线索。

sentences.en: Most people don't want to see these clues.
sentences.zh: 大多数人不想看到这些线索。

sentences.en: It would be an understatement to say that they're attached to their current model; it's what they think in; so they'll tend to ignore the trail of clues left by its breakage, however conspicuous it may seem in retrospect.
sentences.zh: 轻描淡写地说，他们依附于当前的模式。这就是他们的想法；因此，他们往往会忽略其破损留下的线索，无论事后看来多么明显。

blocks.html_en: To find new ideas you have to seize on signs of breakage instead of looking away. That's what Einstein did. He was able to see the wild implications of Maxwell's equations not so much because he was looking for new ideas as because he was stricter.

sentences.en: To find new ideas you have to seize on signs of breakage instead of looking away.
sentences.zh: 为了找到新的想法，你必须抓住破损的迹象，而不是移开视线。

sentences.en: That's what Einstein did.
sentences.zh: 这就是爱因斯坦所做的。

sentences.en: He was able to see the wild implications of Maxwell's equations not so much because he was looking for new ideas as because he was stricter.
sentences.zh: 他能够看到麦克斯韦方程组的巨大含义，与其说是因为他在寻找新的想法，不如说是因为他更加严格。

blocks.html_en: The other thing you need is a willingness to break rules. Paradoxical as it sounds, if you want to fix your model of the world, it helps to be the sort of person who's comfortable breaking rules. From the point of view of the old model, which everyone including you initially shares, the new model usually breaks at least implicit rules.

sentences.en: The other thing you need is a willingness to break rules.
sentences.zh: 您需要的另一件事是愿意打破规则。

sentences.en: Paradoxical as it sounds, if you want to fix your model of the world, it helps to be the sort of person who's comfortable breaking rules.
sentences.zh: 尽管听起来很矛盾，但如果你想修复你的世界模型，成为那种乐于打破规则的人会有所帮助。

sentences.en: From the point of view of the old model, which everyone including you initially shares, the new model usually breaks at least implicit rules.
sentences.zh: 从包括你在内的每个人最初共享的旧模型的角度来看，新模型通常至少会打破隐含的规则。

blocks.html_en: Few understand the degree of rule-breaking required, because new ideas seem much more conservative once they succeed. They seem perfectly reasonable once you're using the new model of the world they brought with them. But they didn't at the time; it took the greater part of a century for the heliocentric model to be generally accepted, even among astronomers, because it felt so wrong.

sentences.en: Few understand the degree of rule-breaking required, because new ideas seem much more conservative once they succeed.
sentences.zh: 很少有人了解需要打破规则的程度，因为新想法一旦成功，就会显得更加保守。

sentences.en: They seem perfectly reasonable once you're using the new model of the world they brought with them.
sentences.zh: 一旦你使用他们带来的新世界模型，他们看起来就完全合理了。

sentences.en: But they didn't at the time; it took the greater part of a century for the heliocentric model to be generally accepted, even among astronomers, because it felt so wrong.
sentences.zh: 但他们当时并没有这么做；日心说模型花了大半个世纪才被普遍接受，甚至在天文学家中也是如此，因为它感觉非常错误。

blocks.html_en: Indeed, if you think about it, a good new idea has to seem bad to most people, or someone would have already explored it. So what you're looking for is ideas that seem crazy, but the right kind of crazy. How do you recognize these? You can't with certainty. Often ideas that seem bad are bad. But ideas that are the right kind of crazy tend to be exciting; they're rich in implications; whereas ideas that are merely bad tend to be depressing.

sentences.en: Indeed, if you think about it, a good new idea has to seem bad to most people, or someone would have already explored it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你仔细想想，一个好的新想法对大多数人来说一定是糟糕的，否则肯定有人已经探索过了。

sentences.en: So what you're looking for is ideas that seem crazy, but the right kind of crazy.
sentences.zh: 所以你要寻找的是看似疯狂但真正疯狂的想法。

sentences.en: How do you recognize these?
sentences.zh: 你如何认识这些？

sentences.en: You can't with certainty.
sentences.zh: 你不能肯定。

sentences.en: Often ideas that seem bad are bad.
sentences.zh: 通常看似糟糕的想法实际上是糟糕的。

sentences.en: But ideas that are the right kind of crazy tend to be exciting; they're rich in implications; whereas ideas that are merely bad tend to be depressing.
sentences.zh: 但真正疯狂的想法往往会令人兴奋。它们蕴含着丰富的含义；而仅仅糟糕的想法往往会令人沮丧。

blocks.html_en: There are two ways to be comfortable breaking rules: to enjoy breaking them, and to be indifferent to them. I call these two cases being aggressively and passively independent-minded.

sentences.en: There are two ways to be comfortable breaking rules: to enjoy breaking them, and to be indifferent to them.
sentences.zh: 有两种方法可以让你轻松地打破规则：享受打破规则的乐趣，以及对规则漠不关心。

sentences.en: I call these two cases being aggressively and passively independent-minded.
sentences.zh: 我将这两种情况称为主动独立思想和被动独立思想。

blocks.html_en: The aggressively independent-minded are the naughty ones. Rules don't merely fail to stop them; breaking rules gives them additional energy. For this sort of person, delight at the sheer audacity of a project sometimes supplies enough activation energy to get it started.

sentences.en: The aggressively independent-minded are the naughty ones.
sentences.zh: 具有积极独立思想的人是顽皮的人。

sentences.en: Rules don't merely fail to stop them; breaking rules gives them additional energy.
sentences.zh: 规则不仅不能阻止它们，而且还能阻止它们。打破规则会给他们额外的能量。

sentences.en: For this sort of person, delight at the sheer audacity of a project sometimes supplies enough activation energy to get it started.
sentences.zh: 对于这类人来说，对一个项目的纯粹大胆感到高兴有时会提供足够的激活能量来开始它。

blocks.html_en: The other way to break rules is not to care about them, or perhaps even to know they exist. This is why novices and outsiders often make new discoveries; their ignorance of a field's assumptions acts as a source of temporary passive independent-mindedness. Aspies also seem to have a kind of immunity to conventional beliefs. Several I know say that this helps them to have new ideas.

sentences.en: The other way to break rules is not to care about them, or perhaps even to know they exist.
sentences.zh: 打破规则的另一种方法是不关心它们，甚至不知道它们的存在。

sentences.en: This is why novices and outsiders often make new discoveries; their ignorance of a field's assumptions acts as a source of temporary passive independent-mindedness.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么新手和局外人经常会有新的发现；他们对某个领域的假设的无知是暂时被动独立思想的根源。

sentences.en: Aspies also seem to have a kind of immunity to conventional beliefs.
sentences.zh: 阿斯皮似乎对传统信仰也有一定的免疫力。

sentences.en: Several I know say that this helps them to have new ideas.
sentences.zh: 我认识的几个人说这有助于他们产生新想法。

blocks.html_en: Strictness plus rule-breaking sounds like a strange combination. In popular culture they're opposed. But popular culture has a broken model in this respect. It implicitly assumes that issues are trivial ones, and in trivial matters strictness and rule-breaking are opposed. But in questions that really matter, only rule-breakers can be truly strict.

sentences.en: Strictness plus rule-breaking sounds like a strange combination.
sentences.zh: 严格加上违反规则听起来是一个奇怪的组合。

sentences.en: In popular culture they're opposed.
sentences.zh: 在流行文化中，他们是反对的。

sentences.en: But popular culture has a broken model in this respect.
sentences.zh: 但流行文化在这方面的模式已经被打破。

sentences.en: It implicitly assumes that issues are trivial ones, and in trivial matters strictness and rule-breaking are opposed.
sentences.zh: 它隐含地假定问题是琐碎的，在琐碎的事情上反对严格和破坏规则。

sentences.en: But in questions that really matter, only rule-breakers can be truly strict.
sentences.zh: 但在真正重要的问题上，只有打破规则的人才能真正严格。

blocks.html_en: An overlooked idea often doesn't lose till the semifinals. You do see it, subconsciously, but then another part of your subconscious shoots it down because it would be too weird, too risky, too much work, too controversial. This suggests an exciting possibility: if you could turn off such filters, you could see more new ideas.

sentences.en: An overlooked idea often doesn't lose till the semifinals.
sentences.zh: 一个被忽视的想法往往直到半决赛才输。

sentences.en: You do see it, subconsciously, but then another part of your subconscious shoots it down because it would be too weird, too risky, too much work, too controversial.
sentences.zh: 你确实在潜意识中看到了它，但你潜意识的另一部分却将其否决，因为它太奇怪、太冒险、太多工作、太有争议。

sentences.en: This suggests an exciting possibility: if you could turn off such filters, you could see more new ideas.
sentences.zh: 这表明了一个令人兴奋的可能性：如果你可以关闭此类过滤器，你可以看到更多新想法。

blocks.html_en: One way to do that is to ask what would be good ideas for someone else to explore. Then your subconscious won't shoot them down to protect you.

sentences.en: One way to do that is to ask what would be good ideas for someone else to explore.
sentences.zh: 一种方法是询问其他人有什么好的想法可以探索。

sentences.en: Then your subconscious won't shoot them down to protect you.
sentences.zh: 那么你的潜意识就不会为了保护你而击落它们。

blocks.html_en: You could also discover overlooked ideas by working in the other direction: by starting from what's obscuring them. Every cherished but mistaken principle is surrounded by a dead zone of valuable ideas that are unexplored because they contradict it.

sentences.en: You could also discover overlooked ideas by working in the other direction: by starting from what's obscuring them.
sentences.zh: 您还可以通过朝另一个方向努力来发现被忽视的想法：从掩盖它们的事物开始。

sentences.en: Every cherished but mistaken principle is surrounded by a dead zone of valuable ideas that are unexplored because they contradict it.
sentences.zh: 每一个被珍视但被错误的原则都被有价值的想法的死区所包围，这些想法因为与原则相矛盾而未被探索。

blocks.html_en: Religions are collections of cherished but mistaken principles. So anything that can be described either literally or metaphorically as a religion will have valuable unexplored ideas in its shadow. Copernicus and Darwin both made discoveries of this type.

sentences.en: Religions are collections of cherished but mistaken principles.
sentences.zh: 宗教是珍视但错误的原则的集合。

sentences.en: So anything that can be described either literally or metaphorically as a religion will have valuable unexplored ideas in its shadow.
sentences.zh: 因此，任何可以从字面上或隐喻上描述为宗教的事物，都将在其阴影下蕴藏着有价值的、未经探索的思想。

sentences.en: Copernicus and Darwin both made discoveries of this type.
sentences.zh: 哥白尼和达尔文都做出了此类发现。

blocks.html_en: What are people in your field religious about, in the sense of being too attached to some principle that might not be as self-evident as they think? What becomes possible if you discard it?

sentences.en: What are people in your field religious about, in the sense of being too attached to some principle that might not be as self-evident as they think?
sentences.zh: 在你的领域里，人们对什么有宗教信仰，即过于执着于某些可能并不像他们想象的那么不言自明的原则？

sentences.en: What becomes possible if you discard it?
sentences.zh: 如果你放弃它，会发生什么？

blocks.html_en: People show much more originality in solving problems than in deciding which problems to solve. Even the smartest can be surprisingly conservative when deciding what to work on. People who'd never dream of being fashionable in any other way get sucked into working on fashionable problems.

sentences.en: People show much more originality in solving problems than in deciding which problems to solve.
sentences.zh: 人们在解决问题时比在决定解决哪些问题时表现出更多的独创性。

sentences.en: Even the smartest can be surprisingly conservative when deciding what to work on.
sentences.zh: 即使是最聪明的人在决定做什么时也会出人意料地保守。

sentences.en: People who'd never dream of being fashionable in any other way get sucked into working on fashionable problems.
sentences.zh: 那些从来没有梦想以任何其他方式变得时尚的人会沉迷于解决时尚问题。

blocks.html_en: One reason people are more conservative when choosing problems than solutions is that problems are bigger bets. A problem could occupy you for years, while exploring a solution might only take days. But even so I think most people are too conservative. They're not merely responding to risk, but to fashion as well. Unfashionable problems are undervalued.

sentences.en: One reason people are more conservative when choosing problems than solutions is that problems are bigger bets.
sentences.zh: 人们在选择问题而不是解决方案时更加保守的原因之一是，问题是更大的赌注。

sentences.en: A problem could occupy you for years, while exploring a solution might only take days.
sentences.zh: 一个问题可能会花费你数年的时间，而探索解决方案可能只需要几天的时间。

sentences.en: But even so I think most people are too conservative.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此我认为大多数人都过于保守。

sentences.en: They're not merely responding to risk, but to fashion as well.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅要应对风险，还要应对时尚。

sentences.en: Unfashionable problems are undervalued.
sentences.zh: 不流行的问题被低估了。

blocks.html_en: One of the most interesting kinds of unfashionable problem is the problem that people think has been fully explored, but hasn't. Great work often takes something that already exists and shows its latent potential. Durer and Watt both did this. So if you're interested in a field that others think is tapped out, don't let their skepticism deter you. People are often wrong about this.

sentences.en: One of the most interesting kinds of unfashionable problem is the problem that people think has been fully explored, but hasn't.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的一种不流行的问题是人们认为已经得到充分探索但实际上还没有的问题。

sentences.en: Great work often takes something that already exists and shows its latent potential.
sentences.zh: 伟大的作品往往需要一些已经存在的东西并展示其潜在的潜力。

sentences.en: Durer and Watt both did this.
sentences.zh: 丢勒和瓦特都做到了这一点。

sentences.en: So if you're interested in a field that others think is tapped out, don't let their skepticism deter you.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你对别人认为已经开发出来的领域感兴趣，不要让他们的怀疑阻止你。

sentences.en: People are often wrong about this.
sentences.zh: 人们在这一点上常常是错误的。

blocks.html_en: Working on an unfashionable problem can be very pleasing. There's no hype or hurry. Opportunists and critics are both occupied elsewhere. The existing work often has an old-school solidity. And there's a satisfying sense of economy in cultivating ideas that would otherwise be wasted.

sentences.en: Working on an unfashionable problem can be very pleasing.
sentences.zh: 解决一个不流行的问题可能会非常令人愉快。

sentences.en: There's no hype or hurry.
sentences.zh: 没有炒作或匆忙。

sentences.en: Opportunists and critics are both occupied elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 机会主义者和批评家都忙于别处。

sentences.en: The existing work often has an old-school solidity.
sentences.zh: 现有的作品通常具有老式的坚固性。

sentences.en: And there's a satisfying sense of economy in cultivating ideas that would otherwise be wasted.
sentences.zh: 培养原本会被浪费的创意，会带来一种令人满意的节约感。

blocks.html_en: But the most common type of overlooked problem is not explicitly unfashionable in the sense of being out of fashion. It just doesn't seem to matter as much as it actually does. How do you find these? By being self-indulgent — by letting your curiosity have its way, and tuning out, at least temporarily, the little voice in your head that says you should only be working on "important" problems.

sentences.en: But the most common type of overlooked problem is not explicitly unfashionable in the sense of being out of fashion.
sentences.zh: 但最常见的被忽视的问题并不是从过时的意义上来说明显不时尚。

sentences.en: It just doesn't seem to matter as much as it actually does.
sentences.zh: 它看起来并不像实际那么重要。

sentences.en: How do you find these?
sentences.zh: 你如何找到这些？

sentences.en: By being self-indulgent — by letting your curiosity have its way, and tuning out, at least temporarily, the little voice in your head that says you should only be working on "important" problems.
sentences.zh: 通过自我放纵——让你的好奇心发挥作用，至少暂时忽略你头脑中那个说你应该只研究“重要”问题的小声音。

blocks.html_en: You do need to work on important problems, but almost everyone is too conservative about what counts as one. And if there's an important but overlooked problem in your neighborhood, it's probably already on your subconscious radar screen. So try asking yourself: if you were going to take a break from "serious" work to work on something just because it would be really interesting, what would you do? The answer is probably more important than it seems.

sentences.en: You do need to work on important problems, but almost everyone is too conservative about what counts as one.
sentences.zh: 你确实需要解决重要的问题，但几乎每个人对于什么算作“一”都过于保守。

sentences.en: And if there's an important but overlooked problem in your neighborhood, it's probably already on your subconscious radar screen.
sentences.zh: 如果您的社区存在一个重要但被忽视的问题，它可能已经出现在您的潜意识雷达屏幕上。

sentences.en: So try asking yourself: if you were going to take a break from "serious" work to work on something just because it would be really interesting, what would you do?
sentences.zh: 所以试着问问自己：如果你打算从“严肃”的工作中休息一下，去做某件事，只是因为它真的很有趣，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: The answer is probably more important than it seems.
sentences.zh: 答案可能比看起来更重要。

blocks.html_en: Originality in choosing problems seems to matter even more than originality in solving them. That's what distinguishes the people who discover whole new fields. So what might seem to be merely the initial step — deciding what to work on — is in a sense the key to the whole game.

sentences.en: Originality in choosing problems seems to matter even more than originality in solving them.
sentences.zh: 选择问题的独创性似乎比解决问题的独创性更重要。

sentences.en: That's what distinguishes the people who discover whole new fields.
sentences.zh: 这就是发现全新领域的人们的独特之处。

sentences.en: So what might seem to be merely the initial step — deciding what to work on — is in a sense the key to the whole game.
sentences.zh: 因此，看似只是第一步——决定做什么——在某种意义上是整个游戏的关键。

blocks.html_en: Few grasp this. One of the biggest misconceptions about new ideas is about the ratio of question to answer in their composition. People think big ideas are answers, but often the real insight was in the question.

sentences.en: Few grasp this.
sentences.zh: 很少有人明白这一点。

sentences.en: One of the biggest misconceptions about new ideas is about the ratio of question to answer in their composition.
sentences.zh: 对新想法最大的误解之一是其作文中问题与答案的比例。

sentences.en: People think big ideas are answers, but often the real insight was in the question.
sentences.zh: 人们认为伟大的想法就是答案，但真正的洞察力往往存在于问题之中。

blocks.html_en: Part of the reason we underrate questions is the way they're used in schools. In schools they tend to exist only briefly before being answered, like unstable particles. But a really good question can be much more than that. A really good question is a partial discovery. How do new species arise? Is the force that makes objects fall to earth the same as the one that keeps planets in their orbits? By even asking such questions you were already in excitingly novel territory.

sentences.en: Part of the reason we underrate questions is the way they're used in schools.
sentences.zh: 我们低估问题的部分原因是它们在学校中的使用方式。

sentences.en: In schools they tend to exist only briefly before being answered, like unstable particles.
sentences.zh: 在学校里，它们往往只存在很短的时间，然后就得到答案，就像不稳定的粒子一样。

sentences.en: But a really good question can be much more than that.
sentences.zh: 但一个真正好的问题可以远不止于此。

sentences.en: A really good question is a partial discovery.
sentences.zh: 一个真正好的问题是部分发现。

sentences.en: How do new species arise?
sentences.zh: 新物种是如何产生的？

sentences.en: Is the force that makes objects fall to earth the same as the one that keeps planets in their orbits?
sentences.zh: 使物体坠落地球的力与使行星保持在其轨道上的力相同吗？

sentences.en: By even asking such questions you were already in excitingly novel territory.
sentences.zh: 即使问了这样的问题，你就已经进入了令人兴奋的新领域。

blocks.html_en: Unanswered questions can be uncomfortable things to carry around with you. But the more you're carrying, the greater the chance of noticing a solution — or perhaps even more excitingly, noticing that two unanswered questions are the same.

sentences.en: Unanswered questions can be uncomfortable things to carry around with you.
sentences.zh: 随身携带未解答的问题可能会让您感到不舒服。

sentences.en: But the more you're carrying, the greater the chance of noticing a solution — or perhaps even more excitingly, noticing that two unanswered questions are the same.
sentences.zh: 但你携带的东西越多，发现解决方案的机会就越大——或者更令人兴奋的是，发现两个未解答的问题是相同的。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes you carry a question for a long time. Great work often comes from returning to a question you first noticed years before — in your childhood, even — and couldn't stop thinking about. People talk a lot about the importance of keeping your youthful dreams alive, but it's just as important to keep your youthful questions alive.

sentences.en: Sometimes you carry a question for a long time.
sentences.zh: 有时你会带着一个问题很长时间。

sentences.en: Great work often comes from returning to a question you first noticed years before — in your childhood, even — and couldn't stop thinking about.
sentences.zh: 伟大的工作往往来自于回到你几年前第一次注意到的问题——甚至是在你的童年——并且无法停止思考。

sentences.en: People talk a lot about the importance of keeping your youthful dreams alive, but it's just as important to keep your youthful questions alive.
sentences.zh: 人们经常谈论保持年轻时的梦想的重要性，但保持年轻时的问题也同样重要。

blocks.html_en: This is one of the places where actual expertise differs most from the popular picture of it. In the popular picture, experts are certain. But actually the more puzzled you are, the better, so long as (a) the things you're puzzled about matter, and (b) no one else understands them either.

sentences.en: This is one of the places where actual expertise differs most from the popular picture of it.
sentences.zh: 这是实际专业知识与流行图片最不同的地方之一。

sentences.en: In the popular picture, experts are certain.
sentences.zh: 在流行的图景中，专家们是肯定的。

sentences.en: But actually the more puzzled you are, the better, so long as (a) the things you're puzzled about matter, and (b) no one else understands them either.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你越困惑越好，只要（a）你感到困惑的事情很重要，并且（b）其他人也没有理解它们。

blocks.html_en: Think about what's happening at the moment just before a new idea is discovered. Often someone with sufficient expertise is puzzled about something. Which means that originality consists partly of puzzlement — of confusion! You have to be comfortable enough with the world being full of puzzles that you're willing to see them, but not so comfortable that you don't want to solve them.

sentences.en: Think about what's happening at the moment just before a new idea is discovered.
sentences.zh: 想想在发现新想法之前此刻正在发生什么。

sentences.en: Often someone with sufficient expertise is puzzled about something.
sentences.zh: 具有足够专业知识的人常常会对某些事情感到困惑。

sentences.en: Which means that originality consists partly of puzzlement — of confusion!
sentences.zh: 这意味着原创性部分地包含着困惑——混乱！

sentences.en: You have to be comfortable enough with the world being full of puzzles that you're willing to see them, but not so comfortable that you don't want to solve them.
sentences.zh: 你必须对这个充满谜题的世界感到足够舒服，以至于你愿意看到它们，但又不能太舒服以至于你不想解决它们。

blocks.html_en: It's a great thing to be rich in unanswered questions. And this is one of those situations where the rich get richer, because the best way to acquire new questions is to try answering existing ones. Questions don't just lead to answers, but also to more questions.

sentences.en: It's a great thing to be rich in unanswered questions.
sentences.zh: 拥有大量未解答的问题是一件很棒的事情。

sentences.en: And this is one of those situations where the rich get richer, because the best way to acquire new questions is to try answering existing ones.
sentences.zh: 这是富人变得更富的情况之一，因为获得新问题的最佳方法是尝试回答现有问题。

sentences.en: Questions don't just lead to answers, but also to more questions.
sentences.zh: 问题不仅会带来答案，还会引发更多问题。

blocks.html_en: The best questions grow in the answering. You notice a thread protruding from the current paradigm and try pulling on it, and it just gets longer and longer. So don't require a question to be obviously big before you try answering it. You can rarely predict that. It's hard enough even to notice the thread, let alone to predict how much will unravel if you pull on it.

sentences.en: The best questions grow in the answering.
sentences.zh: 最好的问题在回答中成长。

sentences.en: You notice a thread protruding from the current paradigm and try pulling on it, and it just gets longer and longer.
sentences.zh: 你注意到一条线从当前的范式中伸出，并尝试拉动它，它只会变得越来越长。

sentences.en: So don't require a question to be obviously big before you try answering it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在尝试回答问题之前，不要要求问题明显很大。

sentences.en: You can rarely predict that.
sentences.zh: 你很少能预测到这一点。

sentences.en: It's hard enough even to notice the thread, let alone to predict how much will unravel if you pull on it.
sentences.zh: 连注意到这根线都已经够困难的了，更不用说预测如果你拉动它会散开多少。

blocks.html_en: It's better to be promiscuously curious — to pull a little bit on a lot of threads, and see what happens. Big things start small. The initial versions of big things were often just experiments, or side projects, or talks, which then grew into something bigger. So start lots of small things.

sentences.en: It's better to be promiscuously curious — to pull a little bit on a lot of threads, and see what happens.
sentences.zh: 最好保持好奇心——在很多线索上稍微拉一点，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Big things start small.
sentences.zh: 大事从小事做起。

sentences.en: The initial versions of big things were often just experiments, or side projects, or talks, which then grew into something bigger.
sentences.zh: 大事情的最初版本通常只是实验、副项目或谈话，然后发展成为更大的事情。

sentences.en: So start lots of small things.
sentences.zh: 所以要从很多小事做起。

blocks.html_en: Being prolific is underrated. The more different things you try, the greater the chance of discovering something new. Understand, though, that trying lots of things will mean trying lots of things that don't work. You can't have a lot of good ideas without also having a lot of bad ones.

sentences.en: Being prolific is underrated.
sentences.zh: 多产被低估了。

sentences.en: The more different things you try, the greater the chance of discovering something new.
sentences.zh: 你尝试的不同事物越多，发现新事物的机会就越大。

sentences.en: Understand, though, that trying lots of things will mean trying lots of things that don't work.
sentences.zh: 但要明白，尝试很多事情就意味着尝试很多行不通的事情。

sentences.en: You can't have a lot of good ideas without also having a lot of bad ones.
sentences.zh: 你不可能在拥有很多好想法的同时也有很多坏想法。

blocks.html_en: Though it sounds more responsible to begin by studying everything that's been done before, you'll learn faster and have more fun by trying stuff. And you'll understand previous work better when you do look at it. So err on the side of starting. Which is easier when starting means starting small; those two ideas fit together like two puzzle pieces.

sentences.en: Though it sounds more responsible to begin by studying everything that's been done before, you'll learn faster and have more fun by trying stuff.
sentences.zh: 虽然从研究以前做过的所有事情开始听起来更负责任，但通过尝试，你会学得更快并获得更多乐趣。

sentences.en: And you'll understand previous work better when you do look at it.
sentences.zh: 当你真正看到以前的作品时，你会更好地理解它。

sentences.en: So err on the side of starting.
sentences.zh: 所以最好还是开始吧。

sentences.en: Which is easier when starting means starting small; those two ideas fit together like two puzzle pieces.
sentences.zh: 当开始意味着从小事做起时，哪一个更容易？这两个想法就像两块拼图一样组合在一起。

blocks.html_en: How do you get from starting small to doing something great? By making successive versions. Great things are almost always made in successive versions. You start with something small and evolve it, and the final version is both cleverer and more ambitious than anything you could have planned.

sentences.en: How do you get from starting small to doing something great?
sentences.zh: 如何从小事做起，成就大事？

sentences.en: By making successive versions.
sentences.zh: 通过制作连续的版本。

sentences.en: Great things are almost always made in successive versions.
sentences.zh: 伟大的事物几乎总是由连续的版本制成的。

sentences.en: You start with something small and evolve it, and the final version is both cleverer and more ambitious than anything you could have planned.
sentences.zh: 你从小事开始，不断发展它，最终的版本比你计划的任何东西都更聪明、更雄心勃勃。

blocks.html_en: It's particularly useful to make successive versions when you're making something for people — to get an initial version in front of them quickly, and then evolve it based on their response.

sentences.en: It's particularly useful to make successive versions when you're making something for people — to get an initial version in front of them quickly, and then evolve it based on their response.
sentences.zh: 当你为人们做一些东西时，制作连续的版本特别有用——快速地在他们面前提供一个初始版本，然后根据他们的反应来改进它。

blocks.html_en: Begin by trying the simplest thing that could possibly work. Surprisingly often, it does. If it doesn't, this will at least get you started.

sentences.en: Begin by trying the simplest thing that could possibly work.
sentences.zh: 首先尝试最简单、可行的方法。

sentences.en: Surprisingly often, it does.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，事实往往如此。

sentences.en: If it doesn't, this will at least get you started.
sentences.zh: 如果没有，这至少会让您开始。

blocks.html_en: Don't try to cram too much new stuff into any one version. There are names for doing this with the first version (taking too long to ship) and the second (the second system effect), but these are both merely instances of a more general principle.

sentences.en: Don't try to cram too much new stuff into any one version.
sentences.zh: 不要试图在任一版本中塞入太多新内容。

sentences.en: There are names for doing this with the first version (taking too long to ship) and the second (the second system effect), but these are both merely instances of a more general principle.
sentences.zh: 对于第一个版本（发布时间太长）和第二个版本（第二个系统效果）有一些名称，但这些都只是更普遍原则的实例。

blocks.html_en: An early version of a new project will sometimes be dismissed as a toy. It's a good sign when people do this. That means it has everything a new idea needs except scale, and that tends to follow.

sentences.en: An early version of a new project will sometimes be dismissed as a toy.
sentences.zh: 新项目的早期版本有时会被视为玩具而被抛弃。

sentences.en: It's a good sign when people do this.
sentences.zh: 当人们这样做时，这是一个好兆头。

sentences.en: That means it has everything a new idea needs except scale, and that tends to follow.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它拥有新想法所需的一切，除了规模之外，而且规模往往会随之而来。

blocks.html_en: The alternative to starting with something small and evolving it is to plan in advance what you're going to do. And planning does usually seem the more responsible choice. It sounds more organized to say "we're going to do x and then y and then z" than "we're going to try x and see what happens." And it is more organized; it just doesn't work as well.

sentences.en: The alternative to starting with something small and evolving it is to plan in advance what you're going to do.
sentences.zh: 除了从小事开始并不断发展之外，另一种选择是提前计划你要做什么。

sentences.en: And planning does usually seem the more responsible choice.
sentences.zh: 规划通常看起来确实是更负责任的选择。

sentences.en: It sounds more organized to say "we're going to do x and then y and then z" than "we're going to try x and see what happens."
sentences.zh: 说“我们要做 x，然后是 y，然后是 z”，这听起来比“我们要尝试 x，看看会发生什么”更有条理。

sentences.en: And it is more organized; it just doesn't work as well.
sentences.zh: 而且更有组织性；它只是不太有效。

blocks.html_en: Planning per se isn't good. It's sometimes necessary, but it's a necessary evil — a response to unforgiving conditions. It's something you have to do because you're working with inflexible media, or because you need to coordinate the efforts of a lot of people. If you keep projects small and use flexible media, you don't have to plan as much, and your designs can evolve instead.

sentences.en: Planning per se isn't good.
sentences.zh: 规划本身并不好。

sentences.en: It's sometimes necessary, but it's a necessary evil — a response to unforgiving conditions.
sentences.zh: 有时这是必要的，但它是一种必要的罪恶——对无情条件的反应。

sentences.en: It's something you have to do because you're working with inflexible media, or because you need to coordinate the efforts of a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这是你必须做的事情，因为你正在与不灵活的媒体合作，或者因为你需要协调很多人的努力。

sentences.en: If you keep projects small and use flexible media, you don't have to plan as much, and your designs can evolve instead.
sentences.zh: 如果您保持项目较小并使用灵活的媒体，则无需进行太多计划，您的设计也可以不断发展。

blocks.html_en: Take as much risk as you can afford. In an efficient market, risk is proportionate to reward, so don't look for certainty, but for a bet with high expected value. If you're not failing occasionally, you're probably being too conservative.

sentences.en: Take as much risk as you can afford.
sentences.zh: 承担尽可能多的风险。

sentences.en: In an efficient market, risk is proportionate to reward, so don't look for certainty, but for a bet with high expected value.
sentences.zh: 在有效市场中，风险与回报成正比，因此不要寻求确定性，而要寻求具有高预期价值的赌注。

sentences.en: If you're not failing occasionally, you're probably being too conservative.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是偶尔失败，那么你可能太保守了。

blocks.html_en: Though conservatism is usually associated with the old, it's the young who tend to make this mistake. Inexperience makes them fear risk, but it's when you're young that you can afford the most.

sentences.en: Though conservatism is usually associated with the old, it's the young who tend to make this mistake.
sentences.zh: 虽然保守主义通常与老年人联系在一起，但年轻人往往会犯这个错误。

sentences.en: Inexperience makes them fear risk, but it's when you're young that you can afford the most.
sentences.zh: 缺乏经验让他们害怕风险，但年轻的时候才是最能承受风险的。

blocks.html_en: Even a project that fails can be valuable. In the process of working on it, you'll have crossed territory few others have seen, and encountered questions few others have asked. And there's probably no better source of questions than the ones you encounter in trying to do something slightly too hard.

sentences.en: Even a project that fails can be valuable.
sentences.zh: 即使一个失败的项目也可能是有价值的。

sentences.en: In the process of working on it, you'll have crossed territory few others have seen, and encountered questions few others have asked.
sentences.zh: 在研究的过程中，你会跨越很少有人见过的领域，并遇到很少有人问过的问题。

sentences.en: And there's probably no better source of questions than the ones you encounter in trying to do something slightly too hard.
sentences.zh: 可能没有比你在尝试做稍微困难的事情时遇到的问题更好的来源了。

blocks.html_en: Use the advantages of youth when you have them, and the advantages of age once you have those. The advantages of youth are energy, time, optimism, and freedom. The advantages of age are knowledge, efficiency, money, and power. With effort you can acquire some of the latter when young and keep some of the former when old.

sentences.en: Use the advantages of youth when you have them, and the advantages of age once you have those.
sentences.zh: 当你拥有年轻的优势时，就利用它；当你拥有这些优势时，就利用年龄的优势。

sentences.en: The advantages of youth are energy, time, optimism, and freedom.
sentences.zh: 年轻的优势是精力、时间、乐观、自由。

sentences.en: The advantages of age are knowledge, efficiency, money, and power.
sentences.zh: 年龄的优势是知识、效率、金钱和权力。

sentences.en: With effort you can acquire some of the latter when young and keep some of the former when old.
sentences.zh: 通过努力，你可以在年轻时获得一些后者，并在年老时保留一些前者。

blocks.html_en: The old also have the advantage of knowing which advantages they have. The young often have them without realizing it. The biggest is probably time. The young have no idea how rich they are in time. The best way to turn this time to advantage is to use it in slightly frivolous ways: to learn about something you don't need to know about, just out of curiosity, or to try building something just because it would be cool, or to become freakishly good at something.

sentences.en: The old also have the advantage of knowing which advantages they have.
sentences.zh: 老年人还有一个好处，就是知道自己有哪些优势。

sentences.en: The young often have them without realizing it.
sentences.zh: 年轻人常常在没有意识到的情况下拥有它们。

sentences.en: The biggest is probably time.
sentences.zh: 最大的可能是时间。

sentences.en: The young have no idea how rich they are in time.
sentences.zh: 年轻人不知道自己的时间有多丰富。

sentences.en: The best way to turn this time to advantage is to use it in slightly frivolous ways: to learn about something you don't need to know about, just out of curiosity, or to try building something just because it would be cool, or to become freakishly good at something.
sentences.zh: 把这段时间变成优势的最好方法是以稍微无聊的方式来利用它：出于好奇而学习一些你不需要知道的东西，或者仅仅因为它很酷而尝试构建一些东西，或者变得非常擅长某件事。

blocks.html_en: That "slightly" is an important qualification. Spend time lavishly when you're young, but don't simply waste it. There's a big difference between doing something you worry might be a waste of time and doing something you know for sure will be. The former is at least a bet, and possibly a better one than you think.

sentences.en: That "slightly" is an important qualification.
sentences.zh: 这个“稍微”是一个重要的限定条件。

sentences.en: Spend time lavishly when you're young, but don't simply waste it.
sentences.zh: 年轻时要大肆挥霍时间，但不要简单地浪费它。

sentences.en: There's a big difference between doing something you worry might be a waste of time and doing something you know for sure will be.
sentences.zh: 做一些你担心可能会浪费时间的事情和做一些你肯定会浪费时间的事情之间有很大的区别。

sentences.en: The former is at least a bet, and possibly a better one than you think.
sentences.zh: 前者至少是一个赌注，而且可能比你想象的更好。

blocks.html_en: The most subtle advantage of youth, or more precisely of inexperience, is that you're seeing everything with fresh eyes. When your brain embraces an idea for the first time, sometimes the two don't fit together perfectly. Usually the problem is with your brain, but occasionally it's with the idea. A piece of it sticks out awkwardly and jabs you when you think about it. People who are used to the idea have learned to ignore it, but you have the opportunity not to.

sentences.en: The most subtle advantage of youth, or more precisely of inexperience, is that you're seeing everything with fresh eyes.
sentences.zh: 年轻的最微妙的优势，或者更准确地说，缺乏经验的最微妙的优势是，你可以用新鲜的眼光看待一切。

sentences.en: When your brain embraces an idea for the first time, sometimes the two don't fit together perfectly.
sentences.zh: 当你的大脑第一次接受一个想法时，有时两者并不完美地结合在一起。

sentences.en: Usually the problem is with your brain, but occasionally it's with the idea.
sentences.zh: 通常问题出在你的大脑上，但有时问题出在想法上。

sentences.en: A piece of it sticks out awkwardly and jabs you when you think about it.
sentences.zh: 当你想到它时，它的一块笨拙地伸出来并刺伤你。

sentences.en: People who are used to the idea have learned to ignore it, but you have the opportunity not to.
sentences.zh: 习惯了这个想法的人已经学会了忽视它，但你有机会不这样做。

blocks.html_en: So when you're learning about something for the first time, pay attention to things that seem wrong or missing. You'll be tempted to ignore them, since there's a 99% chance the problem is with you. And you may have to set aside your misgivings temporarily to keep progressing. But don't forget about them. When you've gotten further into the subject, come back and check if they're still there. If they're still viable in the light of your present knowledge, they probably represent an undiscovered idea.

sentences.en: So when you're learning about something for the first time, pay attention to things that seem wrong or missing.
sentences.zh: 因此，当您第一次学习某些东西时，请注意那些看起来错误或缺失的内容。

sentences.en: You'll be tempted to ignore them, since there's a 99% chance the problem is with you.
sentences.zh: 您可能会想忽略它们，因为 99% 的可能性问题出在您身上。

sentences.en: And you may have to set aside your misgivings temporarily to keep progressing.
sentences.zh: 你可能必须暂时放下疑虑才能继续进步。

sentences.en: But don't forget about them.
sentences.zh: 但不要忘记他们。

sentences.en: When you've gotten further into the subject, come back and check if they're still there.
sentences.zh: 当您进一步了解该主题后，请回来检查它们是否仍然存在。

sentences.en: If they're still viable in the light of your present knowledge, they probably represent an undiscovered idea.
sentences.zh: 如果根据您目前的知识它们仍然可行，那么它们可能代表了一个未被发现的想法。

blocks.html_en: One of the most valuable kinds of knowledge you get from experience is to know what you don't have to worry about. The young know all the things that could matter, but not their relative importance. So they worry equally about everything, when they should worry much more about a few things and hardly at all about the rest.

sentences.en: One of the most valuable kinds of knowledge you get from experience is to know what you don't have to worry about.
sentences.zh: 从经验中获得的最有价值的知识之一就是知道什么是你不必担心的。

sentences.en: The young know all the things that could matter, but not their relative importance.
sentences.zh: 年轻人知道所有可能重要的事情，但不知道它们的相对重要性。

sentences.en: So they worry equally about everything, when they should worry much more about a few things and hardly at all about the rest.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们对所有事情都同样担心，而实际上，他们应该更多地担心几件事，而几乎不担心其他事情。

blocks.html_en: But what you don't know is only half the problem with inexperience. The other half is what you do know that ain't so. You arrive at adulthood with your head full of nonsense — bad habits you've acquired and false things you've been taught — and you won't be able to do great work till you clear away at least the nonsense in the way of whatever type of work you want to do.

sentences.en: But what you don't know is only half the problem with inexperience.
sentences.zh: 但你不知道的只是缺乏经验问题的一半。

sentences.en: The other half is what you do know that ain't so.
sentences.zh: 另一半是你所知道的，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: You arrive at adulthood with your head full of nonsense — bad habits you've acquired and false things you've been taught — and you won't be able to do great work till you clear away at least the nonsense in the way of whatever type of work you want to do.
sentences.zh: 当你成年时，你的脑子里充满了废话——你养成的坏习惯和你被教导的错误的东西——你将无法做出伟大的工作，除非你至少清除了你想做的任何类型工作中的废话。

blocks.html_en: Much of the nonsense left in your head is left there by schools. We're so used to schools that we unconsciously treat going to school as identical with learning, but in fact schools have all sorts of strange qualities that warp our ideas about learning and thinking.

sentences.en: Much of the nonsense left in your head is left there by schools.
sentences.zh: 你脑子里留下的大部分废话都是学校留下的。

sentences.en: We're so used to schools that we unconsciously treat going to school as identical with learning, but in fact schools have all sorts of strange qualities that warp our ideas about learning and thinking.
sentences.zh: 我们已经习惯了学校，以至于不知不觉中把上学和学习等同起来，但事实上，学校有各种奇怪的品质，扭曲了我们对学习和思维的看法。

blocks.html_en: For example, schools induce passivity. Since you were a small child, there was an authority at the front of the class telling all of you what you had to learn and then measuring whether you did. But neither classes nor tests are intrinsic to learning; they're just artifacts of the way schools are usually designed.

sentences.en: For example, schools induce passivity.
sentences.zh: 例如，学校会导致消极性。

sentences.en: Since you were a small child, there was an authority at the front of the class telling all of you what you had to learn and then measuring whether you did.
sentences.zh: 因为你还是个小孩子，所以班级前面有一位权威告诉你们所有人必须学习什么，然后衡量你们是否做到了。

sentences.en: But neither classes nor tests are intrinsic to learning; they're just artifacts of the way schools are usually designed.
sentences.zh: 但课程和考试都不是学习的本质；它们都不是学习的本质。它们只是学校通常设计方式的产物。

blocks.html_en: The sooner you overcome this passivity, the better. If you're still in school, try thinking of your education as your project, and your teachers as working for you rather than vice versa. That may seem a stretch, but it's not merely some weird thought experiment. It's the truth economically, and in the best case it's the truth intellectually as well. The best teachers don't want to be your bosses. They'd prefer it if you pushed ahead, using them as a source of advice, rather than being pulled by them through the material.

sentences.en: The sooner you overcome this passivity, the better.
sentences.zh: 越早克服这种被动性越好。

sentences.en: If you're still in school, try thinking of your education as your project, and your teachers as working for you rather than vice versa.
sentences.zh: 如果您还在上学，请尝试将您的教育视为您的项目，并将您的老师视为为您工作，而不是反之亦然。

sentences.en: That may seem a stretch, but it's not merely some weird thought experiment.
sentences.zh: 这似乎有点夸张，但这不仅仅是一些奇怪的思想实验。

sentences.en: It's the truth economically, and in the best case it's the truth intellectually as well.
sentences.zh: 这在经济上是真理，在最好的情况下，在智力上也是真理。

sentences.en: The best teachers don't want to be your bosses.
sentences.zh: 最好的老师不想成为你的老板。

sentences.en: They'd prefer it if you pushed ahead, using them as a source of advice, rather than being pulled by them through the material.
sentences.zh: 他们更喜欢你继续前进，将他们作为建议的来源，而不是被他们拉着通过材料。

blocks.html_en: Schools also give you a misleading impression of what work is like. In school they tell you what the problems are, and they're almost always soluble using no more than you've been taught so far. In real life you have to figure out what the problems are, and you often don't know if they're soluble at all.

sentences.en: Schools also give you a misleading impression of what work is like.
sentences.zh: 学校也会让你对工作产生误解。

sentences.en: In school they tell you what the problems are, and they're almost always soluble using no more than you've been taught so far.
sentences.zh: 在学校里，他们会告诉你问题是什么，而且这些问题几乎总是可以用你目前所学的内容来解决。

sentences.en: In real life you have to figure out what the problems are, and you often don't know if they're soluble at all.
sentences.zh: 在现实生活中，你必须弄清楚问题是什么，但你常常不知道它们是否可以解决。

blocks.html_en: But perhaps the worst thing schools do to you is train you to win by hacking the test. You can't do great work by doing that. You can't trick God. So stop looking for that kind of shortcut. The way to beat the system is to focus on problems and solutions that others have overlooked, not to skimp on the work itself.

sentences.en: But perhaps the worst thing schools do to you is train you to win by hacking the test.
sentences.zh: 但也许学校对你做的最糟糕的事情就是训练你通过破解考试来获胜。

sentences.en: You can't do great work by doing that.
sentences.zh: 这样做你不可能做出伟大的工作。

sentences.en: You can't trick God.
sentences.zh: 你无法欺骗上帝。

sentences.en: So stop looking for that kind of shortcut.
sentences.zh: 所以不要再寻找那种捷径了。

sentences.en: The way to beat the system is to focus on problems and solutions that others have overlooked, not to skimp on the work itself.
sentences.zh: 击败系统的方法是专注于其他人忽视的问题和解决方案，而不是吝啬于工作本身。

blocks.html_en: Don't think of yourself as dependent on some gatekeeper giving you a "big break." Even if this were true, the best way to get it would be to focus on doing good work rather than chasing influential people.

sentences.en: Don't think of yourself as dependent on some gatekeeper giving you a "big break."
sentences.zh: 不要认为自己依赖某个看门人给你“大突破”。

sentences.en: Even if this were true, the best way to get it would be to focus on doing good work rather than chasing influential people.
sentences.zh: 即使这是真的，实现这一目标的最好方法就是专注于做好工作，而不是追逐有影响力的人。
